summary: 🌟 Summary Ultralytics 8.4.194 makes automatic batch sizing more reliable across tasks, alongside practical fixes for model loading, results saving, datasets, and deployment workflows. 📊 Key Changes 🚀 Automatic batch sizing now uses the training dataset for every task. It accounts for dataset size and labels across classification, detection, and multi-dataset training. If profiling runs out of memory during backward computation, AutoBatch treats that as a limit rather than relying on an invalid measurement. 🛡️ Model YAML parsing is safer and more consistent. Activations must resolve to supported torch.nn modules, and model entries must be PyTorch module classes. Custom YAMLs using other expressions may need updating. 💾 Saving prediction results is more robust. Results.save() and plot(save=True) now produce sensible .jpg filenames for sources such as webcams, videos, or missing paths, and create parent directories when needed. 🔄 Similarity search uses the selected image directory on each startup. This avoids reusing stale indexes from another dataset; the trade-off is that embeddings are rebuilt each time. 🧩 Dataset and URL handling is more dependable. Non-PNG semantic masks are resolved before cache hashing, and URL schemes such as HTTPS:// , GS:// , and UL:// are now handled without case sensitivity. 📈 Benchmarking and evaluation guidance are clearer. TensorFlow GraphDef benchmarks now include OBB and pose, and the docs explain that classes absent from validation receive the overall mAP value rather than a measured per-class score. 🎯 Purpose & Impact ✅ AutoBatch is less likely to choose a batch size that exceeds a small dataset or available GPU memory, and multi-dataset World/YOLOE training avoids label-access failures. 🔒 Consistent, restricted YAML parsing improves safety, though nonstandard custom model configurations may no longer load. 🧰 More reliable result saving, mask-cache updates, and URL routing reduce common workflow errors. 🔍 Similarity search results better reflect the images currently in the chosen folder, while requiring index-building work at startup. 📚 Documentation updates clarify metric interpretation and integration behavior; no new model architecture is introduced in this release. What's Changed Fix classification dataset URL scheme handling by @Vaishnavi220506 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26879 Benchmark TensorFlow GraphDef for OBB and pose by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26952 Give each Colab VM its own anonymous settings id by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26959 Fix settings help URL punctuation by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26962 Update the COCO JSON guide's cache note now that the hash includes mtime by @Echoslayer in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26960 Explain how metrics.box.maps fills classes absent from the val set by @Echoslayer in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26955 Build the similarity search index from the data directory on every start by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26965 Resolve non-PNG semantic mask paths before hashing the label cache by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26954 Handle URL schemes case-insensitively at remaining routing sites by @cainiao33 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26964 Fix Results.save and plot default filename when path is None or extensionless by @Rahulbiradar9 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26958 Fix stale framing, logger defaults and nav order on integration pages by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26957 Use one model YAML parsing path in parse_model by @Y-T-G in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26963 ultralytics 8.4.194 Size AutoBatch from the train dataset for every task by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26956 Full C

summary: Physical reservoir computing leverages the rich dynamical response of non-linear physical bodies to process temporal information without electronic microprocessors. Tensegrity structures, networks of discontinuous compression struts suspended within continuous tension cables, exhibit exceptional compliance, multi-stability, and high-dimensional configuration manifolds, making them prime candidates for mechanical intelligence in extreme, radiation-heavy environments. However, current methodologies rely predominantly on heuristic evolutionary algorithms or brute-force trial-and-error to configure such systems, lacking a rigorous analytical design framework. In this paper, we bridge this gap by establishing an explicit, first-principles mathematical mapping between the internal self-stress null space of a tensegrity network and its Information Processing Capacity (IPC). By decomposing the tangent stiffness matrix into material elastic ($K_e$) and pre-stress geometric ($K_g$) contributions, we demonstrate that the computational memory and fading-memory time constants of a tensegrity reservoir can be systematically engineered by tuning member pre-tensions within an admissible convex cone, holding spatial geometry strictly constant.
title: Formally Verified Pre-Stress Manifolds for Dynamic Stability and Adaptive Physical Intelligence in Tensegrity Reservoir Computing

summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. The original HDF5 simulation files are not redistributed in this record; the repository documents their acquisition, pinned revision, and content-hash verification. The Well: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/ Associated publication: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00568 Dataset documentation: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/datasets/active_matter/ Last-epoch checkpoints named last.pt are excluded; selected best.pt checkpoints are retained. Publication figures, tables, numerical source data, and supplementary videos are supplied with the manuscript submission and are excluded from this archive. Their public availability follows the release of the article and its supplementary materials. The code for generating those outputs remains included. The deposited ZIP contains 1,534 files and occupies approximately 26.18 GB. The accompanying README provides the archive’s SHA-256 checksum, a contents guide, installation references, and verification limits. Packaging integrity and source-checksum checks do not constitute an independent full-data replication. Some archived provenance records retain original execution paths; independent reruns should use a separate work directory and preserve the frozen results. summary: THERMAL MANAGEMENT OF MORPHING ROBOTIC VEHICLE BODIES AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:可變形車體的熱管理極限 22/90 THERMAL MANAGEMENT OF MORPHING ROBOTIC VEHICLE BODIES AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in STARLI's YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy, asking whether a scaled morphing robotic vehicle-body section can redistribute heat without hiding interface hotspots, temperature-induced material degradation or cooling-energy costs. Its three-coupling is Heat Conduction x Distributed Actuation x Thermal Safety. The program is restricted to 24-module unoccupied bench assemblies, coupons, sealed thermal chambers and hardware-in-the-loop control. It makes no claim of a road-ready vehicle, passenger protection or independently demonstrated nanoscale-to-macroscopic performance. The falsifiable candidate compares a frozen morphology-aware heat-management policy against equally resourced fixed passive and centralized wired thermal designs. Under matched mechanical tasks, material mass, source heat, cooling-work budget, sensing access and mission duration, the candidate should reduce the worst qualified local temperature without worsening safety-critical deadline-valid packet survival. The preassigned model rank([C;CA;...;CA^(n-1)])=n tests observability of an ideal local linear state representation; it does not itself prove physical temperature correctness. A hidden heat source, emissivity shift, detached thermal bridge, blocked coolant, over-temperature joint, unaccounted fan input, undercovered uncertainty or ineffective physical stop defeats release. Thirty mathematically distinct research plates address thermal control-volume energy conservation, Fourier and anisotropic conduction, pressure-dependent contact resistance, radiation, convection, dynamic heat storage, resistive heating, actuator dissipation, thermomechanical damage, strain-sensitive thermal conductivity, latent-heat buffering, thermal fatigue, forced cooling, heat-pipe and thermoelectric limits, observability, state-estimator innovation, correlated thermal uncertainty, inverse source ambiguity, physical stop latency, hazard dependence, extreme-tail qualification and Biot/Fourier scale arguments. Every plate specifies construction, dimensions, validity conditions, a separate blind falsification and chapter interfaces. Eighty-two research chapters contain 410 separate single-page investigations into physical heat source truth, changing morphology and thermal contacts, sparse sensor observability, cooling systems, thermally induced damage and second-site qualification. Two hundred Research Gates contain individually anchored hidden-fault, matched-comparator and cross-chapter questions with specific scientific notes and stopping criteria. Thirty-three distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos propose instruments, calorimeters, thermal-refusal cards, contact-heat probes, material aging tests and successor negative-case archives. These are prospective research designs, not completed results or operating vehicle hardware. Reference ancestry includes the author's supplied Flagship 13 identifiers 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 (metadata not independently confirmed). External peer-reviewed component literature includes Robo-Matter (10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6), thermally switchable polymers (10.1038/s41467-024-49354-2), thermally actuated soft robotics (10.1002/adma.202504683), conductive elastomer films (10.1039/D5NR03526K), responsive battery thermal regulation (10.1038/s41560-024-01535-5), phase-change/heat-pipe cooling (10.1016/j.enconman.2024.118506), and the supplied 2026 swarm/microrobot references (10.1038/s44172-026-00715-3; 10.1038/s41427-026-00682-3). Publications support component hypotheses and measurement methods; none independently verifies the integrated F22 concept. summary: Coarse flood maps support regional risk assessment but omit terrain detail relevant to local exposure. We present floodsr, a Python framework for reconstructing fine-grid flood depths using a trained residual U-Net (ResUNet) or the existing terrain-based CostGrow method. We trained the terrain-conditioned ResUNet on paired Canadian hydraulic simulations and evaluated it on withheld spatial tiles and independent simulations at two external sites. Wet-loss training improved reconstruction on five selected tiles, although internal validation favoured the deployed baseline. External depth errors decreased, but wet-depth errors and spatial agreement did not improve consistently. CPU benchmarks quantified runtime and memory for both methods, and repeatability and input-validation checks passed in the tested configurations. The framework supports comparison and reuse of reconstruction methods; application-specific validation remains necessary because finer grids do not guarantee more accurate flood maps.   Non-peer-reviewed preprint. Includes the manuscript and supplementary material. Software: https://github.com/cefect/floodsr . Documentation: https://floodsr.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ .
title: floodsr: A lightweight Python toolkit for terrain-conditioned flood map super-resolution

summary: v2.4.1 (2026-10-31) replaces the age-only standardization of v2.4.0 by indirect standardization over 16 sex-by-age strata (KDCA district-by-sex-by-age-band notifications and resident-registration population by district, sex and age band); all arms, threshold refits and figures were rerun and the credible set is unchanged (fiscal independence only). v2.4.0 (revision R1, 2026-10-31) adds revision_R1/: the additional analyses requested at peer review by JMIR Public Health and Surveillance (indirectly age-standardized expected counts as offset; every count or area covariate re-expressed as a share of district land area, a rate per 1000 residents or a density per km2, with log population density added; two uniform functional forms; parsimonious models; restricted spatial regression; zero-inflated negative binomial; residual Moran's I for every specification; 8 neighbourhood graphs; spatially varying coefficients for forest share and household wells; physicians per 1000 as ascertainment proxy; 2022-2024 only; repeated fits; reruns of the complete data pipeline under alternative screening thresholds and with linear interpolation), all outputs, the revised figures, and the inputs needed beyond the raw files. Under the revised principal model only fiscal independence remains credible (IRR 0.890, 95% CrI 0.819-0.966 per SD); the four other associations of the reviewed version survive age standardization alone but not rescaling, and forest share is credible under no revised specification. Three input corrections (Busanjin-gu and Cheonan-si land-use and well values; boundary-file area in place of the sewerage area field; Incheon Michuhol-gu/Namdong-gu polygon assignment) are documented; the reviewed specification refitted on the corrected inputs reproduces its 5 associations. The main script and results/ (v2.3.3, the reviewed analysis) are unchanged. Earlier history: Reproducibility package for a Bayesian spatiotemporal analysis of district-level hepatitis A incidence in South Korea, 2020-2024 (negative binomial, Besag-York-Mollie convolution + RW1 + Knorr-Held Type I interaction, fitted with R-INLA; 219 districts, 1,095 district-years, 27 covariates). v2.1.0 is a DATA-REPAIR release that supersedes all earlier versions: an audit found that several administrative source files store unavailable values as 0 instead of missing and that some series were redefined in particular years, so that, under binary and quantile coding, covariates encoded data availability rather than their true level. These values are now recoded as missing and filled from the most recent earlier available year, and every change is logged (results/data_repair_log.csv). The v2.0.x associations for piped water-supply coverage and inpatient medical cost, and the v2.0.x claim of nine credible covariates, were artefacts of this defect and are withdrawn. The repaired analysis found four credible covariates (household groundwater wells, dairy-cattle farms, forest area, fiscal independence). A post hoc extreme-value screen then found aggregation errors (eg, a sex ratio near 50 males per 100 females, basic livelihood security recipients above 30%, mostly in cities with non-autonomous wards) affecting 17 district-years in 4 covariates; v2.2.0 adopts this screen as rule R7 of the principal analysis, which excludes 2 further districts (218 districts, 1,090 district-years) and adds sewer-pipe repair sites as a fifth credible covariate. Household groundwater wells and sewer-pipe repair sites are borderline (lost under some neighbourhood graphs, INLA settings or the alternative handling of extreme values), and only forest area is credible in every sensitivity analysis; dairy-cattle farms, sewer-pipe repair sites and fiscal independence are lost when 2020-2021 is excluded. The covariates take up only part of the spatial structure (residual Moran's I +0.22). The package contains a single R script (data repair, models, sensitivity and stability analyses), a figure script, a year-R2 data
title: Spatial Clustering of Hepatitis A in South Korea, 2020-2024: Nationwide Bayesian Analysis of Socioeconomic Gradients and Residual Clustering After Age Standardization (analysis code, data-repair log and compiled data, v2.4.1)

summary: DIGITAL IDENTITY AND STRUCTURAL CONTINUITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS VEHICLES AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:可變形自主車輛的數位身份與結構連續性極限 28/90 DIGITAL IDENTITY AND STRUCTURAL CONTINUITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS VEHICLES AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy, Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 28 of 90. It asks whether the identity of a morphing modular vehicle can remain independently reconstructable after authorized component replacement without confusing a valid digital registration with preserved load-bearing structure. The three-way research coupling is Digital Identity x Structural Evolution x Traceability. The scope is unoccupied scaled panels, instrumented materials and hardware-in-the-loop studies; no working road vehicle, human safety certification or legal identity status is claimed. The falsifiable research contract compares a frozen physical-and-digital provenance architecture against conventional fleet records, competent expert inspection and signed digital-twin workflows under equal material, sensor, energy, computing, time and labor budgets. Its principal target is fewer unsafe identity counterexamples without worse independent handoff and replay completeness. summary: This article examines how customs authorities can shorten clearance times without reducing the detection of violations by redistributing fixed inspection capacity across risk lanes. The empirical basis is a declaration-level dataset from the Customs Committee of Uzbekistan, comprising 8,000 declarations lodged at 12 customs posts during 2023–2026. A log-logistic accelerated failure time model shows that assignment to the red lane multiplies expected clearance time by 2.97, while pre-arrival lodging reduces it by 29.7%. A linear programming model is proposed to rank declarations by the number of detected violations per hour of additional clearance time. With the same 1,820 inspections and 786 detected violations, the model reduces the 90th percentile of clearance time by 21.3 minutes and by 64.2 minutes when combined with an increased share of pre-arrival declarations.
title: TIME-AWARE ALLOCATION OF CUSTOMS INSPECTION RESOURCES ACROSS RISK LANES: DECLARATION-LEVEL EVIDENCE FROM UZBEKISTAN

summary: This article examines how customs authorities can shorten clearance times without reducing the detection of violations by redistributing fixed inspection capacity across risk lanes. The empirical basis is a declaration-level dataset from the Customs Committee of Uzbekistan, comprising 8,000 declarations lodged at 12 customs posts during 2023–2026. A log-logistic accelerated failure time model shows that assignment to the red lane multiplies expected clearance time by 2.97, while pre-arrival lodging reduces it by 29.7%. A linear programming model is proposed to rank declarations by the number of detected violations per hour of additional clearance time. With the same 1,820 inspections and 786 detected violations, the model reduces the 90th percentile of clearance time by 21.3 minutes and by 64.2 minutes when combined with an increased share of pre-arrival declarations.

summary: v2.4.2 (2026-10-31) adds a data-vintage sensitivity analysis (outcome replaced by the current KDCA portal counts; revision_R1/results_portalcases/). v2.4.1 (2026-10-31) replaces the age-only standardization of v2.4.0 by indirect standardization over 16 sex-by-age strata (KDCA district-by-sex-by-age-band notifications and resident-registration population by district, sex and age band); all arms, threshold refits and figures were rerun and the credible set is unchanged (fiscal independence only). v2.4.0 (revision R1, 2026-10-31) adds revision_R1/: the additional analyses requested at peer review by JMIR Public Health and Surveillance (indirectly age-standardized expected counts as offset; every count or area covariate re-expressed as a share of district land area, a rate per 1000 residents or a density per km2, with log population density added; two uniform functional forms; parsimonious models; restricted spatial regression; zero-inflated negative binomial; residual Moran's I for every specification; 8 neighbourhood graphs; spatially varying coefficients for forest share and household wells; physicians per 1000 as ascertainment proxy; 2022-2024 only; repeated fits; reruns of the complete data pipeline under alternative screening thresholds and with linear interpolation), all outputs, the revised figures, and the inputs needed beyond the raw files. Under the revised principal model only fiscal independence remains credible (IRR 0.890, 95% CrI 0.819-0.966 per SD); the four other associations of the reviewed version survive age standardization alone but not rescaling, and forest share is credible under no revised specification. Three input corrections (Busanjin-gu and Cheonan-si land-use and well values; boundary-file area in place of the sewerage area field; Incheon Michuhol-gu/Namdong-gu polygon assignment) are documented; the reviewed specification refitted on the corrected inputs reproduces its 5 associations. The main script and results/ (v2.3.3, the reviewed analysis) are unchanged. Earlier history: Reproducibility package for a Bayesian spatiotemporal analysis of district-level hepatitis A incidence in South Korea, 2020-2024 (negative binomial, Besag-York-Mollie convolution + RW1 + Knorr-Held Type I interaction, fitted with R-INLA; 219 districts, 1,095 district-years, 27 covariates). v2.1.0 is a DATA-REPAIR release that supersedes all earlier versions: an audit found that several administrative source files store unavailable values as 0 instead of missing and that some series were redefined in particular years, so that, under binary and quantile coding, covariates encoded data availability rather than their true level. These values are now recoded as missing and filled from the most recent earlier available year, and every change is logged (results/data_repair_log.csv). The v2.0.x associations for piped water-supply coverage and inpatient medical cost, and the v2.0.x claim of nine credible covariates, were artefacts of this defect and are withdrawn. The repaired analysis found four credible covariates (household groundwater wells, dairy-cattle farms, forest area, fiscal independence). A post hoc extreme-value screen then found aggregation errors (eg, a sex ratio near 50 males per 100 females, basic livelihood security recipients above 30%, mostly in cities with non-autonomous wards) affecting 17 district-years in 4 covariates; v2.2.0 adopts this screen as rule R7 of the principal analysis, which excludes 2 further districts (218 districts, 1,090 district-years) and adds sewer-pipe repair sites as a fifth credible covariate. summary: This record provides additional resources supporting the revised manuscript "Morphology and Flux Transport Effects of Boundary Layer Rolls in the Super Typhoon Yagi: A WRF-LES Study" (manuscript 2026JD047911R). The archive contains: (1) an unmodified official upstream WRF v4.6.1 source snapshot at commit d66e442fccc04111067e29274c9f9eaccc3cef28, together with the Noah-MP and workflow submodule revisions referenced by that commit; (2) the local geographic boundary, land, and coastline files used by the Figure 3 plotting workflow, including nmc_met_graphics bou1_4l files and Natural Earth 1:10m map resources; and (3) the unchanged Figure_S6_Source_Data.xlsx workbook, also designated Data Set S1 in the supporting information. The workbook contains band-integrated energies, displayed spectral curves, shell spectra, sampling information, and methods for paired D04/D05 comparisons at 03:00, 09:15, and 14:15 UTC on 6 September 2024, at nominal heights of 500 and 1500 m above ground. Figure S6 was previously numbered Figure S11. Variable names, units, and original source-file checksums are retained in the workbook. The WRF source is an official upstream version snapshot, not a recovered copy of the original locally modified model source, executable, or build environment.  The map files and workbook are preserved without changes to their contents. The nmc_met_graphics files were verified as byte-identical to the pinned upstream files. The Natural Earth files preserve the local Cartopy cache used for plotting; their original upstream release number was not independently recovered. README files, original licence notices, a provenance manifest, and SHA-256 checksums are included. This additional record complements the processed-data archive at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23528012 and the plotting/analysis-code archive at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23524160. It does not replace either existing record. WRF and its submodules remain attributable to their original developers. The nmc_met_graphics and Natural Earth resources retain their original attribution and reuse terms.

summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.

The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.

summary: This repository provides the MATLAB source code and reproducibility resources associated with the manuscript entitled “Physics-Guided Reduced-Order Screening of Radiative Loss, Preferential Diffusion, and NOₓ Pathway Competition in Ammonia/Hydrogen Diffusion Flames,” submitted to the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy (Manuscript No. HE-D-26-13275). The computational framework employs a two-dimensional axisymmetric, physics-guided reduced-order model to investigate the coupled effects of radiative heat loss, preferential diffusion, ammonia cracking, hydrogen enrichment, pressure, and strain on non-premixed ammonia/hydrogen diffusion flames. The MATLAB implementation supports the reproduction of the manuscript's numerical analyses, including baseline flame characteristics, reaction-zone localization, thermal response, relative NOₓ formation tendencies, scalar dissipation, extinction susceptibility, robustness indicators, mechanism-isolation studies, numerical convergence, closure sensitivity, uncertainty analyses, parametric sweeps, and Pareto-based screening. Repository contents and reproducibility The principal file, Master_NH3H2_ROM_Reproducibility.m , contains the model formulation, numerical procedures, analysis modules, and routines for generating supporting figures, numerical tables, and datasets. Executing the master function creates an organized output directory containing the enabled computational results. Model scope and limitations The framework is intended for comparative mechanism screening and prioritization of operating conditions for subsequent higher-fidelity investigations. It does not solve the full governing conservation equations or detailed chemical kinetics. The relative NOₓ formation-tendency index is not an absolute emission concentration, emission factor, or outlet flux. Similarly, the extinction and robustness indicators represent comparative screening metrics rather than experimentally validated stability limits. The repository supports transparency, reproducibility, and further development of computational screening methods for ammonia/hydrogen combustion. Associated manuscript: International Journal of Hydrogen Energy, HE-D-26-13275. Keywords: Ammonia/hydrogen combustion; reduced-order modeling; MATLAB; radiative heat loss; preferential diffusion; NOₓ formation tendency; extinction; uncertainty analysis; reproducibility.

The repository supports transparency, reproducibility, and further development of computational screening methods for ammonia/hydrogen combustion. summary: Croft asked for the largest regular polygon that can be translated, rotated, and scaled inside another. For coprime side counts at least five, we prove the conjecture of Dilworth and Mane that an optimum occurs at one of two endpoint configurations. The endpoint values never tie, and every interior orientation in the fundamental interval is strictly suboptimal. Together with the published cases, this determines the exact optimum for every ordered pair of regular polygons. In the coprime case, the optimal placement is unique modulo the natural dihedral symmetries of the two polygons and has exactly four contacts between inner vertices and the relative interiors of outer sides. These form two reflected pairs. They lie in a common open half-plane whose boundary passes through the outer center exactly for (m, n) = (2k + 1, 2k), k ≥ 3; otherwise one lies in each open quadrant determined by the common symmetry axis and its perpendicular. The proof uses support constraints, balanced three-constraint certificates, and centered modular residues. Supplementary computations check identities and finite ranges without serving as proof premises. summary: Learned surrogates of process simulators are often evaluated on random states from plants they have already seen. This technical report compares interpolation, leave-one-case-out, and leave-one-ore-group-out evaluation for five models trained on a steady-state mineral-processing simulator. The simulator tracks mineral mass over 63 size classes, water, closed grinding circuits, and unit-level balance closure. It reports limitations against published examples alongside the comparisons. On a 3,072-state design over twelve authored cases, the multilayer perceptron gives the lowest interpolation recovery RMSE (3.38 percentage points), but has a 26.24-point mean RMSE when each case is held out. The Gaussian process has the lowest mean held-out-case RMSE (10.95 points), while the perceptron has the highest median case-fold R-squared (0.547). Under ore-group holdout, the perceptron's median recovery R-squared is 0.437 across seven groups, but varies from 0.795 for the five chalcopyrite cases to -10.2 for the two gold-in-pyrite cases. Log-upgrade transfer is poor for every model. The cases are authored; these results do not establish performance on operating plants. The report documents the mineral-processing simulator, its physical models, machine-learning evaluation methods, a process-specific optimization study, data and preprocessing, validation protocols, limitations, and reproducibility. Source code and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_OreFlow

title: CasADi - A software framework for nonlinear optimization and optimal control

summary: PhenoRewire is a Python command-line tool for detecting network rewiring in metabolomics data. It builds one metabolite co-variation network per biological state, classifies every pair of metabolites as shared, specific to one state or reversed in sign, and tests whether the difference between the two networks exceeds what an arbitrary split of the same samples produces. It identifies metabolites whose correlation neighbourhood reorganised between two states, including those whose abundance did not change and which a differential-abundance analysis cannot report. This release carries the ground-truth benchmarks behind its claims, against DiffCorr and DGCA, with their result tables.
title: PhenoRewire: phenotype-aware metabolomics network rewiring

summary: Raw surface EMG (13 shoulder and elbow muscles) and isometric force/torque recordings (6 channels), sampled at 1 kHz, from three chronic stroke survivors who performed a virtual reaching task in immersive virtual reality with their most affected arm. The virtual cursor was driven either by the measured isometric force (force control) or by the force estimated from EMG (myoelectric control). In myoelectric control, a patient-tailored assistive-adaptive algorithm projected the participant's muscle pattern towards a healthy reference pattern, with an assistance level progressively reduced across blocks. For each participant the dataset contains one session of 9 to 16 blocks (376 trials in total): a maximum voluntary contraction block, force-control baseline blocks and myoelectric-control blocks at different assistance levels. Each trial file contains the raw EMG, forces and torques, the force driving the cursor, the task state, the trial events and the trial metadata (target direction, block, assistance level). A configuration file per participant describes the channels, the sensor calibration and the block settings. The data are pseudonymised. The files are MATLAB v7 MAT-files that can be read in MATLAB and in Python (scipy.io.loadmat). See README.md for the full description of the files and variables. These data support: Nocilli M., d'Avella A., Berger D.J. (2025). A novel approach to promote upper-limb motor recovery in stroke survivors using assistive myoelectric control and adaptive visual feedback in virtual reality. Front. Bioeng. Biotechnol. 13:1628679. https://doi.org/10.3389/fbioe.2025.1628679  Funding: Italian Ministry of Health, European Union - NextGenerationEU - NRRP M6C2 - Investment 2.1, project PNRR-POC-2022-12375705, CUP J83C22002060007.
title: Raw EMG and isometric force data from a pilot study of assistive myoelectric control with adaptive visual feedback in virtual reality in chronic stroke survivors

summary: Military installation energy readiness depends on having sufficient resources to sustain mission-critical loads throughout a prolonged utility outage. This paper develops a method to help operators manage energy resources during normal grid-connected operation while preserving islanded readiness. A robust viability kernel identifies combinations of battery energy, fuel, and load-shifting capability sufficient to sustain critical load under uncertain demand and photovoltaic generation. A probability bound translates stochastic generator start failures and recovery into a deterministic generator count selected to meet a specified availability requirement at islanding. Case studies for a fourteen-day islanding requirement at 0.999 islanding-entry availability show that advance warning of an outage can be used to prepare resources to meet a higher readiness requirement before islanding begins. The case studies further demonstrate that economic-only operation and the evaluated fixed battery reserve policy can fail to sustain critical load for the required duration, whereas enforcing the resource-dependent requirement preserves readiness at a modest increase in modeled grid-connected operating cost. These results demonstrate how active resource management can preserve long-duration energy readiness. The framework also helps commanders understand how readiness changes with operating conditions, even when the available resources remain the same.
title: Readiness-Constrained Pre-Islanding Dispatch for Military Microgrids

summary: Fight, flight, and relaxation describe bodily mobilisation and recovery but leave open how attention is selectively withheld or invested in discovery. This article examines ignoring and exploring as two modes of engagement whose neural and bodily organisation requires separate analysis. Ignoring reduces processing of particular information; exploring gathers information about something incompletely known. Evidence from distractor-suppression research indicates that ignoring is an organised, often learned and sometimes anticipatory form of neural selection. Research on curiosity, exploratory choice, and orienting relates exploration to motivated learning and arousal regulation, and shows that cardiac responses unfold in stages that distinguish information intake from preparation for action. The article separates attentional investment in an input from bodily mobilisation, which permits relaxed exploration, mobilised investigation, ignoring at ease, and ignoring under exertion. It distinguishes three ways of letting something pass (sensory filtering, nonreactivity to a noticed experience, and effortful suppression) that differ in what is recognised and in their bodily costs. Quiet readiness is defined in signal-detection terms as reduced interference from irrelevant inputs, preserved sensitivity to inputs whose relevance changes, a response criterion near its optimum, and bodily cost no greater than the task requires. Three failure profiles follow: rigid filtering (an overly conservative criterion), anxious vigilance (an overly liberal criterion at high cost), and distractible ease (weak suppression). Five hypotheses, each paired with a rival, are assigned to three staged studies. Implications for the M⁵ model of mindfulness are outlined. The framework is an agenda for testing, not a taxonomy of nervous-system states.
title: Ignoring and Exploring: Nervous System Engagement Beyond Fight, Flight, and Relaxation

summary: An effective agent memory system should adapt to a user's history and task requirements. Human-annotated supervision can guide this adaptation by providing feedback for evaluating and improving memory designs. Yet suitable labels are rarely available for new user histories, and manually constructing QA pairs and supporting evidence is costly. We introduce MemSteer, which turns unlabeled user histories into question-answer (QA) supervision with supporting evidence for memory-design optimization. MemSteer constructs an evidence-grounded answer plan that specifies how facts across related records jointly support a reference answer. The plan guides question generation, while source-grounded auditing and blind answer recovery check the resulting annotations. To study the utility of this supervision, we develop MemSteer-Opt, which combines QA-based design evaluation with evidence-guided failure diagnosis to revise memory store, retrieval, and context construction without updating model parameters. Experiments on ATM-Bench and RHELM show that this supervision is competitive with official-QA-guided optimization. Relative to Base-BM25, MemSteer-Opt improves ATM-Bench Question Score by 13.4 points and RHELM accuracy by 4.1 and 6.6 points without and with external data, respectively. The supervision also benefits two existing optimizers on ATM-Bench, while new-user experiments demonstrate continued design optimization using supervision generated from the target histories.
title: MemSteer: Turning User Histories into Supervision for Agent Memory Optimization

summary: Luggage re-identification (ReID) is a critical task in video surveillance for forensics, security or border management (suspicious or abandoned luggage recognition), as well as luggage management (lost luggage recovery). It enables the association of observations of the same luggage across disjoint camera views in complex environments such as airports, train stations and border crossing. While existing approaches primarily focus on appearance-based cropped image matching under relatively clean conditions, real-world scenarios are characterized by frequent occlusions, cluttered background and crowded scenes which significantly degrade performance. Yet, strategies leveraging the complementarity of multiple shots and views from different video streams is overlooked. In this paper, we study strategies for an end-to-end pipeline that operates from multiple video streams to detect and re-identify luggage. We evaluate different variants on a benchmark dataset acquired in real-world environments to address the questions of selecting and merging different views and shots of the same luggage as well as training on different environment datasets for an overall ReID performance improvement in practical applications.
title: Luggage re-identification: A study of strategies towards a real-world application

summary: At high redshift, the cosmic microwave background (CMB) both cools relativistic leptons and provides seed photons for inverse-Compton (IC) X-ray emission. These two effects link the particle content of a bubble directly to the soft X-ray depression used to identify a cavity. We derive a physical criterion connecting lepton cooling, bubble volume, enthalpy evolution, and 0.5--2 keV X-ray visibility, while separating intrinsic filling of the X-ray depression from detector-dependent cavity recovery. For uncooled electron populations described by a power law with spectral index $s=2.5$, minimum Lorentz factor $100\leqγ_{\min}\leq1000$, and maximum Lorentz factor $γ_{\max}=10^5$, the measured atmosphere of the testbed high-redshift cluster SPT-CL J2215$-$3537 requires 0.6--1.2\% of the pressure in radiating leptons to fill the soft-band deficit. Across the full tested ranges of $s$, $γ_{\min}$, and atmospheric properties, the required fraction is 0.2--3.7\%. Complete loss of this component reduces the enthalpy by less than 3\% relative to an otherwise identical adiabatic bubble at the same pressure. A low-cutoff control with $γ_{\min}=10$ and $s=3$ instead requires 18.9\%, identifying the poorly constrained low-energy spectrum as the main physical uncertainty. For a fixed atmosphere and spectrum, the required fraction scales as $(1+z)^{-4}$. The declining-pressure tracks show that the X-ray deficit can cross the adopted detection threshold while the enthalpy deficit remains below 0.4\%; the time of this transition depends on the assumed pressure history. Thus, high-redshift cavity visibility depends on both the surrounding atmosphere and the pressure-carrying particle spectrum. This criterion provides the physical basis for an instrument-specific recovery analysis.
title: The Conditional CMB Visibility of High-Redshift X-Ray Cavities in Galaxy clusters

summary: Comparing observed and predicted surface temperatures on airless planetary bodies is crucial for interpreting their surface processes, constraining activity, and deriving their surface properties. We present a new tool in this endeavour: TEMPEST (Thermophysical Evolution Model for Planetary Environment Surface Temperatures). It is a modular, open-source Python model for diurnal thermal evolution on irregular bodies. TEMPEST can reproduce non-Lambertian multiple scattering using arbitrary Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Functions (BRDFs) and notably incorporates surface roughness on sub-facet scales through representative sphere-section geometry. The model includes an explicit time-stepping one-dimensional periodic conduction solver influenced by Spencer's thermal model Thermprojrs, and a semi-implicit Crank-Nicolson solver, and can be paired with other thermal solvers. Precomputed look-up tables enable fast application of scattering laws (Lambertian, Lommel-Seeliger, Hapke, or input empirical BRDF data), allowing the user to assess their effects in permanently shadowed regions or partially shadowed terrains. TEMPEST is parallelised, running on personal computers in minutes for thousands of facets and scaling to high-performance servers for models exceeding 100,000 facets. Validation was performed against Thermprojrs in one dimension, against Sorli's Binary Thermophysical Model in three dimensions, and with empirical thermal data from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, showing good agreement in each case. Application to the high-resolution shape-model of 25143 Itokawa shows the importance of self-shadowing and radiative mutual heating in controlling local temperatures. TEMPEST has already been used to analyse data from the Lucy Mission, Galileo, and ground-based observations, and is adaptable to upcoming datasets from targets of missions such as Comet Interceptor and Europa Clipper.
title: TEMPEST - A modular Python-based thermophysical model for rough, irregularly-shaped airless bodies

summary: Writing the Related Work section is a challenging task for inexperienced researchers, requiring significant time, effort, and skill. This study aims to ease this burden by introducing an ICT-based framework that automates the generation of cohesive and well-structured Related Work sections. We propose SciRelate, a novel framework that combines abstractive multidocument summarization and automated keyword-based subsection heading extraction. SciRelate comprises three main modules: (1) document clustering using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), (2) related Work generation via a fine-tuned Bidirectional and Autoregressive Transformer (BART) model, and (3) Topic keyword extraction using TopicFusion-MP, a hybrid method that integrates LDA, TextRank, and MPNET embeddings. Experiments were conducted using the NudtRwG dataset, and BART was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. LDA clustering effectively identified subsection headings aligned with ground truth structures. The BART model achieved high ROUGE scores: 81.53 (ROUGE-1), 76.19 (ROUGE-2), and 79.03 (ROUGE-L). TopicFusion-MP outperformed six baseline keyword extraction methods in four scenarios, reaching a top similarity score of 0.6398. This study presents a comprehensive, automated pipeline for generating Related Work sections, integrating clustering, summarization, and keyword extraction in a unified framework. SciRelate highlights the potential of ICT tools to support scientific writing, particularly for new researchers.
title: SciRelate: A Framework for Related Work Generation with TopicFusion-MP for Subsection Heading Extraction

summary: We introduce Continuous-Action World Models (CoAWM), a framework for learning cross-embodiment spatiotemporal dynamics priors that support robot action generation across embodiments and execution frequencies. At its core is a shared latent function space that captures the spatial and temporal structure of robot actions. We learn this space through two stages. First, function pretraining brings trajectories from different embodiments and sampling frequencies into a common representation, learning shared dynamics priors through action reconstruction and consistency across temporal sampling views. By accommodating heterogeneous robot trajectories, this stage broadens the range of data sources available for pretraining and facilitates scaling to larger and more diverse datasets. Second, we connect the pretrained function space to a world-model backbone, enabling observations, language instructions, and the current robot state to condition the prediction of a latent action function. A single decoder takes any query time and returns the corresponding end-effector action. By separating shared dynamics priors from task-conditioned action selection and temporal sampling, our approach provides a unified foundation for transferring robot experience across embodiments and control frequencies.
title: Continuous-Action World Models: Learning Cross-Embodiment Spatiotemporal Dynamics Priors

summary: Gravitational observations can leave material properties undetermined in two different ways: distinct states can have the same total source, and distinct spacetime histories can have the same retained observations. We organize these inverse problems in general relativity through a property-level identifiability criterion, with applications to stars and black hole candidates. Two ideal massless gases illustrate equal-source ambiguity: their temperatures differ by a factor of $(8/29)^{1/4}$ and their entropies differ while their stress-energy tensors agree. A separate causal-fluid example starts with identical sources and geometric data but different constitutive responses; the two models' curvature histories separate at linear order in proper time and their scale factors at cubic order. For black hole candidates, the relevant distinction is between stationary exterior parameters, perturbing fluxes and constituent history. The framework provides a test for whether retained data identify a material property, separating instantaneous source equality, history-wide source equality and observational projection.
title: Curvature Blindness: Material Inference in Stars and Black Hole Candidates

summary: Weight-normalized (WN) training is emerging as a compelling alternative to conventional weight decay (WD), with recent studies reporting substantial pretraining loss gains. We show that these gains are driven primarily by the induced effective learning rate (ELR) trajectory rather than by normalization alone. Matching ELR trajectories largely collapses the training loss dynamics of WN and WD. Schedule design should therefore target ELR rather than the nominal learning rate (LR) alone. Building on this principle, we propose AIR (Affine Inverse-square-Root decay), which combines a theoretically derived $1/\sqrt{t}$ decay with an affine adjustment to satisfy prescribed peak and terminal LRs over a finite training horizon. We further identify late-stage ELR scheduling as a key source of its gains, because a shared late schedule attenuates the effect of earlier LR choices. Experiments on 128 B-token Mixture-of-Experts pretraining demonstrate that AIR outperforms cosine and other candidate schedules in training loss, downstream performance, and hyperparameter robustness, reducing terminal training loss by approximately 0.01 relative to cosine at matched cumulative LR. Applying the same ELR trajectory to WD reproduces the corresponding training dynamics, showing that the benefits extend beyond fixed-norm training and establishing ELR as the principled scheduling object.
title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training

summary: Recommender systems face a tension between broadening exposure to diverse viewpoints and avoiding interactions that reinforce extreme positions. This tension is especially consequential in already polarized populations. Here we investigate whether recommendation strategies can reverse polarization rather than merely slow its development. Building on the Attraction--Repulsion Model of opinion dynamics, we introduce two complementary design principles: Tolerance-aware recommendation, which seeks to learn each individual's tolerance for disagreement and reduces exposure to viewpoints beyond that tolerance, and adaptive diversification, which broadens exposure for agents with more extreme opinions while retaining stronger personalization for moderates. Agent-based experiments show that highly personalized recommendations intensify polarization under polarized initial conditions. Tolerance awareness alone primarily slows polarization, whereas combining it with adaptive diversification can reduce polarization below its initial level and, under suitable conditions, restore consensus. Additional experiments incorporating persistent extreme influencers and a spiral-of-silence mechanism show that the combined strategy can mitigate polarization under social pressure and selective participation. To examine whether these findings extend beyond predefined opinion-update rules, we repeat the experiments on a simulated social platform populated by 100 LLM-driven agents prompted to move toward opinions similar to their own and away from those that differ substantially. Across three runs, the combined strategy is again the only recommendation policy tested that reverses polarization in every run. These findings distinguish polarization prevention from reversal and identify tolerance-aware, adaptive exposure as a promising recommendation design principle for reconnecting divided populations.
title: Reversing Polarization through Tolerance-Aware Recommendation and Adaptive Diversification

summary: We present posterior-landscape, a Python framework to identify and characterize morphological features in two-dimensional probability densities. The framework combines concepts from topological data analysis, statistical density-ridge estimation, and scale-space image analysis. It extracts localized concentrations, valleys, ridges, and changes of slope; for Bayesian reconstructions, it propagates uncertainty in feature recovery, geometry, and correspondence across posteriors. The framework also connects two-dimensional structures to features in one-dimensional marginals, and quantifies their correlation with other inferred parameters. We validate the method on controlled densities, and demonstrate its use on gravitational-wave population reconstructions, where it provides a systematic way to identify and interpret population features and assess which ones carry information relevant for cosmology. The resulting catalogues also offer a common morphological representation for future comparisons between predictions and population reconstructions.
title: posterior-landscape: morphological feature finding in two-dimensional probability densities

summary: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based channel state information (CSI) feedback reduces overhead in frequency division duplexing (FDD) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, yet its reconstructed CSI depends on the integrity of pilot acquisition. This paper identifies and evaluates the attack path of adversarial pilot injection against this feedback. A transmitted disturbance can damage the user-side estimation before encoding; correctly delivered quantized bits can still represent a contaminated channel estimate. We model this path through attacker propagation, linear minimum mean square error estimation, compression, quantization, and decoding under a total transmit-energy constraint. An adversarial perturbation generator (APG) implements the attack using channel statistics without current legitimate CSI or instantaneous attacker-channel observations at deployment. At a Rician attacker-channel factor of 10~dB and a transmit perturbation-to-signal ratio of $-4$~dB, APG produces a normalized mean-square error (NMSE) of 0.84~dB in base-station CSI reconstruction, compared with $-10.31$~dB for Gaussian interference. Estimator-targeted and reconstruction-targeted attacks yield different error orderings, and reconstruction damage also degrades beamforming. As a countermeasure, alternating adversarial training (AAT) adapts the feedback encoder and decoder to contaminated pilots. With condition-matched training and APGs reoptimized for the final receiver, AAT reduces NMSE by 2.40--3.79~dB across six representative channel--power conditions. The results demonstrate the importance of protecting pilot acquisition alongside quantized feedback delivery.
title: Adversarial Pilot Injection Against AI-Based CSI Feedback in FDD Massive MIMO Systems

summary: We have developed an array of up to 20 organic glass scintillator detectors, each consisting of a $3~\mathrm{cm}\times3~\mathrm{cm}\times3~\mathrm{cm}$ scintillator cube coupled to a photomultiplier tube. Sensitive to neutrons from a few hundred keV to several tens of MeV, the array was designed for use with recoil separators in inverse-kinematics measurements of astrophysical $(α,n)$ and $(p,n)$ reactions. It provides a prompt start signal for identifying recoil-neutron coincidences from the recoil time of flight. We characterize eight detectors used in an inverse-kinematics measurement of $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(α,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$, using source and in-beam data. From the widths of $γ$-ray Compton-edge peaks at 311, 341, 477, and 1062 keVee, we find an energy resolution described by $\mathrm{FWHM}(E)/E=\sqrt{A^2/E+B^2/E^2+C^2}$, with $A=0.00(7)$, $B=0.0618(54)$, and $C=0.135(5)$. The time-difference spectrum of nearest-neighbor $γ$-$γ$ coincidences from a $^{22}\mathrm{Na}$ source (250--600 keVee) gives a FWHM coincidence timing resolution of $910(40)$ ps, corresponding to a single-detector resolution of $640(30)$ ps. Mixed neutron-$γ$ fields from the in-beam reaction and a $^{241}\mathrm{AmBe}$ source show pulse-shape discrimination with an $n$-$γ$ figure of merit $>1$ down to about 100 keVee. Below 100 keVee, the total neutron yield can still be extracted using two-Gaussian fits to energy-gated pulse-shape discrimination spectra. Monte Carlo simulations of the present $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(α,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$ measurement give a neutron singles detection efficiency of $1.56(45)%$, with uncertainty dominated by systematic effects in the simulation inputs.
title: {DEMAND}: {A}n organic glass scintillator array for direct measurements of $(α,n)$ and $(p,n)$ reactions in inverse kinematics

summary: We consider three-dimensional imaging of compactly supported anisotropic electric media from fixed-frequency polarimetric Maxwell far-field data. Maxwell transversality creates an obstruction absent from scalar Born inversion: each measurement determines only a projected action of the tensor-valued Fourier transform. We first resolve this obstruction by a finite-dimensional polarimetric inversion. For a general complex $3\times3$ contrast, three incidence--observation configurations are necessary, and we give an explicit three-configuration design that is sufficient at every nonzero interior Fourier point. Its Gram determinant yields quantitative conditioning information and exhibits the loss of recoverability at the boundary of the accessible Fourier ball. After tensor demixing, the inverse problem reduces componentwise to restricted Fourier inversion on the unit ball, which we regularize by spectral cutoff in three-dimensional ball generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions. For discrete acquisition, a combined reconstruction error estimate separates the effects of measurement noise, polarimetric amplification, off-grid Fourier mismatch, quadrature error, Born modeling error, and spectral truncation. Numerical tests examine polarimetric conditioning and use analytically generated Born data to compare three- and six-configuration recovery and assess off-grid sensitivity. Reconstructions from full-Maxwell volume-integral data assess the effects of noise, wavenumber, and basis choice, as well as the recovery of different tensor components.
title: Polarimetric Low-Rank Imaging of Anisotropic Maxwell Media

summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers information-theoretic security, but device imperfections introduce implementation vulnerabilities. Experimental evidence of the security consequences of transmitter vulnerabilities in continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD) remains limited. Here, we experimentally investigate a reversible photorefractive attack in a local-local-oscillator CV-QKD system. Moderate blue-light illumination reduces the modulation variance of a lithium-niobate IQ modulator to a stable value without appreciably increasing estimated excess noise. The variance recovers after illumination is removed. We elucidate the underlying physical mechanisms and develop an attack that exploits recovery to compromise modulation calibration. Receiver measurements confirm that the resulting calibration mismatch leads to overestimated channel transmittance and underestimated excess noise. Key rate calculations based on measured parameters yield a positive estimated rate when the correctly calibrated rate is nonpositive. Recovery can also make the preceding manipulation harder to identify through later inspection. This work provides the first system-level experimental evidence that a reversible photorefractive response can be exploited to compromise modulation calibration in CV-QKD. These findings highlight reversible changes in quantum transmitters as a practical security concern, motivating security analyses and protection strategies that account for both optical perturbations and subsequent recovery.
title: Reversible photorefractive attack in continuous-variable quantum key distribution

summary: Low-bit quantization enables efficient deployment of large language models by reducing memory footprint and computational cost. Achieving high accuracy at low precision requires selecting quantization ranges, linear transformations, and weight rounding decisions. Existing approaches typically optimize these components independently using local reconstruction objectives, which fail to account for the varying impact of quantization errors on downstream predictions. Direct optimization of task-level metrics would provide a more faithful objective, but is challenging due to the discontinuous nature of quantization operations and the high computational cost of evaluating their downstream effects. In this work, we derive a Hessian-guided approximation of the output change induced by joint weight and activation quantization. Based on a tractable Fisher approximation, we formulate a unified post-training quantization framework that enables the joint optimization of quantization ranges, linear transformations, and weight rounding under a common output-sensitivity objective. The resulting method remains practical for modern large language models and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art transformation and rounding methods across both channel-wise and block-wise quantization settings.
title: A Unified Hessian-Guided Framework for Post-Training Quantization

summary: As Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in persistent social environments, understanding their long-term social interaction capabilities becomes increasingly important. While existing research has advanced long-term memory and conversational context retrieval, less attention has been paid to whether agents can autonomously re-engage with previously inactive conversations. In particular, remembering a past interaction does not necessarily mean that an agent can identify when to revisit it, decide to return, or reconstruct the context needed for a coherent continuation. To investigate this gap, we introduce agent social re-entry as a multi- dimensional evaluation problem, distinguishing three complementary capabilities: Finding, Returning, and Reconstructing. We develop a shared-snapshot evaluation framework that measures these dimensions independently, allowing us to examine how conversational resurfacing and persistent memory relate to different aspects of social re-entry. Evaluations across six LLM configurations show that resurfacing substantially improves target conversation identification, while persistent memory is associated with higher rates of autonomous target-directed replying. However, neither improvement is accompanied by consistent gains in contextual reconstruction. These results highlight the distinction between accessing previous conversations, choosing to re-engage, and maintaining conversational continuity. Our framework provides a way to evaluate these capabilities separately rather than relying on memory retrieval or conversational response quality alone.
title: Finding Is Not Returning, Returning Is Not Reconstructing: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Agent Social Re-entry

summary: A memory can be outdated for present-day reasoning yet indispensable for reconstructing the past. Relevance-based retrieval overlooks this tension: semantic relevance, evidence-grounded validity, and query-specific eligibility are distinct. We propose CALM, a conflict-aware lifecycle memory governance framework that decouples persistent memory preservation from query-time admission. CALM converts heterogeneous records into evidence-grounded memory cells, updates validity and lifecycle states using support, conflict, and dependency signals, and admits query-appropriate evidence through training-free or learned gating informed by temporal applicability. Across LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo with Qwen and GPT backbones, CALM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving the best overall accuracy. Compared with simple filtering and reranking, query-conditioned admission further improves evidence selection. Conflict-blocking and robustness analyses show CALM suppresses erroneous retrieved memories while retaining useful evidence. Historical-reconstruction experiments demonstrate that preserving superseded records supports accurate earlier-state reasoning without compromising current-state answers.
title: CALM: Conflict-Aware Lifecycle Memory Governance for Long-Horizon Language Agents

summary: Stationary learning admits an ideal-gas description under restrictive noise assumptions. In neural networks whose gradient noise departs from these assumptions, however, an entropy-scaling relation resembling a Maxwell relation remains approximately valid. We ask which thermodynamic-looking relations follow from scale symmetry rather than equilibrium, and how departures from the ideal-gas description can be quantified, for discrete stochastic gradient dynamics with memory. An exact rescaling of trajectories explains the entropy relation without assuming thermal equilibrium. Within a local harmonic approximation, self-adjusting weight norms yield a spectral equation of state whose virial coefficients are set by moments of the curvature spectrum, and coupled parameter groups can sustain stationary probability currents. Our central result beyond this approximation is an exact curvature-transport identity. Together with a finite-step loss balance, it decomposes corrections to the harmonic fluctuation relation into measurable curvature changes, finite-step remainders, gradient-memory correlations and finite-window drift terms. A related displacement-weighted curvature change provides a diagnostic of the arrow of time; its mean and second moment give a lower bound on the relative entropy between forward and reversed state pairs. We also calculate the activation-boundary contribution to curvature for rectified teacher-student networks with Gaussian inputs. Tests in sphere models, teacher-student networks and convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 support the transport description and identify limits of the harmonic and cubic-remainder approximations. These results separate symmetry-based relations from equilibrium assumptions and provide quantitative diagnostics of nonideal fluctuations in learning dynamics.
title: Finite-step statistical mechanics of scale-invariant learning: spectral equations of state and curvature transport

summary: Full-order surrogates for high-dimensional nonlinear flows are often unnecessary when applications require only selected degrees of freedom. We propose reduced-order models that bypass full-state reconstruction by deploying graph neural networks (GNNs) directly on coarse meshes. Applied to parameterized 2D/3D confined cylinder flows and an unevenly heated cavity over Reynolds/Rayleigh-number ranges, the models generalize to unseen conditions and accurately predict sparse probe locations and integrated quantities. Coarse-mesh GNNs match or outperform finer-mesh surrogates while reducing training time and memory, even for 3D chaotic dynamics. A dynamics-informed adaptive sampling strategy guided by frequency-spectrum variations reduces maximum errors by an order of magnitude versus uniform sampling at negligible cost. Coarse-mesh training also makes noise-augmented multi-step unrolling practical, improving long-horizon autoregressive predictions. The approach outperforms parametric DMD, sparse MLPs, U-Nets, and Fourier neural operators at lower cost, and enables system identification and state estimation from sparse observations. These results show that coarse-mesh representations, adaptive sampling, and noise-augmented unrolled training form an efficient framework for reduced-order modeling of parameterized unsteady flows without solver-resolution reconstruction.
title: Predicting Sparse Observables in Parameterized Unsteady Flows Using Coarse-Mesh Graph Neural Networks

summary: Metis is a bet that better data, better training methods and new architectures can buy what a bigger parameter count cannot, at a fraction of the cost. Metis-1.6 is its latest step: two language models built from scratch by a single researcher, Praxis (2.94B parameters, 0.46B active per pass) and Logos (10.23B parameters, 1.18B active per pass). Both run a hybrid Mamba-2 and attention mixture-of-experts stack twice for every token, so each token gets a second look. Each was trained on 1.02T tokens in total: 804.76B of pretraining, 18B of context extension to 131,072 tokens, and 200B of supervised fine-tuning. Metis-1.6 was never meant to challenge frontier models, and across 40 post-trained benchmarks it mostly does not: Logos averages 52.93, seventh of 17 models in its comparison set and within a point of Qwen3-4B. But it gets there on roughly a twelfth of the median training data of the comparators that disclose it, and with fewer active parameters per token than any model that beats it, which puts it on the Pareto frontier for both. In mathematics it ranks second of 30 models, with 67.50% on AIME 2025 and 63.64% on HMMT February 2026. It is weak at code, instruction following and long context. The rest of the report is the part I found most valuable: what went wrong. The optimizer I configured never ran, and attention trained with AdamW for all of pretraining. A 1.77B-parameter n-gram memory learned to switch itself off. Five fine-tuning choices cost capability. And a length reward under group-mean normalization punished correct solutions for being long once a group's pass rate passed 2/3, a sign inversion I prove and fix with a one-line clamp. I close with the 10B-token ablations behind MoRE (Mixture of Recursive Experts), the looped architecture of Metis-1.7.
title: Think Twice: The Metis-1.6 Technical Report

summary: Multi-agent search and coverage is critical to autonomous exploration, search-and-rescue, and defense applications. This paper investigates settings where a mobile sensor network is tasked with coordinating to discover the position of a stationary target within a bounded region. We develop a Bayesian update scheme where agents iteratively combine local uncertainties derived from their sensor measurements through inverse variance weighting to get a better global understanding of where the target may be located given some prior belief. Network agents' trajectories are governed by a primal-dual gradient update rule that simultaneously minimizes the expected sensing uncertainty and enforces network connectivity among the agents. We prove that the belief converges to the target under mild, planner-agnostic conditions, with an explicit exponential rate of false-hypothesis rejection and a bound on expected search time. Simulation results show that we can successfully find the target and collapse belief to the ground truth target location while ensuring connectivity of our sensor network. They also empirically confirm our theoretical bounds and revisiting assumption. Finally, we compare against a lawnmower sweep, showing that our method locates the target more quickly when the prior is informative.
title: Belief-Driven Search in Connectivity-Constrained Mobile Sensor Networks with Convergence Guarantees

summary: PHOTOSTABILITY OF BOTANICAL ACTIVES AND PACKAGING ENGINEERING AT THE LIMIT 中文書名:植物活性成分光穩定性與包材工程極限 Photostability of Botanical Actives and Packaging Engineering at the Limit is a 777-page English research working monograph investigating three coupled but independently falsifiable questions: photochemical degradation of identifiable botanical marker compounds, wavelength-resolved optical transmission through real packaging, and the qualification of storage safety against oxygen ingress and unknown photoproducts. Its central claim is conditional, not asserted. A package that retains more apparent active compound after simulated light exposure may simply exclude oxygen, reduce lamp heating, alter extraction recovery, or hide degradation products. The proposed test therefore crosses films with matched oxygen-transmission rates but contrasting spectral transmittance, and films with matched optical protection but contrasting oxygen transport. Incident spectra, absorbed dose, headspace oxygen, intact parent, isomers and degradants must remain distinct physical measurements. The opening candidate relation D_light = integral over time and wavelength of E_lambda times A_lambda formalizes spectral exposure only within explicitly measured optical and unit conventions. Thirty mathematically diverse research plates specify physical construction, dimensions, assumptions, blind falsification and linked chapters. Eighty-two research chapters and 410 separate-page investigations explore botanical provenance, optical metrology, photochemistry, oxygen transport, package manufacture, chemical recovery, second-site requalification and governance of false-positive claims. Two hundred single-page Research Gates challenge identifiable observables and strong alternative explanations; thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos describe distinguishable scientific instruments, assay references, failure sentinels, and research inheritance objects. Each Gate preserves an adverse test and a successor handoff rather than presuming the hypothesis will win. Three author-designated STARLI mother works provide methodological ancestry in identity protection, functional requalification and uncertainty-aware sampling, not experimental evidence of this skincare application. External method references span IUPAC actinometry, ASTM optical transmission and oxygen permeation, curcumin and anthocyanin photochemistry, and barrier-film research. Their scientific domains and limits are explicitly differentiated. This manuscript is a prospective, nonclinical Research Working Edition, not a completed photostability campaign, human trial, proof of cosmetic efficacy, or regulatory approval. Author: Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli Series: STARLI Research Institute XXXV / Herbal Nano-Quantum Skincare Atlas / Flagship F22
