summary: TriadSense contains synchronised sensor recordings of nine groups of three people who assembled a puzzle together, with annotations of what every participant, every pair and the whole group did. Each participant wore an ear-worn device (OpenEarable 2.0) and a wrist-worn device (Xsens DOT); an optical motion-capture system (OptiTrack) recorded their positions. The record holds the raw recordings of the nine sessions, the annotations of three annotators (the final annotations, the original annotator's annotations before the review, and the reliability sample of 76 clips), the synchronised streams with the final labels on every sample, and the 5-second window table of the benchmark. Video and audio are not released. README.md describes every file and column. Access to the files requires accepting the terms of use (TERMS_OF_USE.md), which prohibit any attempt to re-identify the participants. The code that reproduces the processing and the benchmark: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/triadsense-pipeline-78DB/
title: TriadSense: body-worn and optical sensing of group activity in triads

summary: This record contains the supporting materials of the article “A trade-based Forest Club as a path to halting tropical deforestation”. It has two parts: a multi-regional input–output (MRIO) assessment of the deforestation embodied in agricultural trade and consumption, and the computable general equilibrium (CGE) model of the Forest Club . Every figure and table of the article, its Extended Data and its Supplementary Information is produced from the code, input data and results provided here. The Forest Club is a trade-based coalition. Its members hold their forest at its 2019 extent and are deemed compliant with the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). They charge the forest-risk commodities they import from non-members, either with a flat penalty or with a surcharge proportional to the deforestation embodied in each product. 1. MRIO impact assessment (folders 1. Data and 2. MRIO) The forest-to-cropland and forest-to-pasture transitions of HILDA+ v2.1 (2012–2019) are extracted from the netCDF files and assigned to countries. They are then allocated to the agricultural sectors of the GLORIA MRIO using FAOSTAT harvested areas and livestock numbers, smoothed with three-year moving averages; the FAO–GLORIA mapping and the hectares per head are in A-1_FAO_Cropland_mapping_GLORIA.xlsx and A-2_Head_per_ha.xlsx. Consumption-based accounting (CBA) attributes this agricultural deforestation to final consumers. Throughflow-based accounting (TBA, by hypothetical extraction) traces the share that transits through intermediary economies such as the EU, in detail for Brazil, Indonesia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The folders hold the Python script (CBA_TBA_script.py), the Alteryx workflows, the satellite accounts, the results and the visualisation files (Tableau, Sankey diagrams). These produce sections 2–4 of the Supplementary Information (Tables S1–S2, Figs S1–S4), which describe the deforestation the EUDR covers. 2. CGE model (synced from GitHub) The study simulates how the club forms, round by round, as each country compares its welfare inside and outside it. The model is GTAP-AEZ, a global CGE model with agro-ecological zones (42 regions, 35 sectors, 18 zones; GEMPACK). Every result is measured against a baseline that combines the EUDR with the business-as-usual clearing that DeDuCE v2.1 attributes to agriculture. The coalitions reached are tested for one-country deviations and for their sensitivity to the switching cost. 0_External_data: footprint intensities and border charges derived from DeDuCE v2.1, the EUDR import cut shares, the business-as-usual clearing by region and agro-ecological zone (HILDA+ v2.1 patterns; MapBiomas RAD 2025 for Brazil), and the productivity calibration of the cleared land. 1_Code: R scripts that calibrate and solve the two-stage baseline, run the membership game and the one-deviation stability tests, and calibrate the land-supply elasticities to Miranda et al. (2024). 2_Model: the GTAP-AEZ model files (TABLO code, command files, sets and aggregation). 3_Output and 4_DB: the text outputs of every solve and the result tables of every run, by region and round, for all membership processes and stability tests of the paper. 5_Figures: the Python pipeline that redraws all figures and tables from these results, with their source data. Data not included The GTAP Data Base (version 12, reference year 2019) is licensed by the Center for Global Trade Analysis, Purdue University. Solving the model requires a licensed copy in 2_Model/in/. Redrawing the figures and tables does not, because the extracted results are provided in 5_Figures/data. The GLORIA tables are distributed by the Global MRIO Lab. The README of the repository describes each step of the CGE pipeline. Code synced from the GitHub repository: https://github.com/etiennebert/forest_club/tree/main
title: A Trade-Based Forest Club as a Path to Halting Tropical Deforestation

Per distruggere i commerci con Etruschi e Cartaginesi, venne fatta la Battaglia di Alalia https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battaglia_del_Mare_Sardo Per distruggere i rapporti con la Facies Sarda dei Bessi di Perperikon, venne fatta la battaglia del Monte Emo:   La battaglia del Monte Emo (o Haemus ) è storicamente legata a due momenti distinti dell'antichità che videro scontrarsi gli eserciti invasori con le tribù tracie, in particolare i Bessi , e il cui contesto geografico e spirituale è strettamente connesso al celebre sito monumentale di Perperikon , situato nelle montagne dei Rodopi in Bulgaria. [ 1 , 2 ] Ecco come si collegano questi tre elementi:   1. La prima battaglia del Monte Emo (335 a.C.) Prima di lanciare la sua campagna contro i Persiani, Alessandro Magno guidò una spedizione nei Balcani per rendere sicuri i confini settentrionali del suo regno. Sul Monte Emo (l'attuale catena dei Monti Balcani) affrontò i Traci Liberi e altre tribù locali. La tattica funzionò alla perfezione: i carri rimbalzarono sugli scudi senza causare vittime tra i Macedoni. Le truppe di Alessandro caricarono poi la vetta, sbaragliando i difensori. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]   2. Lo scontro dei Bessi con Roma (72 a.C.) In epoca successiva, il nome della battaglia del Monte Emo si associa alla sottomissione definitiva dei Bessi , una delle tribù tracie più bellicose e fanaticamente dedite al culto religioso. Il proconsole romano Marco Licinio Lucullo affrontò i Bessi proprio nei pressi della catena del Monte Emo, sconfiggendoli duramente in una grande battaglia campale, conquistando il loro centro principale ( Uscudama ) e aprendo la strada alla successiva egemonia romana nella regione. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]   3. Il legame con Perperikon La tribù dei Bessi era storicamente la custode del famosissimo Santuario e Oracolo di Dioniso , situato proprio sulla maestosa roccia sacra di Perperikon . Questo luogo ha un valore storico eccezionale per due importanti profezie collegate ai protagonisti di queste guerre: [ 1 , 2 ] La profezia di Alessandro Magno: Secondo le fonti antiche, prima di iniziare la sua spedizione in Asia (subito dopo aver pacificato la Tracia), Alessandro visitò l'oracolo di Dioniso a Perperikon. Il vino versato sull'altare creò una fiammata altissima fino al cielo, un segno divino che i sacerdoti interpretarono come il presagio che avrebbe conquistato il mondo intero. summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.
tags: Ropelength filtration, compact Lie group, weak slope, metric criticality, isotropy, Lipschitz local section, symmetry-constrained minimax, Noether theorem
title: Lie group actions and metric criticality in ropelength-filtered knot spaces

summary: Cross-border art transactions carry two kinds of legal uncertainty that reform proposals typically treat as one: incomplete verification of who owned, sold, or previously possessed a work, and divergent national rules about what follows once ownership and possession are established beyond dispute. Drawing on a nineteen-year restitution dispute in which the underlying facts were settled well before the litigation ended, this article shows that only the first kind of uncertainty yields to better documentation, tracing, or verification infrastructure; the second persists because national legal systems assign the risk of a stolen object's resale differently, a distributive choice that additional evidence does not change. Recent computational and blockchain-based compliance proposals close real gaps in beneficial-ownership tracing and anti-money-laundering enforcement. Applied to restitution litigation, the same proposals leave the underlying divergence untouched. Reclassifying the deficits identified in existing legal-architecture scholarship along this line separates the problems computational investment can solve from the one that needs a binding choice-of-law rule instead.
tags: art market regulation; provenance; choice of law; anti-money laundering; cultural property restitution; regulatory architecture.
title: A. TILLARD AND THE LEGAL QUESTIONS BEHIND THE GLOBAL ART MARKET

summary: Online sensor telemetry feeds the digital-twin, forecasting, control, and maintenance tools of instrumented water infrastructure. Probes deployed in these assets silently accumulate drift, flatlines, volatility bursts, and outages that existing pipelines often miss, because detectors and imputers are evaluated separately and under inflated synthetic metrics, and decay is treated as isolated events. This work proposes HARDIO, a Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator, an operational data-quality framework that pairs a duration-weighted sensor decay scorecard with a per-variable, chained detector-imputer benchmark. The assignment is selected by a four-pillar composite score (operational 35%, health coverage 30%, reconstruction 20%, calibration 15%) that scores the signal an operator actually receives after detection and imputation. HARDIO processes sensor installations independently, enabling parallel execution and avoiding the need to evaluate all plant channels jointly. HARDIO is validated on the Cheles wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), a real 1,177 population-equivalent (PE) plant, over 432 days, 19 channels, and eight sensor installations. No single detector-imputer pair is best for every channel, so detection and chained imputation distribute across SAITS, KNN Residual, and LSTM-AE. Chained quality is reported for all 19 channels using 1-NRMSE; relative R² is interpreted on the 16 channels where the signal variance makes it meaningful, and 12 of these exceed R²=0.90. On the held-out final 20% of the record (12 channels in five installations), HARDIO achieves a mean chained 1-NRMSE of 0.976, within 0.0035 of a per-channel oracle, and outperforms the uniform SAITS pipeline (p=0.003). Its reconstruction performance is close to that of the strongest uniform pipelines, without a statistically significant improvement over them, and slightly below that of a single detector-imputer pair selected on validation data (0.978). The released artefact exposes the model map, confidence labels, margins, and production masks for decision support.
title: Experimental Artefacts for HARDIO: A Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator for Operational Data Quality in Instrumented Water Infrastructure

summary: Introduction: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent inflammation and progressive joint damage. Interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) contribute to its pathogenesis, while musculoskeletal ultrasound provides valuable information about joint inflammatory activity. The aim of the study was to evaluate changes in IL-1β and IL-6 protein and gene expression and their correlations with clinical and ultrasonographic disease activity in RA patients before and after Tofacitinib treatment. Methods: Fourteen patients with RA were evaluated at baseline and after Tofacitinib treatment. Disease activity was assessed using the 28-joint Disease Activity Score (DAS28) and the seven joint Global Ultrasound Score (GUS7). Plasma cytokine concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA), and gene expression in peripheral blood cells was assessed by qPCR. Results: After six months, median DAS28 decreased from 5.80 to 3.31 (p<0.001), while GUS7 decreased from 20.0 to 11.0 (p=0.002). Plasma IL-6 concentrations decreased significantly from 7.83 to 0.06 pg/mL (p=0.020). No significant changes were observed in plasma IL-1β concentrations (p=0.445) or IL1-β and IL-6 gene expression (p=0.922 and p=1.0, respectively). DAS28 and GUS7 were positively correlated at baseline (ρ=0.890, p<0.001) and after treatment (r=0.689, p=0.006). Conclusion: Tofacitinib treatment was associated with improved clinical and ultrasonographic disease activity and reduced plasma IL-6 concentrations. The absence of significant changes in IL-1β concentrations and cytokine gene expression highlights the complexity of inflammatory regulation in RA. Combined clinical, imaging, and molecular assessments may provide complementary information on treatment response.
title: Beyond clinical improvement: a pilot study on cytokine and ultrasonographic changes following Tofacitinib treatment in Rheumatoid arthritis

summary: Background: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a popular age-linked ailment featured by prostatic enlargement and urinary obstruction. Dinoprostone (DINO) is prostaglandin E 2 having anti-proliferative and anti-inflammatory actions. Objective: This research attempted to assess the effect of DINO vs. finasteride (FINA) on testosterone (TEST)-induced BPH in rats. Methods: 40 adult male rats were haphazardly separated into 4 groups (n = 10); namely control, TEST, TEST + FINA, and TEST + DINO. BPH was induced with subcutaneous TEST (3 mg per kg per day) for 4 weeks. FINA (5 mg per kg) and DINO (7 mg per kg) were delivered orally. Results: TEST administration led to marked prostatic enlargement and hyperplasia, paralleled by remarkable elevations in PCNA, DHT, 5α-reductase, β-catenin, ERβ, pro-inflammatory IL-6, and pro-fibrotic TGF-β and VEGF mediators. FINA and DINO effectively attenuated these alterations, restoring prostate weight and histoarchitecture, downregulating β-catenin and ERβ, ameliorating PCNA expression, and suppressing DHT and 5α-reductase activity. Both drugs modified inflammatory and angiogenic mechanisms and corrected PPAR-γ expression and regulated BCL-2 levels, indicating diminished apoptosis. While FINA surpassed DINO in inhibiting DHT, IL-6, and β-catenin expression, both treatments were equally effective in terms of anti-hypertrophic, anti-inflammatory, and anti-angiogenic actions. Conclusions: DINO demonstrated promising anti-BPH effects comparable to FINA, acting via EP receptor-mediated modulation of prostatic growth and inflammation. These findings are viewed as preliminary and warrant further investigations of DINO for BPH treatment.
title: Preventive effect of Dinoprostone (Prostaglandin E2) on testosterone-induced prostatic hyperplasia in a rat model

summary: The genus Hypocala Guenée, 1852 (Lepidoptera: Erebidae, Hypocalinae) was previously treated in the Fauna Sinica volume on Noctuidae, which recognised four species, based on external morphology from China: H. subsatura Guenée, 1852, H. deflorata (Fabricius, 1794) H. rostrata (Fabricius, 1794) and H. violacea Butler, 1879. A fifth species, H. andamana Wileman, 1923 is known from Taiwan, based on literature records, but was not available for examination in this study. In the present study, based on examination of available museum material, we provide updated diagnoses, descriptions and illustrations of adults and male genitalia for all four species, as well as female genitalia for two species where material was available. A taxonomic key to the Chinese species, updated synonymies and host plant records are also provided. This study establishes a comprehensive baseline for future taxonomic and pest-management research on Hypocala in China.
title: Review of the genus Hypocala Guenée (Lepidoptera, Erebidae, Hypocalinae) from Chinese fauna

summary: 量子輔助車房能源管理極限 38/90 Quantum-Assisted Energy Management For Autonomous Mobile Habitats At The Limit QUANTUM-ASSISTED ENERGY MANAGEMENT FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 38 of 90). It investigates whether a frozen quantum-assisted scheduling approach can coordinate photovoltaic generation, battery storage, power converters and representative habitat service loads while preserving independently measurable energy balances and a physically enforceable safe-stop authority. The three-way research coupling is Quantum Optimization x Distributed Energy x Habitat Service Loads. All proposed tests concern isolated, unoccupied low-voltage scaled apparatus, environmental chambers, hardware-in-the-loop sources and controlled load emulators. No habitable mobile building, live human occupancy, fire or grid interconnection certification is claimed. The principal falsifiable candidate is that, with identical solar forecasts, load traces, storage capacity, computational budgets, instrument calibration and safety rules, the frozen approach improves simulation-to-bench power prediction error without increasing the number of redesigns or losing any critical protected service. The strongest baselines are competent mixed-integer energy scheduling, model-predictive control and a well-tested rule-based fallback, not unrelated structural topology optimization. Six sealed solar-load-climate briefs test cloud ramps, winter demand, overheating, outages, aged storage and telemetry failures. Hidden auxiliary supply, forecast leakage, unsafe battery reserve, infeasible QUBO decoding and unmetered quantum-cloud work are legitimate ways to refute the claim. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates develop electrical and thermal energy balances, photovoltaic current-voltage behavior, storage dynamics, charge/discharge efficiency, AC power and converter losses, protected reserves, service deficit, weather-dependent demand, rolling-horizon constraints, chance and tail-risk measures, binary scheduling, QUBO and Ising mappings, QAOA evaluation, complete quantum computation time, feasible objective gaps, locked-reference Pareto hypervolume and physical simulation-to-test uncertainty. The F38 source's DeltaHV = HV(A_new) - HV(A_base) remains a secondary multiobjective research metric; its reference point and normalization must be frozen before measurement. Each mathematical plate defines units, assumptions, a specific blind falsification and related chapters. These are established conditional relations or proposed evaluation metrics, not newly discovered laws or demonstrations of quantum advantage. Eighty-two research chapters contain 410 separately paginated investigations about power custody, solar conversion, aging batteries, critical load services, control under uncertainty, quantum-classical comparisons and cross-laboratory evidence. Two hundred individually numbered Research Gates require targeted concealed faults, strong resource-matched rival explanations and hard-stop conditions. Thirty-three distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos propose specialized metering fixtures, load-emulation references, safety devices, computation audits and successor-ready evidence interfaces. These are prospective scientific objects, not fabricated instruments or completed research discoveries. Rejected runs, solver failures, negative experiments and correctly refused commands remain within the recorded study population. This monograph is a hypothesis-forming, non-occupancy research architecture; its methods require prospective physical validation, expert mathematical review and independent replication. summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .

summary: Analysis code accompanying the paper "When Fidelity Becomes Disclosure: Privacy Risk of Synthetic Data Generated from Very Small Rehabilitation Trials in Parkinson's Disease" (submitted to ACDSA 2027). The code trains four tabular generators (Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, TVAE, CopulaGAN) and a differentially private generator (AIM) on a pilot trial of serious games versus physiotherapy in Parkinson's disease (n = 22; arms of 10 and 12). It measures how much the synthetic records disclose about the training patients: normalised distance to closest record (DCR), near and exact copies, nearest-neighbour distance ratio, a leave-one-out membership-inference attack and an attribute-inference attack, with patient-level cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals. Fidelity (mean |Δ Spearman ρ| and Kolmogorov–Smirnov) is reported as a comparison axis. Contents: privacy_eval.py (generators, metrics, attacks, Table I), supplementary_analyses.py (Table II, per-patient atypicality, discretised-real baseline), make_figures.py (Figs. 2–4), copula_diagnostics.py (rank and marginal-family diagnostics of the Gaussian Copula with n < p), requirements.txt with the exact library versions. The README maps every command to the table or figure it reproduces. The de-identified dataset is not included in this record. Download it from https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23091123 and place it in dataset/ .

summary: This archive reproduces every table and figure in Onodje, P. and Adekoya, O., 'Administered farmgate prices and the cross-border leakage of cocoa: evidence from mirror trade statistics in West Africa'. The paper relates importer-reported (mirror) imports of cocoa beans (HS 1801) from Togo, Liberia and Guinea to the gap between the world cocoa price and the farmgate prices fixed by the marketing boards of Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire, 2012 to 2026. The package contains Python scripts for data download, estimation and figures; a hand-compiled record of 40 farmgate price announcements (2015/16 to 2026/27) with a source for each; openly licensed price, exchange rate and FAOSTAT production data; aggregated outlet-level trade series with SHA-256 checksums of the raw files; all outputs; and a dated, hashed prediction file that pre-specifies a held-out test for June to December 2026. UN Comtrade terms of use do not permit redistribution of the trade records, so the archive provides aggregated series that reproduce the headline estimates; the download script retrieves the underlying records with a free UN Comtrade subscription key. Code is released under the MIT licence; data compiled by the authors and outputs under CC BY 4.0. See README.md for instructions.

summary:
Submission-ready reproducibility release for the PL-Seq reanalysis.

This version includes the revised manuscript source and title, complete Nature-style software references, the bioRxiv PDF build workflow, seven machine-readable supplementary tables, the renamed and updated Supplementary Figure 1 catalog, updated Figure 1 timeline, and stable Zenodo concept-DOI citation metadata.

All repository safety, syntax, and reviewed-figure checksum checks passed before release. This version adds the exact AMD64 Apptainer SIF used for FASTQ alignment, BAM processing, molecule filtering, and PSI reconstruction. The binary environment is accompanied by a SHA-256 checksum, embedded image labels, a command-derived software-version report, and usage documentation. The original Apptainer definition file was not retained; therefore, the archived SIF is the authoritative record of the executed computational environment. This version adds plseq-plotting.sif , a rebuildable Apptainer environment for programmatic PL-Seq and direct-RNA figure generation. It includes Python, Matplotlib, pyGenomeTracks, R plotting packages, Pandoc, and Poppler. The image passed embedded dependency tests, PNG/PDF artifact tests, and end-to-end rendering of the seven-page, 28-gene direct-RNA atlas.
title: Reproducible reanalysis of targeted long-read RNA sequencing data improves statistical inference and read-level visualization

summary: An authentic group of pre-Columbian ceramics, probably from Risaralda, appears to rhyme with Japan's 5,000-year-old Jōmon Venus. The resemblance is real; a historical connection is not. This GLIAG essay shows how two distant societies independently turned clay and the human body into instruments of memory, identity and ritual, and why archaeological context determines what we can responsibly know. The Japanese comparator is identified securely: the 27 cm, 2.14 kg clay dogū known as the Jōmon Venus, recovered intact at the Tanabatake site in Chino, Nagano, and dated by the responsible museum to the Middle Jōmon, about 3000 BCE. The Colombian objects are, on their custodian's account, authentic, Colombian and probably from Risaralda, reportedly recovered by guaqueros; their context, ceramic phase and date are undocumented. The essay sets out a disciplined visual comparison across eight analytical axes, discusses the body as vessel, gender and fertility, convergence without contact, and guaquería as knowledge loss, and closes with a research programme for the Risaralda objects. Nothing in it demonstrates trans-Pacific contact; the strongest explanation is convergent figuration. Bilingual edition, English then Spanish. This Zenodo edition (Revision 2.1, 31 October 2026) reproduces the web edition first published on Petroleum & Energy Insights on 13 September 2026 (GLIAG-ESS-2026-038-CH REV 002), with an amendment register, full references, licence and citation. Figure 1 of the web edition (two source images) is not reproduced for rights reasons. The essay is not an appraisal, title opinion or authentication of any object.
title: Two Worlds, One Human Form: the Jōmon Venus of Japan and anthropomorphic ceramics from Cauca Medio, Colombia

summary: Next Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) requires the integration of increasingly heterogeneous evidence from New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), computational models, chemical information, biological mechanisms and exposure assessment. RISK-HUNT3R WP9 has addressed a fundamental challenge for this transition: how to organise, connect and reuse diverse scientific information so that it can support transparent, reproducible and human-relevant safety assessment. The RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure provides a FAIR-oriented digital environment for managing and connecting experimental data, methods, compounds, computational resources and mechanistic knowledge. Its architecture combines harmonised data and metadata templates, controlled vocabularies and ontologies, compound and methods databases, BioStudies and EdelweissData integration, knowledge graphs, computational tools, AI assistance resources and cloud-based services. Together these resources support the progression from data capture and curation to analysis, mechanistic interpretation and evidence integration. The infrastructure has been deployed across distributed project partners to support collaborative research and reuse of RISK-HUNT3R and legacy EU-ToxRisk resources. A central principle emerging from this work is that effective NGRA infrastructure must support more than FAIR data. Methods, models, workflows, provenance, applicability and uncertainty also need to be captured so that scientific results can be interpreted within their Context of Use and assembled into evidence supporting a decision. Resources including ToxTemp, compound and methods databases, knowledge graphs, EdelweissData and ASPA-based workflows provide complementary components of this evolving evidence architecture. The resulting infrastructure provides both an operational resource for RISK-HUNT3R and a foundation for future development. By connecting data, methods, models and mechanistic knowledge through interoperable digital resources, RISK-HUNT3R demonstrates a pathway from fragmented NAM outputs towards reusable evidence workflows supporting transparent NGRA.

summary: This repository provides the MATLAB source code and reproducibility resources associated with the manuscript entitled “Physics-Guided Reduced-Order Screening of Radiative Loss, Preferential Diffusion, and NOₓ Pathway Competition in Ammonia/Hydrogen Diffusion Flames,” submitted to the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy (Manuscript No. HE-D-26-13275). The computational framework employs a two-dimensional axisymmetric, physics-guided reduced-order model to investigate the coupled effects of radiative heat loss, preferential diffusion, ammonia cracking, hydrogen enrichment, pressure, and strain on non-premixed ammonia/hydrogen diffusion flames. The MATLAB implementation supports the reproduction of the manuscript's numerical analyses, including baseline flame characteristics, reaction-zone localization, thermal response, relative NOₓ formation tendencies, scalar dissipation, extinction susceptibility, robustness indicators, mechanism-isolation studies, numerical convergence, closure sensitivity, uncertainty analyses, parametric sweeps, and Pareto-based screening. Repository contents and reproducibility The principal file, Master_NH3H2_ROM_Reproducibility.m , contains the model formulation, numerical procedures, analysis modules, and routines for generating supporting figures, numerical tables, and datasets. Executing the master function creates an organized output directory containing the enabled computational results. Model scope and limitations The framework is intended for comparative mechanism screening and prioritization of operating conditions for subsequent higher-fidelity investigations. It does not solve the full governing conservation equations or detailed chemical kinetics. The relative NOₓ formation-tendency index is not an absolute emission concentration, emission factor, or outlet flux. Similarly, the extinction and robustness indicators represent comparative screening metrics rather than experimentally validated stability limits. The repository supports transparency, reproducibility, and further development of computational screening methods for ammonia/hydrogen combustion. Associated manuscript: International Journal of Hydrogen Energy, HE-D-26-13275. Keywords: Ammonia/hydrogen combustion; reduced-order modeling; MATLAB; radiative heat loss; preferential diffusion; NOₓ formation tendency; extinction; uncertainty analysis; reproducibility.
title: Physics-Guided Reduced-Order MATLAB Framework for Radiative Loss, Preferential Diffusion, and NOₓ Pathway Competition in Ammonia/Hydrogen Diffusion Flames: Code and Reproducibility Data

summary: Learned surrogates of process simulators are often evaluated on random states from plants they have already seen. This technical report compares interpolation, leave-one-case-out, and leave-one-ore-group-out evaluation for five models trained on a steady-state mineral-processing simulator. The simulator tracks mineral mass over 63 size classes, water, closed grinding circuits, and unit-level balance closure. It reports limitations against published examples alongside the comparisons. On a 3,072-state design over twelve authored cases, the multilayer perceptron gives the lowest interpolation recovery RMSE (3.38 percentage points), but has a 26.24-point mean RMSE when each case is held out. The Gaussian process has the lowest mean held-out-case RMSE (10.95 points), while the perceptron has the highest median case-fold R-squared (0.547). Under ore-group holdout, the perceptron's median recovery R-squared is 0.437 across seven groups, but varies from 0.795 for the five chalcopyrite cases to -10.2 for the two gold-in-pyrite cases. Log-upgrade transfer is poor for every model. The cases are authored; these results do not establish performance on operating plants. The report documents the mineral-processing simulator, its physical models, machine-learning evaluation methods, a process-specific optimization study, data and preprocessing, validation protocols, limitations, and reproducibility. Source code and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_OreFlow
title: How far does a learned surrogate of a flowsheet simulator transfer across ores? A closed-circuit, size-by-mineral engine, with cases and ore groups held out

summary: Cross-border art transactions carry two kinds of legal uncertainty that reform proposals typically treat as one: incomplete verification of who owned, sold, or previously possessed a work, and divergent national rules about what follows once ownership and possession are established beyond dispute. Drawing on a nineteen-year restitution dispute in which the underlying facts were settled well before the litigation ended, this article shows that only the first kind of uncertainty yields to better documentation, tracing, or verification infrastructure; the second persists because national legal systems assign the risk of a stolen object's resale differently, a distributive choice that additional evidence does not change. Recent computational and blockchain-based compliance proposals close real gaps in beneficial-ownership tracing and anti-money-laundering enforcement. Applied to restitution litigation, the same proposals leave the underlying divergence untouched. Reclassifying the deficits identified in existing legal-architecture scholarship along this line separates the problems computational investment can solve from the one that needs a binding choice-of-law rule instead.
tags: art market regulation; provenance; choice of law; anti-money laundering; cultural property restitution; regulatory architecture.
title: A. TILLARD AND THE LEGAL QUESTIONS BEHIND THE GLOBAL ART MARKET

summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
title: DinHot: A Holographic Optical Trap Studio Comparing Hologram Methods on a Device Model

summary: An authentic group of pre-Columbian ceramics, probably from Risaralda, appears to rhyme with Japan's 5,000-year-old Jōmon Venus. The resemblance is real; a historical connection is not. This GLIAG essay shows how two distant societies independently turned clay and the human body into instruments of memory, identity and ritual, and why archaeological context determines what we can responsibly know. The Japanese comparator is identified securely: the 27 cm, 2.14 kg clay dogū known as the Jōmon Venus, recovered intact at the Tanabatake site in Chino, Nagano, and dated by the responsible museum to the Middle Jōmon, about 3000 BCE. The Colombian objects are, on their custodian's account, authentic, Colombian and probably from Risaralda, reportedly recovered by guaqueros; their context, ceramic phase and date are undocumented. The essay sets out a disciplined visual comparison across eight analytical axes, discusses the body as vessel, gender and fertility, convergence without contact, and guaquería as knowledge loss, and closes with a research programme for the Risaralda objects. Nothing in it demonstrates trans-Pacific contact; the strongest explanation is convergent figuration. Bilingual edition, English then Spanish. This Zenodo edition (Revision 2.1, 31 October 2026) reproduces the web edition first published on Petroleum & Energy Insights on 13 September 2026 (GLIAG-ESS-2026-038-CH REV 002), with an amendment register, full references, licence and citation. Figure 1 of the web edition (two source images) is not reproduced for rights reasons. The essay is not an appraisal, title opinion or authentication of any object.
title: Two Worlds, One Human Form: the Jōmon Venus of Japan and anthropomorphic ceramics from Cauca Medio, Colombia

summary: This record contains the derived data, analysis code and search exports produced by a controlled re-analysis of publicly available mass-spectrometry proteomics datasets on the extracellular matrix (ECM) and the matrisome. summary: Next Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) requires the integration of increasingly heterogeneous evidence from New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), computational models, chemical information, biological mechanisms and exposure assessment. RISK-HUNT3R WP9 has addressed a fundamental challenge for this transition: how to organise, connect and reuse diverse scientific information so that it can support transparent, reproducible and human-relevant safety assessment. The RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure provides a FAIR-oriented digital environment for managing and connecting experimental data, methods, compounds, computational resources and mechanistic knowledge. Its architecture combines harmonised data and metadata templates, controlled vocabularies and ontologies, compound and methods databases, BioStudies and EdelweissData integration, knowledge graphs, computational tools, AI assistance resources and cloud-based services. Together these resources support the progression from data capture and curation to analysis, mechanistic interpretation and evidence integration. The infrastructure has been deployed across distributed project partners to support collaborative research and reuse of RISK-HUNT3R and legacy EU-ToxRisk resources. A central principle emerging from this work is that effective NGRA infrastructure must support more than FAIR data. Methods, models, workflows, provenance, applicability and uncertainty also need to be captured so that scientific results can be interpreted within their Context of Use and assembled into evidence supporting a decision. Resources including ToxTemp, compound and methods databases, knowledge graphs, EdelweissData and ASPA-based workflows provide complementary components of this evolving evidence architecture. The resulting infrastructure provides both an operational resource for RISK-HUNT3R and a foundation for future development. By connecting data, methods, models and mechanistic knowledge through interoperable digital resources, RISK-HUNT3R demonstrates a pathway from fragmented NAM outputs towards reusable evidence workflows supporting transparent NGRA.
title: From NAM Data to Trusted Evidence: RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure for Next Generation Risk Assessment

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. summary: This study presents the first comprehensive investigation of the horsefly (Diptera: Tabanidae) fauna of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic, Azerbaijan, based on field surveys conducted between 2021 and 2025. A total of 451 specimens were collected and identified, comprising 37 species belonging to the subfamilies Tabaninae, Chrysopsinae and Pangoninae. Four species Tabanus nemoralis , T. obsolescens , Haematopota pallidula and H. pandazisi are recorded for the first time from Azerbaijan, while ten species are new records for Nakhchivan, raising the known Tabanidae fauna of the country to 90 species. Tabanus bifarius (20.39%) and T. bromius (17.52%) were the most frequently captured species, whereas Haematopota pandazisi , was rarely sampled, represented by only a single specimen. Ecological diversity analysis revealed the highest species richness in Julfa and Babek, while Ordubad (Goygol) and Ordubad (Pazmari) exhibited markedly reduced diversity, reflecting a clear altitudinal zonation of the fauna across the region. These findings substantially expand the known distribution and diversity of Tabanidae in Azerbaijan and provide baseline data for future ecological and veterinary research in Nakhchivan.
title: New contributions to the fauna of horseflies (Diptera, Tabanidae) in Azerbaijan, Nakhchivan

summary: This archive contains the replication package for the article "Are colour-coded economies empirically distinct? A cross-country test of economic specialisation" (submitted to Structural Change and Economic Dynamics). It includes four Google Colab notebooks that reproduce all results, a fifth notebook that assembles the package, the HS 2017 product lists used to define the trade colours (UNCTADstat classifications), the activity-to-colour concordance files, all processed data, the supplementary workbook (Supplementary_Data.xlsx) and a data dictionary. Employment specialisation is computed from ILOSTAT (ISIC Rev. 4 divisions) and export specialisation from CEPII BACI (HS 2017, version 202601) for 2017–2024. Raw source files are not redistributed; the notebooks download them from the providers. Code is released under the MIT licence; derived data and product lists under CC BY 4.0.

summary: 智能奈米機器人自主建築修復極限 41/90 INTELLIGENT NANOROBOTIC AUTONOMOUS ARCHITECTURAL REPAIR AT THE LIMIT INTELLIGENT NANOROBOTIC AUTONOMOUS ARCHITECTURAL REPAIR AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 41 of 90). It investigates whether locally operated micro-scale robotic inspection and repair methods might detect concealed cracks, moisture ingress, damaged mechanical interfaces and environmental faults, then restore independently measurable properties without concealing failure. The core coupling is Micro/Nano Sensing x Local Repair x Structural Reliability. Every proposed integrated test is limited to unoccupied scaled habitat panels, damaged coupons, environmental chambers and supervised hardware-in-the-loop systems; no inhabited dwelling, nanorobotic building maintenance system or structural certification is claimed. The falsifiable candidate predicts higher independently verified fault recall without worsening preregistered post-repair air-quality recovery under equal inspection exposure, material supply, energy, sensing, computation, time and human-operations budgets. Repair success is separately conditional on load-path requalification, credible reference identity, moisture containment and a functioning physical stop. A controlled localized robotic repair system must compete with scheduled expert inspection, replace-on-failure maintenance and expert-performed local treatment. Concealed moisture, common-mode sensor drift, inaccessible crack ligaments, incompatible repair chemistry and hidden support fixtures are ways the hypothesis can fail. Negative specimens, refused states, destructive tests and incomplete repairs remain in the full denominator. Thirty mechanically and statistically distinct research plates include Paris-regime fatigue crack growth, mode-I and mixed-mode fracture, energy release, cohesive-interface work, load balance, fatigue survival, detection recall and false clearance, ultrasound and acoustic observability, thermal and moisture transport, contaminant mass balance, resin flow, cure kinetics, correlated uncertainty, materials and energy accounting, conditional causal effects and physically verified stop latency. Each mathematical plate states its mechanism, dimensional assumptions, independent reference, blinded contradiction and research-chapter links. The seed Paris relation da/dN = C(Delta K)^m is a conditional empirical model for particular fatigue regimes, not a universal law of repair or evidence that a crack has healed. Eighty-two chapters and 410 single-page investigations examine specimen provenance, hidden crack truth, fracture and fatigue, imaging and sensor drift, repair-material chemistry, robotic deposition, wall-module utility boundaries, environmental requalification, long-cycle maintenance and independent laboratory reconstruction. Two hundred individually worded Research Gates challenge different physical witnesses, resource-matched rivals, coupled faults, false-clear decisions and reproducibility limits. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separate future scientific objects, including fracture-reference capsules, moisture witnesses, cure validation rigs, aerosol exposure ledgers, physical interlocks and cross-site specimen relays. These are research proposals and evidence contracts, not demonstrated autonomous repair devices. The research is hypothetical, non-occupancy and intentionally vulnerable to refutation. Existing studies establish bounded robotic crack inspection and concrete sealing methods, polymer-glass simulation mechanisms, fatigue testing practices and material measurement approaches, but do not validate the integrated F41 architecture. Relevant external literature includes Li et al. (2026), DOI 10.1038/s44172-026-00637-0; Ruiz-Franco and Giuntoli (2025), DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-59426-6; Huang et al. (2026), DOI 10.1016/j.autcon.2026.107006; Chen et al. (2022), DOI 10.1

Every proposed integrated test is limited to unoccupied scaled habitat panels, damaged coupons, environmental chambers and supervised hardware-in-the-loop systems; no inhabited dwelling, nanorobotic building maintenance system or structural certification is claimed. The falsifiable candidate predicts higher independently verified fault recall without worsening preregistered post-repair air-quality recovery under equal inspection exposure, material supply, energy, sensing, computation, time and human-operations budgets. Repair success is separately conditional on load-path requalification, credible reference identity, moisture containment and a functioning physical stop. A controlled localized robotic repair system must compete with scheduled expert inspection, replace-on-failure maintenance and expert-performed local treatment. Concealed moisture, common-mode sensor drift, inaccessible crack ligaments, incompatible repair chemistry and hidden support fixtures are ways the hypothesis can fail. Negative specimens, refused states, destructive tests and incomplete repairs remain in the full denominator. summary: This repository contains the analysis code and public-safe source data accompanying the manuscript “Mid-Holocene rise in Pinus pollen across Northeast Asia without regional forest expansion” (submitted to Communications Earth & Environment ) and its Supplementary Information. Package Contents code/ : five standalone Python scripts reproducing the REML random-effects meta-analysis ( reproduce_public_meta.py ), astronomical insolation calculations ( compute_orbital_insolation.py ), Lake Xiaolongwan marker-calibrated pollen accumulation rate (PAR) bootstraps ( confirmed_xlw_par.py ), genus-level taxon decompositions ( reproduce_taxon_decomposition.py ), and Lake Moon pseudocount sensitivity tests ( recompute_lake_moon_pseudocount.py ). source_data/tables/ : cell-by-cell synchronized CSV tables for Supplementary Tables S1–S15. source_data/figure_sources/ : underlying data points and summaries for main Figures 1–6 and Supplementary Figures S1–S8. source_data/moon_sensitivity/ : 100-year bin data and sensitivity outputs across four pseudocount treatments for Lake Moon. source_data/Supplementary_Data_1_Xiaolongwan_* : derived concentrations, PAR, bin summaries, and bootstrap outputs for Lake Xiaolongwan. source_data/Supplementary_Data_2_TraCE21ka.csv : nine-site TraCE-21ka climate metrics. source_data/taxon_aggregates/ , dali_aggregates/ , orbital_insolation/ : supporting aggregates, Berger–Loutre 1991 insolation inputs, and validation data. summary: This repository contains the data, Python code and supporting computational material accompanying the article “Auditing life-cycle loss comparisons for seismic retrofit: a traceable stone-masonry case study.” The package supports the reproducible examination of historical life-cycle loss calculations for a stone-masonry building and alternative strengthening interventions. It provides traceability between source-reported quantities, calculation assumptions, recalculated results and the numerical figures and tables presented in the article. The archive includes: A source-data register with source-page references, provenance classifications and uncertainty notes. Python scripts reproducing the historical arithmetic and reconciling 22 reported loss values. Numerical datasets, figures and tables supporting the article. An independent loss-assessment engine and its synthetic test suite, kept separate from the historical reproduction workflow. Execution instructions, dependency versions, verification logs and file checksums. The reconciliation identifies 17 of 22 reported values within the tolerance bands obtained by propagating the stated precision of the fitted parameters ; five values fall outside those bands. Verification of the independent engine produced 114 passing tests and 10 skipped comparisons , with the skips attributable to unavailable earlier engine versions. Version: 1.0

summary: This repository contains the data, Python code and supporting computational material accompanying the article “Auditing life-cycle loss comparisons for seismic retrofit: a traceable stone-masonry case study.” The package supports the reproducible examination of historical life-cycle loss calculations for a stone-masonry building and alternative strengthening interventions. It provides traceability between source-reported quantities, calculation assumptions, recalculated results and the numerical figures and tables presented in the article. The archive includes: A source-data register with source-page references, provenance classifications and uncertainty notes. Python scripts reproducing the historical arithmetic and reconciling 22 reported loss values. Numerical datasets, figures and tables supporting the article. An independent loss-assessment engine and its synthetic test suite, kept separate from the historical reproduction workflow. Execution instructions, dependency versions, verification logs and file checksums. The reconciliation identifies 17 of 22 reported values within the tolerance bands obtained by propagating the stated precision of the fitted parameters ; five values fall outside those bands. Verification of the independent engine produced 114 passing tests and 10 skipped comparisons , with the skips attributable to unavailable earlier engine versions. Version: 1.0

summary: AnaTele is an open-source desktop tool for investigating ArduPilot flight logs (.tlog, .bin, .log). It infers flight phases, replays the recorded path in 3D, evaluates a versioned declarative rule pack with four explicit result states, and ranks competing failure hypotheses by capped evidence-family support minus contradictions, without assigning probabilities. Every finding links to the exact log record. It includes a fault-injection quadcopter simulator and a hash-verified shareable analysis format (.ant). Documentation: avinashistoocool.github.io/AnaTele

summary: CIRCULAR MATERIAL ECONOMIES FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE CITIES AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:移動城市循環經濟與材料永續極限 55/90 CIRCULAR MATERIAL ECONOMIES FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE CITIES AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 55 of 90). It investigates whether a deliberately unoccupied six-module mobile-city research system can reduce relocation-related material loss through qualified reuse, automated selective disassembly and auditable remanufacturing, while preserving deployment latency and critical-service safety. The three-way research coupling is Circular Materials x Autonomous Manufacturing x Urban Sustainability. Neither a functioning autonomous city nor a human-occupied habitat is asserted. The falsifiable proposal compares a frozen circular material strategy against competent conventional manual recovery, replacement and stationary emergency infrastructure under equal material, energy, sensing, technician-hour, tool, water and transport budgets. Original intake, declined parts, work in progress, consumed adhesives, repeated repairs, rejected batches and retired material remain in the denominator. Blind faults include grade swaps, hidden fatigue, wrong material passports, replayed scale measurements, contamination, source-energy omissions and optimistic virgin-substitution credits. A proposal fails whenever a load-bearing component, utility service, waste route, safety interlock or material identity cannot be independently reconstructed. Thirty mechanism-distinct research formula plates address mass custody, qualified yield, bond separation work, fatigue, polymer rheology, sensor residuals, covariance, electrical energy, verified lifecycle inventory, carbon-allocation sensitivity, replacement counterfactuals, tail risk, second-site reproduction and noncompensatory physical release. The original contract's cyber-physical residual r_k = y_k - yhat_k(x_k,u_k) is retained as one fault-detection method; it is not treated as a law of circularity or sustainability. Every mathematical plate states units, validity assumptions, a blinded counterexample and scientific chapter interfaces. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated research studies and 200 Research Gates, each connected to a specified material state, independent reference, fault or competing process. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose research instruments, material-qualification fixtures, provenance devices, circularity accounting tools and successor-ready evidence protocols. This work proposes hypotheses and reproducibility obligations, not physical trial outcomes. Its complete PDF also contains research limits, negative-result custody and second-laboratory transfer requirements. The scope remains prospective, scaled and non-occupancy. Environmental performance requires functional-unit parity and a complete lifecycle inventory; increasing recovered mass alone does not prove lower environmental burden. Relevant method references include Ostapska et al. (10.1016/j.spc.2024.05.014), Formentini et al. (10.1016/j.jclepro.2025.145459), Attia et al. (10.1016/j.autcon.2024.105521), Mao and Cao (10.1016/j.spc.2024.12.021), Poschmann et al. (10.1002/cite.201900107) and Keating et al. (10.1126/scirobotics.aam8986). The Flagship 13 mother genealogy identifiers (10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839) were provided by the author and their metadata have not been independently confirmed. No external study cited here establishes this integrated F55 architecture. It investigates whether a deliberately unoccupied six-module mobile-city research system can reduce relocation-related material loss through qualified reuse, automated selective disassembly and auditable remanufacturing, while preserving deployment latency and critical-service safety. The three-way research coupling is Circular Materials x Autonomous Manufacturing x Urban Sustainability. Neither a functioning autonomous city nor a human-occupied habitat is asserted. The falsifiable proposal compares a frozen circular material strategy against competent conventional manual recovery, replacement and stationary emergency infrastructure under equal material, energy, sensing, technician-hour, tool, water and transport budgets. Original intake, declined parts, work in progress, consumed adhesives, repeated repairs, rejected batches and retired material remain in the denominator. Blind faults include grade swaps, hidden fatigue, wrong material passports, replayed scale measurements, contamination, source-energy omissions and optimistic virgin-substitution credits. A proposal fails whenever a load-bearing component, utility service, waste route, safety interlock or material identity cannot be independently reconstructed. Thirty mechanism-distinct research formula plates address mass custody, qualified yield, bond separation work, fatigue, polymer rheology, sensor residuals, covariance, electrical energy, verified lifecycle inventory, carbon-allocation sensitivity, replacement counterfactuals, tail risk, second-site reproduction and noncompensatory physical release. The original contract's cyber-physical residual r_k = y_k - yhat_k(x_k,u_k) is retained as one fault-detection method; it is not treated as a law of circularity or sustainability. Every mathematical plate states units, validity assumptions, a blinded counterexample and scientific chapter interfaces. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated research studies and 200 Research Gates, each connected to a specified material state, independent reference, fault or competing process. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose research instruments, material-qualification fixtures, provenance devices, circularity accounting tools and successor-ready evidence protocols. This work proposes hypotheses and reproducibility obligations, not physical trial outcomes. Its complete PDF also contains research limits, negative-result custody and second-laboratory transfer requirements. The scope remains prospective, scaled and non-occupancy. Environmental performance requires functional-unit parity and a complete lifecycle inventory; increasing recovered mass alone does not prove lower environmental burden. Relevant method references include Ostapska et al. (10.1016/j.spc.2024.05.014), Formentini et al. (10.1016/j.jclepro.2025.145459), Attia et al. (10.1016/j.autcon.2024.105521), Mao and Cao (10.1016/j.spc.2024.12.021), Poschmann et al. (10.1002/cite.201900107) and Keating et al. (10.1126/scirobotics.aam8986). The Flagship 13 mother genealogy identifiers (10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839) were provided by the author and their metadata have not been independently confirmed. summary: Annotatsiya. Maqolada O‘zbekiston sug‘urta kompaniyalarining moliyaviy barqarorligini choraklik hisobotlar asosida baholashning integral indeks taklif etilgan. Asosiy e’tibor indikatorlar yo‘nalishini aniqlash masalasiga qaratilgan bo‘lib, zararlilik koeffitsiyenti va mukofotlar o‘sishi bozor etalonidan har ikki tomonga chetlanish sifatida olingan. 36 ta kompaniyaning 2021-2025 yillardagi ma’lumotlarida bunday indeks kompaniyalarning bozordan chiqishini an’anaviy indeksdan ancha yaxshi ajratib berishi asoslangan. Kalit so‘zlar: sug‘urta kompaniyasi, moliyaviy barqarorlik, integral indeks, zararlilik koeffitsiyenti, ob’ektiv vaznlar, ROC ( Tasniflash sifatini baholash egri chizig‘i) tahlil. Аннотация. В статье предлагается интегральный показатель для оценки финансовой устойчивости страховых компаний Узбекистана, основанный на данных из общедоступной квартальной отчетности. Основное внимание уделяется определению динамики показателей: коэффициент убыточности и темпы роста страховых премий рассматриваются как отклонения, в ту или иную сторону,   от рыночного ориентира. Анализ данных по 36 компаниям за период 2021-2025 гг. показывает, что данный показатель позволяет выявлять компании, покидающие рынок, значительно эффективнее, чем традиционный индекс. Ключевые слова: страховая компания, финансовая устойчивость, интегральный индекс, коэффициент убыточности, объективные веса, ROC-анализ. Abstract. The article proposes an integral index for assessing the financial stability of insurance companies in Uzbekistan based on quarterly reports. The main attention is focused on determining the direction of indicators, with the loss ratio and premium growth considered as deviations from the market benchmark in both directions. Based on data from 36 companies for 2021–2025, it is demonstrated that such an index distinguishes companies exiting the market significantly better than the traditional index. Keywords: insurance company, financial stability, composite index, loss ratio, objective weights, ROC analysis.

summary: Annotatsiya. Maqolada O‘zbekiston sug‘urta kompaniyalarining moliyaviy barqarorligini choraklik hisobotlar asosida baholashning integral indeks taklif etilgan. Asosiy e’tibor indikatorlar yo‘nalishini aniqlash masalasiga qaratilgan bo‘lib, zararlilik koeffitsiyenti va mukofotlar o‘sishi bozor etalonidan har ikki tomonga chetlanish sifatida olingan. 36 ta kompaniyaning 2021-2025 yillardagi ma’lumotlarida bunday indeks kompaniyalarning bozordan chiqishini an’anaviy indeksdan ancha yaxshi ajratib berishi asoslangan. Kalit so‘zlar: sug‘urta kompaniyasi, moliyaviy barqarorlik, integral indeks, zararlilik koeffitsiyenti, ob’ektiv vaznlar, ROC ( Tasniflash sifatini baholash egri chizig‘i) tahlil. Аннотация. В статье предлагается интегральный показатель для оценки финансовой устойчивости страховых компаний Узбекистана, основанный на данных из общедоступной квартальной отчетности. Основное внимание уделяется определению динамики показателей: коэффициент убыточности и темпы роста страховых премий рассматриваются как отклонения, в ту или иную сторону,   от рыночного ориентира. Анализ данных по 36 компаниям за период 2021-2025 гг. показывает, что данный показатель позволяет выявлять компании, покидающие рынок, значительно эффективнее, чем традиционный индекс. The article proposes an integral index for assessing the financial stability of insurance companies in Uzbekistan based on quarterly reports. The main attention is focused on determining the direction of indicators, with the loss ratio and premium growth considered as deviations from the market benchmark in both directions. Based on data from 36 companies for 2021–2025, it is demonstrated that such an index distinguishes companies exiting the market significantly better than the traditional index. summary: يهدف البحث الى اعداد برنامج علاجي سلوكي في الدافعية العقلية وتعلم السباحة الحرة لدى الطالبات، والتعرف على تأثير البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي في الدافعية العقلية وتعلم السباحة الحرة لدى الطالبات، ولتحقيق الهدف استخدمت الباحث المَنهجُ التجريبي وبتصميم المجموعتين التجريبية والضابطة المتكافئتين ذو الإختِبار القبلي والبعدي لملائمته مع مشكلة واهداف البحث، حدد مجتمع البحث بطالبات المرحلة الثانية للدراسة الصباحية في كلية التربية البدنية وعلوم الرياضة_ جامعة بغداد، للعامُ الدراسي   2025 - 2026   و البالغ عددهم (110) طالبة مُوَزَعات على (4) شعب وهي (أ، ب، ج، د) وتم تحديد مجتمع البحث بطالبات المرحلة الثانية كون هذه المرحلة تدرس مادة السباحة، أما عينة البحث، فقد اختيرت بالطريقة العشوائية باستخدام القرعة، إذ أُجريت قرعة بين الشعب الأربع لتحديد مجموعتي البحث (التجريبية والضابطة)، وأسفرت عن اختيار شعبتي (ب) و(د). وبعد ذلك، اختيرت (25) طالبة من كل شعبة بالطريقة نفسها، لتُمثل شعبة (ب) المجموعة التجريبية، في حين مثلت شعبة (د) المجموعة الضابطة، وبذلك بلغ العدد الكلي لعينة البحث (50) طالبة، أي ما نسبته (45.45%) من مجتمع البحث.ولتحقيق أهداف الدراسة، طبقت الباحثة الاختبارات القبلية على المجموعتين قبل البدء بتنفيذ الوحدات التعليمي، واجريت المعالجات الإحصائية المناسبة، وقد استنتجت الباحث بإنّ أسهم البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي بشكل إيجابي وفعّال في تنمية مستوى الدافعية العقلية لدى الطالبات، من خلال تعزيز الانتباه والتركيز والرغبة في التعلم، وكذلك وجود تحسن ملحوظ في تعلم السباحة الحرة لدى أفراد المجموعة التي طبّق عليها البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي، تفوق المجموعة التجريبية التي استخدمت البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي على المجموعة الضابطة التي اعتمدت الأسلوب التقليدي في كل من الدافعية العقلية والأداء المهاري. . The research aims to develop a behavioral intervention program focused on mental motivation and freestyle swimming acquisition among female students, and to determine the program's impact on these aspects. To achieve the research objective, the researcher employed the experimental method—specifically a design featuring two equivalent groups (experimental and control) with pre- and post-tests—due to its suitability for the research problem and objectives. The study population consisted of second-year female students in the morning program at the College of Physical Education and Sports Sciences, University of Baghdad, during the 2025–2026 academic year. The total population comprised 110 students distributed across four sections (A, B, C, and D); the second-year cohort was selected because the swimming course is taught at this stage of the curriculum. The research sample was selected by randomly assigning the class sections to the experimental and control groups. Subsequently, the researcher randomly selected 25 female students from each section—specifically Section B (25 students) and Section D (25 students)—resulting in a total sample of 50 students (representing 45.45% of the population). The researcher then administered pre-tests and post-tests to both the experimental and control groups. Appropriate statistical analyses were conducted, leading the researcher to conclude that the behavioral therapeutic program contributed positively and effectively to enhancing the female students' level of mental motivation by fostering attention, concentration, and the desire to learn. Furthermore, a marked improvement in freestyle swimming skills was observed among the participants who underwent the behavioral therapeutic program; the experimental group utilizing this program outperformed the control group—which relied on the traditional method—in both mental motivation and skill performance.
title: تأثير برنامج علاجي سلوكي في الدافعية العقلية وتعلم السباحة الحرة للطالبات. The Effect of a Behavioral Therapeutic Program on Cognitive Motivation and Freestyle Swimming Learning Among Female Students

summary: This record provides the frozen Python research scripts and derived experimental evidence for a study of selective sensor-quality gating in wearable human activity recognition. The included code covers subject-disjoint evaluation on PAMAP2 and MHEALTH, synthetic sensor degradation, comparisons with uniform, static and confidence-based fusion, and a Windows-host pipeline timing benchmark. Derived CSV and JSON files include evaluation reports, per-window classification results, static fusion weights and timing measurements. Original PAMAP2 and MHEALTH sensor recordings are not redistributed; they must be obtained from their respective official sources (DOIs: 10.24432/C5NW2H and 10.24432/C5TW22). The original experiment scripts are preserved byte-for-byte and contain Windows-specific paths and dependencies; they should not be interpreted as turnkey portable software. The reported gains are condition-dependent and exploratory, and the timing measurements do not establish embedded-device energy efficiency or latency. No research manuscript, publication figures or LaTeX sources are included.
title: Selective Sensor-Quality Gating for Wearable Activity Recognition: Research Code and Derived Evidence

summary: This package contains the code that produces every table and figure quoted in the paper "The Widening Mathematics Gap: Boys, Girls and Who Is Missing from PISA. 38 OECD Countries, 2015–2025", the small public inputs it needs (population and coverage tables), and the country-level results behind every OECD average. PISA microdata are not redistributed; they are public and must be downloaded from the OECD (see README). Code comments and docstrings are in Spanish; the README documents the pipeline in English. Version 2 (31 October 2026) adds code/53_revision_v18.py (inference for the trend bounds of Table 5: bias correction of country-specific extrema, coverage simulation, Stoye intervals) and replaces the supplement PDF with version v19. Scripts 01–38 and data files S1–S13 are unchanged.

summary: تهدف الدراسة الى التعرف على العلاقة مستوى الطموح الرياضي وعلاقته بالحواجز النفسية لدى لاعبي الدوري العراقي الممتاز بالكرة الطائرة. ولهذا الغرض استخدم الباحث منهج الوصفي على عينة من(84)لاعب تم اختيارها بشكل عمدي ولجمع البيانات استخدم الباحث استبيان مستوى الطموح الرياضي و الحواجز النفسية بعد جمع النتائج ومعالجتها تم التوصل أن وجود علاقة ارتباطية عكسية بين مستوى الطموح الرياضي و الحواجز النفسية, وعلى هذا الاساس أوصت الدراسة ضرورة وجود مختص نفسي لكل من الفرق المحلية للكرة الطائرة وكذلك حث اللاعبين بجميع الفئات على تطوير مستوى الطموح لديهم وان يكون يتناسب مع قدرات هم The present study aims to investigate the correlational relationship between athletic ambition and psychological barriers among players competing in the Iraqi Premier Volleyball League. To achieve this objective, the researcher employed the descriptive survey method, utilizing a purposively selected sample comprising (84) players. Data were collected using the Athletic Ambition Scale and the Psychological Barriers Scale. Following data collection and statistical analysis, the findings revealed a statistically significant inverse (negative) correlation between athletic ambition and psychological barriers. Accordingly, the study recommends the integration of a specialized psychologist within each local volleyball club. Furthermore, it emphasizes the necessity of encouraging players across all categories to develop their ambition levels in a manner that is commensurate with their individual capabilities
