summary: LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:可變形移動居住系統長期宜居性極限 56/90 LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 56 of 90). It investigates whether a traceable unoccupied morphing habitat testbed can improve the joint coverage of measured thermal, airflow, moisture, energy and structural engineering envelopes across controlled seasonal sequences while preserving independently reconstructable module identity. Its core coupling is Human-Comfort Proxy Models x Environmental Control x Longitudinal Test Evidence. The project uses guarded coupons, scaled modules, environmental chambers, inert-water and tracer-air circuits, and hardware-in-the-loop tests; it does not observe residents or establish an occupancy certificate. The preregisterable hypothesis is that, under matched materials, energy reserves, maintenance, sensor access, control computation and test time, a frozen morphing environmental-control policy will improve complete-cohort comfort-envelope proxy coverage without worsening module-identity continuity relative to competent static-habitat and expert manual-reconfiguration baselines. The supplied selective-risk candidate R_sel(tau)=E[L(yhat,y)|c>=tau] must be published with accepted coverage, so a low risk score cannot be purchased by refusing nearly every difficult climate or aging case. Hidden trials vary aging gaskets, radiant asymmetry, tracer-air pockets, power outages, sensor common-mode drift, broken connectors, incorrect material identity and ineffective physical stop contacts. Thirty mechanism-specific mathematical plates analyze heat balance, conductive and radiant transfer, operative temperature proxies, vapor mass and dew-point margins, air exchange, ventilation pressure, energy and water closure, sound, light, fatigue, reliability, stale information, uncertainty covariance, selective-risk coverage, tail excursions and second-site reconstruction. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated investigations spanning material aging, climate control, indoor-environment proxy limitations, repair, operator authority and versioned evidence. Two hundred Research Gates formulate disconfirmable experimental questions across concealed faults, equal-resource comparisons and two-mechanism interfaces. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separately falsifiable future rigs, calibration artifacts, safe-stop witnesses and successor evidence packages. The volume is a prospective research design rather than a completed experimental study. An unoccupied thermal or tracer-gas rig cannot establish human comfort, healthy air, habitable water, fire and structural compliance, actual multiyear life, or a right to place people inside a mobile dwelling. The 777-page layout and enumerated items are structurally checked, but a language-duplication audit finds reused long editorial method spans; semantic uniqueness, physical modeling and all evidence inferences remain subject to deeper independent review. Relevant independently identified method references include Fanger (1973), DOI 10.1136/oem.30.4.313; de Dear and Brager (2001), DOI 10.1007/s004840100093; Brager and de Dear (1998), DOI 10.1016/S0378-7788(97)00053-4; Dang, Janssen and Roels (2024), DOI 10.1007/s12273-024-1176-8; Dang et al. (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.buildenv.2025.112867; and Broughton and Maxwell (2023), DOI 10.47120/npl.mgpg103. Standards ISO 7730:2025, ASHRAE 55-2023, and ASHRAE 62.1/62.2-2025 provide bounded normative context, not F56 verification. summary: Abstract Debates about artificial intelligence increasingly focus on synthetic data, simulation, model reasoning, and autonomous agents rather than on data collection alone. This paper examines whether these developments justify describing the emerging digital economy as “post-data.” It argues that the term is useful only as a qualified analytical proposition: data is not disappearing, but its strategic value is being recombined with compute, model architecture, simulation, evaluation, and institutional trust. The paper uses a structured integrative literature review and comparative case analysis to examine three domains: compute-efficient language-model training and synthetic data; biomolecular modelling through AlphaFold 3; and synthetic data and simulation in healthcare and operational decision-making. The analysis identifies a transition from data accumulation as a standalone competitive advantage toward a complementary capability stack in which provenance, validation, domain constraints, and human accountability remain essential. The evidence does not support a universal replacement of empirical data by synthetic environments. Instead, it shows that synthetic systems can extend scarce or expensive observations while also reproducing source-data biases, creating privacy risks, and degrading when generated outputs are recursively reused without adequate grounding. The paper contributes a conceptual framework linking data provenance, synthetic generation, compute and reasoning, validation, and governance. It concludes with research propositions and a practical agenda for evaluating when synthetic and autonomous systems create durable value. Keywords : synthetic data; autonomous systems; simulation; digital economy; AI governance; model collapse; data provenance

summary: An authentic group of pre-Columbian ceramics, probably from Risaralda, appears to rhyme with Japan's 5,000-year-old Jōmon Venus. The resemblance is real; a historical connection is not. This GLIAG essay shows how two distant societies independently turned clay and the human body into instruments of memory, identity and ritual, and why archaeological context determines what we can responsibly know. The Japanese comparator is identified securely: the 27 cm, 2.14 kg clay dogū known as the Jōmon Venus, recovered intact at the Tanabatake site in Chino, Nagano, and dated by the responsible museum to the Middle Jōmon, about 3000 BCE. The Colombian objects are, on their custodian's account, authentic, Colombian and probably from Risaralda, reportedly recovered by guaqueros; their context, ceramic phase and date are undocumented. The essay sets out a disciplined visual comparison across eight analytical axes, discusses the body as vessel, gender and fertility, convergence without contact, and guaquería as knowledge loss, and closes with a research programme for the Risaralda objects. Nothing in it demonstrates trans-Pacific contact; the strongest explanation is convergent figuration. Bilingual edition, English then Spanish. This Zenodo edition (Revision 2.1, 31 October 2026) reproduces the web edition first published on Petroleum & Energy Insights on 13 September 2026 (GLIAG-ESS-2026-038-CH REV 002), with an amendment register, full references, licence and citation. Figure 1 of the web edition (two source images) is not reproduced for rights reasons. The essay is not an appraisal, title opinion or authentication of any object.
title: Two Worlds, One Human Form: the Jōmon Venus of Japan and anthropomorphic ceramics from Cauca Medio, Colombia

summary: Titolo: USAI-AGI: A Hybrid Cognitive Architecture for Artificial General Intelligence based on Applied Category Theory This work has been developed with the support of artificial intelligence linguistic models (Large Language Models), used as tools for consultation, exploration and co-elaboration. Every conceptual choice, every critical synthesis and every direction taken in solving the problem are the result of my autonomous thinking and my intellectual responsibility. The use of AI has represented an extension of my skills, not a substitute for my human contribution. Description: A Hybrid, Category-Theoretic Framework for Artificial General Intelligence: Architecture for Continuous Learning, Causal Reasoning, and Self-Improvement Author:  Luigi Usai Abstract: Current advancements in artificial intelligence, particularly Large Language Models, demonstrate impressive generative capabilities but often lack robust mechanisms for persistent knowledge integration, causal reasoning, and autonomous, goal-directed behavior. The system's core is a probabilistic Knowledge Base (KB) built on RDF, where each fact is associated with a confidence score that evolves over time. summary: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses natural electromagnetic field variations to image subsurface electrical resistivity at depths ranging from tens of metres to hundreds of kilometres. It is widely used in geophysical exploration for natural resources, including minerals, geothermal energy, and groundwater, as well as in the characterisation of sites for CO$_2$ storage and in studies of crustal and lithospheric structure. The MT inverse problem is, however, inherently non-unique: many distinct resistivity models reproduce the observations equally well. Conventional practice nonetheless reports a single regularised model, with no quantitative measure of its uncertainty. MTGeophysics.jl is a Julia package developed to address this limitation. Its principal aim is the quantification of uncertainty in MT model building, advancing interpretation from a single deterministic model, through an ensemble of plausible models, towards the full posterior distribution. The package also provides tools for data analysis, mesh generation, masking, forward modelling, inversion, model analysis and visualisation for MT research and applications. summary: Background. End-stage renal disease (ESRD) carries high mortality, but existing prognostic models begin at dialysis initiation, ignoring the metabolic trajectory that preceded renal failure. Whether the prodromal phenotype measured years before ESRD onset predicts subsequent survival is unknown. Methods. We studied 1,991 UK Biobank participants who developed ESRD (ICD-10 N185, Z992, or Z940) during a median 14.0 years of follow-up. Seven non-renal organ-specific prodromal function failure (pFF) scores and the Metabolic Inversion Phenotype (MIP) score were computed from baseline biomarkers measured 5–15 years before ESRD onset. Three renal pFF scores (pKD, pRD, pGN) were excluded a priori to avoid circularity. Cox proportional hazards models assessed the association of prodromal scores with all-cause mortality (642 deaths, 32.2%). Unsupervised K -means clustering identified distinct prodromal phenotypes. A compound endpoint model (dESRD) was built using gradient-boosted trees with out-of-fold evaluation on the full cohort. Results. Prodromal scores predicted mortality within the ESRD cohort. Age-sex-adjusted Cox models with individual pFF scores achieved C* 1 = 0 . 636 (∆C* = +0 . 023 vs. age + sex alone). Prodromal hypertension (pHT) was the dominant predictor (HR 5.55, 95% CI 2.93–10.49, p = 2 . 4 × 10 −7 ). Three prodromal phenotypes emerged: low-burden (N = 1,326; 15-year survival 76.2%), metabolic-vascular ( N = 574; 60.1%), and multi-organ storm ( N = 91; 38.0%; log-rank p = 2 . 5 × 10 −19 ). Cause-specific mortality shifted across phenotypes: cancer dominated the low-burden group (34.6% of deaths) while cardiovascular disease dominated the multi-organ storm (44.8%), with zero cancer deaths. The MIP score independently predicted survival (HR 0.81 per unit, p = 1 . 5 × 10 −9 ), with a gradient across cause-of- death categories from survivors (pMIP − 0 . 31) through cancer deaths ( − 0 . 51) to cardiovascular ( − 0 . 78) and diabetes deaths ( − 0 . 94; Kruskal-Wallis p = 6 . 6 × 10 −12 ). Cross-tabulating MIP tertile by pFF burden tertile revealed a 2.5-fold mortality gradient (19.7% to 48.5%). The compound dESRD model, integrating prodromal scores with clinical variables via gradient-boosted trees, achieved C* = 0 . 881 (95% CI 0.858–0.904), exceeding a portable model restricted to raw biomarkers (C* = 0.863). summary: A reading, from physics, of the two opening phrases of The Forgotten Quantum of Einstein : Einstein's question of whether the moon is there when no one looks, and the author's image of a space–time quantum some 186,000 miles across, pivoted on the Earth, holding the quantum world and the Universe in an interplay of information and gravity. Einstein's phrase is the realism/measurement problem (EPR, Bell); the macrobiotic quantum is the unit in which information, gravity and the observer are not separable — a light-ratio cell (ℓ/τ = c), an internal vacuum that stores state and an external vacuum observed as geometry, balanced by a vacuum angle θ_v, with energy E = mc² e^{iθ_v} + I·ΔS. The paper then draws the consequence for artificial intelligence: alignment, hallucination, interpretability, control, machine moral status, the fear of human replacement, and runaway behaviour persist because mainstream systems treat information, value and the observer as external to the substrate. Macrobiotic Quantum Theory (MQT) makes them physical, and an architecture built on it — the Large Theory Language Model (LTLM), toward Super Natural Intelligence (SNI) — treats alignment, interpretability and responsibility as structural properties rather than bolted-on filters, keeping the human (SDM) and the machine (MDS) as complementary, inseparable poles. The note stays strictly on the public MQT surface.

summary: Data and code for Mapping bioimage-analysis software adoption in microscopy. The registry contains 33 entries: 23 analysis packages, six microscope-control programs, MATLAB and Jupyter notebooks as references, Adobe Photoshop for figure preparation and NIH Image for historical counts. The 29-package aggregate combines the 23 analysis packages with six microscope-control programs. References, Photoshop and NIH Image are excluded. The archive holds processed counts, annotator-labelled validation sets, identifier-only sampling frames, configuration, code and provenance. summary: This dataset provides the reported aggregate results, supplementary tables, figures and mathematical documentation supporting the manuscript “Genetic evaluation of growth and morphometric traits across ages in Peranakan Etawa goats”. The study analysed 49,162 measurements from 1,976 animals across 35 trait–age responses, using a pedigree comprising 2,819 individuals. Analyses included direct-only and common-dam animal models, within-age bivariate correlations, targeted joint models incorporating earlier measurements, descriptive birth-cohort profiles, and sensitivity analyses for flagged measurements. The deposit contains 16 CSV files reproducing the displayed numerical tables and normalized parameter/correlation records, 14 original embedded figure files, supplementary material, model equations, variable dictionaries, and reference post-processing utilities. The numerical values retain the rounding used in the source documents. Unavailable accepted estimates are explicitly distinguished from zero. This reporting release does not contain individual phenotypic records, pedigree rows, individual estimated breeding values, full-precision parameter covariance matrices, or the original DMU fitting pipeline. It therefore supports inspection and reuse of the reported results but does not permit independent reproduction of all REML estimates and standard errors. See the README for file descriptions, provenance and analytical limitations.

summary: This report was developed within seizmic – Scaling Social Entrepreneurship and Innovation: Zooming in on Multidisciplinary Interconnected Challenges, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network funded under Horizon Europe. It synthesises insights from four literature reviews conducted within Work Package 3, Impact Investing for Social Entrepreneurship Scaling, to provide a practical framework for understanding how impact investing can support the sustainable scaling of social enterprises. The report explores impact investing as a system of relationships involving investors, social enterprises, beneficiaries, intermediaries, and policymakers. It examines how investment objectives, financial instruments, governance arrangements, impact measurement practices, and ecosystem dynamics shape the ability of social enterprises to scale their social and environmental impact while preserving mission integrity. Drawing on complementary reviews of impact investing strategies, financing instruments, mission drift, governance, and ecosystem coordination, the report analyses how different forms of impact capital support three major scaling pathways: scaling up (systemic and policy change), scaling out (replication and expansion), and scaling deep (changes in values, norms, and community practices). Particular attention is given to the opportunities and challenges associated with instruments such as crowdfunding, venture philanthropy, social impact bonds, blended finance, development finance institution investments, and social venture capital. The report highlights the importance of aligning investor expectations, enterprise missions, governance structures, and impact measurement systems throughout the investment lifecycle. It identifies key risks, including mission drift, coordination failures, reporting burdens, and scaling-related challenges, while proposing practical safeguards and governance mechanisms to foster long-term mission fidelity and impact effectiveness. Based on this synthesis, the report offers actionable recommendations for investors, social enterprises, intermediaries, and policymakers. It argues that successful impact investing depends not only on the availability of capital, but also on the design of investment relationships, ecosystem infrastructure, and measurement practices that remain aligned with social purpose over time. By translating academic evidence into practitioner-oriented guidance, the report contributes to the development of a more effective and resilient European impact investing ecosystem.

summary: 中文書名 / Chinese Title: 自主城市微電網與能源共享極限 63/90 | PART III | STARLI RESEARCH INSTITUTE XXXVI English Title: AUTONOMOUS URBAN MICROGRIDS AND DISTRIBUTED ENERGY SHARING AT THE LIMIT Research Working Edition v1.0 | 1 November 2026 | Author: 33 / STARLI This prospective research working edition examines whether separately controlled district microgrids can exchange physically metered energy while preserving protected electrical services after a local fault. Its core three-coupling is Microgrids x Distributed Control x Energy Sharing. Studies are restricted to unoccupied scaled feeders, guarded controller hardware-in-the-loop, carefully bounded power interfaces and auditable digital-physical twins; the work claims neither city governance authority nor suitability for occupation. The preregistered main hypothesis asks whether distributed coordination improves state-of-charge estimation error against capable fixed-rule dispatch without worsening net lifecycle energy yield, when generation, storage, conductors, weather, labor, sensor resources and available forecast information are matched. Independent safety outcomes include loss-of-load duration, critical-load service, phase and voltage transients, physically measured frequency nadir and actual breaker isolation. The candidate swing model M domega/dt + D omega = Pm - Pe is treated as an operating-regime-limited frequency surrogate, not as a universal description of grid-following and grid-forming electronics. Withheld forecast shifts, islanding, battery thermal drift, network partitions, stale permissions and meter-reference biases provide explicit refutation tests. Its F02-anchored 777-page architecture comprises 14 scientific introductory pages, 30 differently purposed equation plates with units and blind rebuttals, 82 chapters with 410 separate one-page investigations, 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix proposals for distinct scientific instruments or evidence objects, plus seven closure pages. The 200 Gates pose prospective tests rather than completed laboratory results; the 33 Phoenix objects require independent prototypes and may fail their proposed qualifications. Each evidence line retains the full assigned denominator, rejected trials, metrology and a physical hard-stop code. External evidence includes An IoT-Based Framework for Distributed Generic Microgrid Controllers (10.1109/TCST.2024.3378989), Physical vulnerability-oriented reconfiguration of microgrids: centralized vs. decentralized control (10.1038/s41598-026-63123-9), the IEEE microgrid controller specification (10.1109/IEEESTD.2018.8340204), and Controller hardware-in-the-loop testing of multi-feeder hybrid control (10.1016/j.epsr.2026.113933; online 2026 with 2027 issue metadata). The FAIR data principles (10.1038/sdata.2016.18) inform independent reconstruction. summary: This record archives version 0.3.0 of takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg, research software for classifying prepared electrocardiogram (ECG) images as takotsubo syndrome or acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The source archive corresponds to GitHub tag v0.3.0 at commit 341ac955353f535fb74a4b6d8005a8b3b1290ad4. The repository includes retained model-development and evaluation sources, an inference command-line interface, an English Google Colab example, and optional Grad-CAM output for ViT and ConvNeXtV2. It supports ViT, ConvNeXtV2 and MLP-Mixer predictions and their three-model ensemble. Trained model weights are distributed separately as weight release v0.2.0. The default inference input is an already prepared 480 x 480 pixel image. Supported single-frame formats are PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF and WebP; the loader converts images to RGB. Other dimensions are rejected unless the explicit resize option is selected. Resizing alone does not reproduce the study's upstream ECG preparation. Patient ECG images, training datasets and participant records are not included. Paper-default test-time augmentation (TTA) uses 24 views with magnitude 1 for ViT, one unchanged view (no TTA) for ConvNeXtV2, and 32 views with magnitude 3 for MLP-Mixer. View counts include the unchanged image. Raw logits are averaged across each model's views, followed by an equal-weight mean of the three models' raw logits and softmax. Class order is tako, AMI; AMI denotes the acute anterior STEMI comparison group. Defaults include float32 precision, seed 1234, batch size 1 and four workers. TTA results can depend on the execution environment and data-loading configuration. Grad-CAM maps use a separate unaugmented float32 pass for each visualized model. By default, each map targets that model's TTA-logit argmax. These are not attributions of the three-model ensemble or the full TTA average. No MLP-Mixer or ensemble heatmap is provided. Historical reader-study heatmap equivalence has not been established. Validation includes a ten-image float32/no-TTA comparison for the v0.2.1 inference baseline, within the documented numerical tolerance with no class changes. Earlier paired CPU and WSL checks of the Grad-CAM candidate confirmed exactly unchanged predictions when Grad-CAM was enabled. On 24 October 2026, the published v0.3.0 Colab workflow completed paper-TTA inference and Grad-CAM on one generated image using an NVIDIA A100, Python 3.13.16 and CUDA float32. Recorded source and weight identities, prediction calculations, both finite maps and downloaded artifacts were verified. That Colab run did not include a paired Grad-CAM-off comparison. Synthetic execution checks do not establish clinical performance; full training, all-dataset evaluation and human-study runtime reproduction remain outside the verified scope. The archived tag is unchanged. The later documentation-only update at commit f8553b994cc8f3ac99c5e7e3ed44cea312dde512 records the completed validation. See the dated implementation status (https://github.com/ekagawa007/takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg/blob/f8553b994cc8f3ac99c5e7e3ed44cea312dde512/docs/implementation_status.md) and Grad-CAM methods and limitations (https://github.com/ekagawa007/takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg/blob/f8553b994cc8f3ac99c5e7e3ed44cea312dde512/docs/gradcam.md). The source code is distributed under the MIT License, copyright 2026 Eisuke Kagawa. The model weights have separate terms. These materials are intended for research; no warranty is given regarding clinical accuracy, reliability or fitness for clinical use. Warranty exclusions and liability limitations, including consequences of use in diagnosis or treatment decisions, are governed by the applicable code and model-weight licenses. Source release: v0.3.0 (https://github.com/ekagawa007/takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg/releases/tag/v0.3.0). Companion weight release: v0.2.0 (https://github.com/ekagawa007/takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg/releases/tag/v0.2.0).

summary: EXTERNAL QIGONG AND HUMAN THERMAL RADIATION PATTERNS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English research working monograph investigating whether thermographic differences observed during culturally defined qigong and matched neutral tasks can be distinguished from ordinary human thermoregulation, environmental exchange and measurement bias. The governing three-coupling is infrared thermal imaging x physiological regulation x heat-transfer models. The research treats “external qi” as a cultural and experimental task label, not an established physical energy carrier. The scientific core separates raw infrared radiance from inferred skin temperature and estimated heat flux. It develops emissivity and reflected-wall correction, blackbody calibration, spectral detector response, conduction and perfusion bioheat models, convection, evaporation, respiration-related temperature patterns, posture and muscular activity. The original candidate bulk heat equation is explicitly refined by separating volumetric tissue transport from surface heat-transfer boundary conditions. The principal proposed test uses concealed task assignments, matched breathing/movement/clothing, phantom references, negative-control regions and conventional physics-first rivals. Thirty physically distinct mathematical plates document governing relationships, units, assumptions, identifiability, masked falsifiers and chapter links. Eighty-two independent research chapters contain 410 single-page investigations. The true center of the monograph is its 200 one-page Research Gates, each posing a falsifiable question in bold deep-navy typography and asking what an independent successor must measure, challenge, disprove or preserve. Thirty-three differentiated Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future instruments, error-correction artifacts, negative-result protocols and reproducibility tools. The DOI registry separates three STARLI author mother volumes from eleven externally published methodological or conventional-science references on infrared thermography, emissivity, classical bioheat and research design. Bibliographic sources constrain methods; they do not validate extraordinary qigong mechanisms. Every integrated experiment is prospective. The book presents no completed human intervention, clinically established effect, new physical particle or evidence of treatment efficacy. Ethical authorization and independent scientific review would be required before future human-observation research. Author: 33 | STARLI White Rainbow Epoch Series: STARLI Research Institute XXXIII | Flagship 38 of 90
