summary: ENERGY DISTRIBUTION IN INTELLIGENT ROBOTIC MATTER AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:智能機器人物質能源分配極限 21/90 ENERGY DISTRIBUTION IN INTELLIGENT ROBOTIC MATTER AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition of STARLI's YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy, asking whether twenty-four locally controlled robotic-matter modules can share a bounded energy supply for a fixed, verified vehicle-body reconfiguration task without concealing external work, structural risk or unsafe communication delays. The three-coupling is Energy Networks x Distributed Power Supply x Vehicle Reconfiguration. Tests are restricted to unoccupied, scaled hardware, traceable electrical rails and laboratory/hardware-in-the-loop environments; no completed roadworthy or nanorobotic supercar is claimed. The falsifiable hypothesis is that a pre-registered distributed allocator can reduce total mission joules at the same useful task, material mass, sensing quality, energy sources, cooling, computation, time and operator budget as a properly optimized wired centralized architecture, while not worsening critical command latency. A hidden unmetered driver, local thermal hotspot, power-rail partition, stale packets, reserve deficit or failure of physical stopping defeats the claim. The supplied consensus model, dx_i/dt = -sum_j a_ij(x_i-x_j)+w_i, is used to study local agreement; agreement alone cannot prove charge conservation, battery state of charge or safe power distribution. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates examine energy-balance and signed-work integration, nodal current conservation, converter and contact losses, motor work, SOC integration and transient terminal voltage, resistor networks, rated-edge loading, droop sharing, negative incremental impedance, spectral connectivity, packet age, deadline reliability, thermal RC and Joule heating, dependent hazards, stop-energy reserve, constrained dispatch, worst-node tail risk, covariance propagation and physical safe-stop latency. Each plate provides mathematical or physical construction, dimensional limits, an individually specified blind challenge and chapter references. Across eighty-two chapters and 410 single-page investigations, the research program spans power-source custody, reconfigurable conductors, communication and consensus, electrothermal safety, fault isolation and independent qualification. Two hundred Research Gates pose distinct concealed-fault, equal-resource competitor and cross-interface problems with separate challenge, rival and stopping explanations. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose experimental meters, isolation benches, duty referees, communication-energy witnesses, thermal artifacts and second-laboratory transfer contracts. These are hypothesis-forming research proposals, not completed devices or demonstrated physical outcomes. The DOI ancestry preserves author-supplied parent identifiers 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 (metadata not independently confirmed). External component and methodology references include Robo-Matter (10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6), flying-swarm shape assembly (10.1038/s44172-026-00715-3), adaptive magnetic microrobots (10.1038/s41427-026-00682-3), changing-topology consensus (10.1109/TAC.2005.846556), distributed power sharing (10.1109/TPWRD.2012.2212919), energy-aware multi-robot allocation (10.1016/j.robot.2024.104762), and wireless robotic power transfer (10.1049/csy2.70065). These studies support limited component analogies and methods; none proves the integrated F21 vehicle-body architecture, passenger safety or nanoscale-to-macroscopic feasibility. summary: Welcome to WARP WARP (WDL Analysis Research Pipelines) repository is a collection of cloud-optimized pipelines for processing biological data from the Broad Institute Data Sciences Platform and collaborators. The contents of this repository are open source and released under the BSD 3-Clause license . You can count on WARP for rigorously scientifically validated, high scale, reproducible and open source pipelines. Our pipelines are written as "workflows" using the Workflow Description Language (WDL) and they process a broad spectrum of "omic" and array-related datasets (see the overview table below). | Pipeline Category | Data Types | | --- | --- | | Germline Variant Discovery | Genomes, Exomes | | Genotyping Arrays | Variant discovery, Chip validation, Joint array analysis | | Single-cell/nuclei Transcriptomics | Droplet based (10x Genomics), Smartseq2 | | Single-cell Epigenomics | Single nuclei ATAC-seq, Single nuclei MethylC-seq | | Joint Genotyping | Genomes, Exomes | | Somatic Alignment (beta) | Exomes | Try our pipelines in Terra , a platform for collaborative cloud analysis! Learn how in the Using WARP section. Navigating WARP All versioned and released pipelines are in one of the three pipelines subdirectories: broad (pipelines for the Broad Institute's Genomics Platform), cemba (pipelines for the BRAIN Initiative) or skylab (pipelines for the Human Cell Atlas Project). Each pipeline directory hosts a main workflow WDL that includes a pipeline version number and a corresponding changelog file. Workflows may call additional WDLs, referred to as tasks, that are located in the tasks directory. Pipelines that are in progress or have not yet been validated are in the beta-pipelines folder. Using WARP There are three ways to use WARP pipelines: 1. Download the workflow and run on a WDL-compatible execution engine WDL workflows run on multiple systems, including Cromwell , miniWDL , and dxWDL (see the openwdl documentation ). To run a pipeline's latest release, first navigate to WARP Releases , search for your pipeline's tag, and download the pipeline's assets (the WDL workflow, the JSON, and the ZIP with accompanying dependencies; see Optimus example below). You can also access a pipeline's release page by selecting the pipeline version number at the top of the pipeline's README. After downloading the pipeline's assets, launch the workflow following your execution engine's instructions. 2. These workspaces include both the WDL workflow and downsampled data so that you can test the pipeline at low-cost. If you are new to Terra, you can get started by registering with your Google account and visiting Terra Support . After registration, search for WARP-related workspaces with the "warp-pipelines" tag. To test the pipeline, clone (make a copy of) the workspace following the instructions in this Terra Support guide . 3. To view all available pipelines, just search "warp" in the Dockstore search and browse the workflow list. See Dockstore documentation for details on launching the workflow. summary: Real Analysis Volume 1: Foundations of Real Analysis , authored by Helbert Justo Luque Zevallos and published by Proyecto Ágora as part of the Undergraduate Mathematics Series , is a university-level academic textbook devoted to the logical, algebraic, and axiomatic foundations of real analysis. The book provides a systematic and rigorous introduction to mathematical reasoning, formal proof techniques, and the fundamental structure of the real number system. Its primary objective is to develop the conceptual understanding and mathematical maturity required for advanced undergraduate studies in mathematical analysis. Chapter 1: Mathematical Language and Proof Techniques This chapter introduces propositional logic, logical connectives, truth tables, implications, equivalences, universal and existential quantifiers, and the negation of quantified statements. It develops the theory of sets, equivalence and order relations, injective, surjective, and bijective functions, images, preimages, composition, and inverse functions. Particular emphasis is placed on direct proof, proof by contraposition, proof by contradiction, mathematical induction, and the construction of counterexamples. The chapter also examines rigorous mathematical writing, common logical errors, finite and infinite sets, countability, and the uncountability of the real numbers. Chapter 2: The Real Number System The second chapter develops the axiomatic structure of the real numbers through field axioms, order axioms, and the compatibility of algebraic operations with order. It examines absolute value, the triangle inequality, fundamental inequalities, intervals, neighborhoods, upper and lower bounds, suprema, infima, maxima, and minima. A central component is the completeness property of the real numbers , including the structural distinction between rational and real numbers, the Archimedean property, the density of rational and irrational numbers, and the nested interval theorem. The chapter concludes with significant consequences of completeness, including the existence of roots, rational approximations, the supremum principle as a mathematical proof technique, and the relationship between completeness and convergence. Pedagogical Approach The textbook integrates precise definitions, propositions, lemmas, theorems, complete mathematical proofs, explanatory examples, and carefully constructed counterexamples. It includes 120 fully solved exercises and 150 proposed exercises , organized according to the main topics of the two chapters. These activities reinforce theoretical understanding, logical reasoning, mathematical writing, and independent problem-solving skills. Intended Audience This publication is intended for undergraduate mathematics students, university instructors, mathematics educators, and independent learners seeking a rigorous foundation in real analysis. As the first volume of a six-volume academic collection, it establishes the theoretical and methodological foundations for subsequent studies of sequences, numerical series, limits, continuity, metric spaces, compactness, differential calculus, Riemann integration, uniform convergence, and differential equations. summary: v2.4.1 (2026-10-31) replaces the age-only standardization of v2.4.0 by indirect standardization over 16 sex-by-age strata (KDCA district-by-sex-by-age-band notifications and resident-registration population by district, sex and age band); all arms, threshold refits and figures were rerun and the credible set is unchanged (fiscal independence only). v2.4.0 (revision R1, 2026-10-31) adds revision_R1/: the additional analyses requested at peer review by JMIR Public Health and Surveillance (indirectly age-standardized expected counts as offset; every count or area covariate re-expressed as a share of district land area, a rate per 1000 residents or a density per km2, with log population density added; two uniform functional forms; parsimonious models; restricted spatial regression; zero-inflated negative binomial; residual Moran's I for every specification; 8 neighbourhood graphs; spatially varying coefficients for forest share and household wells; physicians per 1000 as ascertainment proxy; 2022-2024 only; repeated fits; reruns of the complete data pipeline under alternative screening thresholds and with linear interpolation), all outputs, the revised figures, and the inputs needed beyond the raw files. Under the revised principal model only fiscal independence remains credible (IRR 0.890, 95% CrI 0.819-0.966 per SD); the four other associations of the reviewed version survive age standardization alone but not rescaling, and forest share is credible under no revised specification. Three input corrections (Busanjin-gu and Cheonan-si land-use and well values; boundary-file area in place of the sewerage area field; Incheon Michuhol-gu/Namdong-gu polygon assignment) are documented; the reviewed specification refitted on the corrected inputs reproduces its 5 associations. The main script and results/ (v2.3.3, the reviewed analysis) are unchanged. Earlier history: Reproducibility package for a Bayesian spatiotemporal analysis of district-level hepatitis A incidence in South Korea, 2020-2024 (negative binomial, Besag-York-Mollie convolution + RW1 + Knorr-Held Type I interaction, fitted with R-INLA; 219 districts, 1,095 district-years, 27 covariates). v2.1.0 is a DATA-REPAIR release that supersedes all earlier versions: an audit found that several administrative source files store unavailable values as 0 instead of missing and that some series were redefined in particular years, so that, under binary and quantile coding, covariates encoded data availability rather than their true level. These values are now recoded as missing and filled from the most recent earlier available year, and every change is logged (results/data_repair_log.csv). The v2.0.x associations for piped water-supply coverage and inpatient medical cost, and the v2.0.x claim of nine credible covariates, were artefacts of this defect and are withdrawn. The repaired analysis found four credible covariates (household groundwater wells, dairy-cattle farms, forest area, fiscal independence). A post hoc extreme-value screen then found aggregation errors (eg, a sex ratio near 50 males per 100 females, basic livelihood security recipients above 30%, mostly in cities with non-autonomous wards) affecting 17 district-years in 4 covariates; v2.2.0 adopts this screen as rule R7 of the principal analysis, which excludes 2 further districts (218 districts, 1,090 district-years) and adds sewer-pipe repair sites as a fifth credible covariate. Household groundwater wells and sewer-pipe repair sites are borderline (lost under some neighbourhood graphs, INLA settings or the alternative handling of extreme values), and only forest area is credible in every sensitivity analysis; dairy-cattle farms, sewer-pipe repair sites and fiscal independence are lost when 2020-2021 is excluded. The covariates take up only part of the spatial structure (residual Moran's I +0.22). The package contains a single R script (data repair, models, sensitivity and stability analyses), a figure script, a year-R2 data
title: Spatial Clustering of Hepatitis A in South Korea, 2020-2024: Nationwide Bayesian Analysis of Socioeconomic Gradients and Residual Clustering After Age Standardization (analysis code, data-repair log and compiled data, v2.4.1)

This is a prospective, non-occupancy research program for instrumented material coupons, unoccupied modular bodies and hardware-in-the-loop experiments, not evidence of self-manufacturing roadworthy vehicles. Its falsifiable candidate requires a pre-registered design-evolution method, under the same total material, energy, sensor, computing, operator and testing budgets as capable fixed and classical redesign baselines, to improve independently reproducible successor handoff success without worsening actual structural safety, identity continuity or the complete-denominator rate of severe failures. It asks whether the identity of a morphing modular vehicle can remain independently reconstructable after authorized component replacement without confusing a valid digital registration with preserved load-bearing structure. The three-way research coupling is Digital Identity x Structural Evolution x Traceability. The scope is unoccupied scaled panels, instrumented materials and hardware-in-the-loop studies; no working road vehicle, human safety certification or legal identity status is claimed. The falsifiable research contract compares a frozen physical-and-digital provenance architecture against conventional fleet records, competent expert inspection and signed digital-twin workflows under equal material, sensor, energy, computing, time and labor budgets. Its principal target is fewer unsafe identity counterexamples without worse independent handoff and replay completeness. Sealed challenges include cloned credentials, unlogged load-bearing module replacements, mismatched software epochs, shared sensor drift, missing repair history and physical specimens exchanged after shipping. Every refused or incomplete case remains in the denominator. Authentication, a consistent twin model and traceable physical load are independent requirements. Thirty mechanism-distinct mathematical plates examine Bayesian identity inference, physical genealogy and typed attachment graphs, critical replacement fractions, physical capacity margins, event causal order, cryptographic integrity and its limits, revocation freshness, observable configuration states, calibrated innovation statistics, shared covariance, hidden change detection, dangerous false-clear risk, complete release conjunctions and cross-laboratory identity handoffs. summary: This article examines how customs authorities can shorten clearance times without reducing the detection of violations by redistributing fixed inspection capacity across risk lanes. The empirical basis is a declaration-level dataset from the Customs Committee of Uzbekistan, comprising 8,000 declarations lodged at 12 customs posts during 2023–2026. A log-logistic accelerated failure time model shows that assignment to the red lane multiplies expected clearance time by 2.97, while pre-arrival lodging reduces it by 29.7%. A linear programming model is proposed to rank declarations by the number of detected violations per hour of additional clearance time. With the same 1,820 inspections and 786 detected violations, the model reduces the 90th percentile of clearance time by 21.3 minutes and by 64.2 minutes when combined with an increased share of pre-arrival declarations.

summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.

summary: This repository provides the MATLAB source code and reproducibility resources associated with the manuscript entitled “Physics-Guided Reduced-Order Screening of Radiative Loss, Preferential Diffusion, and NOₓ Pathway Competition in Ammonia/Hydrogen Diffusion Flames,” submitted to the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy (Manuscript No. HE-D-26-13275). The computational framework employs a two-dimensional axisymmetric, physics-guided reduced-order model to investigate the coupled effects of radiative heat loss, preferential diffusion, ammonia cracking, hydrogen enrichment, pressure, and strain on non-premixed ammonia/hydrogen diffusion flames. The MATLAB implementation supports the reproduction of the manuscript's numerical analyses, including baseline flame characteristics, reaction-zone localization, thermal response, relative NOₓ formation tendencies, scalar dissipation, extinction susceptibility, robustness indicators, mechanism-isolation studies, numerical convergence, closure sensitivity, uncertainty analyses, parametric sweeps, and Pareto-based screening. Repository contents and reproducibility The principal file, Master_NH3H2_ROM_Reproducibility.m , contains the model formulation, numerical procedures, analysis modules, and routines for generating supporting figures, numerical tables, and datasets. Executing the master function creates an organized output directory containing the enabled computational results. Model scope and limitations The framework is intended for comparative mechanism screening and prioritization of operating conditions for subsequent higher-fidelity investigations. It does not solve the full governing conservation equations or detailed chemical kinetics. The relative NOₓ formation-tendency index is not an absolute emission concentration, emission factor, or outlet flux. Similarly, the extinction and robustness indicators represent comparative screening metrics rather than experimentally validated stability limits. The repository supports transparency, reproducibility, and further development of computational screening methods for ammonia/hydrogen combustion. Associated manuscript: International Journal of Hydrogen Energy, HE-D-26-13275. Keywords: Ammonia/hydrogen combustion; reduced-order modeling; MATLAB; radiative heat loss; preferential diffusion; NOₓ formation tendency; extinction; uncertainty analysis; reproducibility.

summary: An institution's directives may in fact serve its recipients' reasons, as Raz's Normal Justification Thesis requires, while the institution lacks standing to insist that recipients forgo their own checks. This article separates objective authority from that entitlement. For continuing, consequential, and contestable directives, the entitlement depends on two substantiated presuppositions of the demand: that deference is worthwhile for the recipient's reference class, with a route for individual rebuttal, and that the exposure to error it creates is correctable at the scale of issuance. Given a justified directive role and a decision not reserved to the recipient's own judgment, the two are jointly sufficient. Serviceability is operationalized by a Scale-Indexed Serviceability test applied to a specified mechanism, lawful architecture, horizon, issuance scale, and claim mix. Failure to substantiate withholds the entitlement; a certified absence of any feasible plan defeats it and requires affected adverse issuance, or its effect, to be restricted to what can be serviced. Neither status invalidates lawful acts. Two consequences follow: a Wide-Scope Duty of Sustainable Issuance binds the bodies controlling scale and capacity, and Deontic Debt preserves directed claims when due obligations are deficiently serviced, even where incapacity is excused. A stipulated benefits administration shows each status at work. It reproduces the baseline waiting times and checks the defeat, withholding, and recovery scenarios. Python 3 standard library only; run with python3 halden_schedule_check.py . Related work. (2026), The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority , Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23272655 .

summary: Learned surrogates of process simulators are often evaluated on random states from plants they have already seen. This technical report compares interpolation, leave-one-case-out, and leave-one-ore-group-out evaluation for five models trained on a steady-state mineral-processing simulator. The simulator tracks mineral mass over 63 size classes, water, closed grinding circuits, and unit-level balance closure. It reports limitations against published examples alongside the comparisons. On a 3,072-state design over twelve authored cases, the multilayer perceptron gives the lowest interpolation recovery RMSE (3.38 percentage points), but has a 26.24-point mean RMSE when each case is held out. The Gaussian process has the lowest mean held-out-case RMSE (10.95 points), while the perceptron has the highest median case-fold R-squared (0.547). Under ore-group holdout, the perceptron's median recovery R-squared is 0.437 across seven groups, but varies from 0.795 for the five chalcopyrite cases to -10.2 for the two gold-in-pyrite cases. Log-upgrade transfer is poor for every model. The cases are authored; these results do not establish performance on operating plants. The report documents the mineral-processing simulator, its physical models, machine-learning evaluation methods, a process-specific optimization study, data and preprocessing, validation protocols, limitations, and reproducibility. Source code and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_OreFlow

summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
title: DinHot: A Holographic Optical Trap Studio Comparing Hologram Methods on a Device Model

summary: This archive reproduces every table and figure in Onodje, P. and Adekoya, O., 'Administered farmgate prices and the cross-border leakage of cocoa: evidence from mirror trade statistics in West Africa'. The paper relates importer-reported (mirror) imports of cocoa beans (HS 1801) from Togo, Liberia and Guinea to the gap between the world cocoa price and the farmgate prices fixed by the marketing boards of Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire, 2012 to 2026. The package contains Python scripts for data download, estimation and figures; a hand-compiled record of 40 farmgate price announcements (2015/16 to 2026/27) with a source for each; openly licensed price, exchange rate and FAOSTAT production data; aggregated outlet-level trade series with SHA-256 checksums of the raw files; all outputs; and a dated, hashed prediction file that pre-specifies a held-out test for June to December 2026. UN Comtrade terms of use do not permit redistribution of the trade records, so the archive provides aggregated series that reproduce the headline estimates; the download script retrieves the underlying records with a free UN Comtrade subscription key. Code is released under the MIT licence; data compiled by the authors and outputs under CC BY 4.0. See README.md for instructions.
title: Replication package for 'Administered farmgate prices and the cross-border leakage of cocoa: evidence from mirror trade statistics in West Africa'

summary: An authentic group of pre-Columbian ceramics, probably from Risaralda, appears to rhyme with Japan's 5,000-year-old Jōmon Venus. The resemblance is real; a historical connection is not. This GLIAG essay shows how two distant societies independently turned clay and the human body into instruments of memory, identity and ritual, and why archaeological context determines what we can responsibly know. The Japanese comparator is identified securely: the 27 cm, 2.14 kg clay dogū known as the Jōmon Venus, recovered intact at the Tanabatake site in Chino, Nagano, and dated by the responsible museum to the Middle Jōmon, about 3000 BCE. The Colombian objects are, on their custodian's account, authentic, Colombian and probably from Risaralda, reportedly recovered by guaqueros; their context, ceramic phase and date are undocumented. The essay sets out a disciplined visual comparison across eight analytical axes, discusses the body as vessel, gender and fertility, convergence without contact, and guaquería as knowledge loss, and closes with a research programme for the Risaralda objects. Nothing in it demonstrates trans-Pacific contact; the strongest explanation is convergent figuration. Bilingual edition, English then Spanish. This Zenodo edition (Revision 2.1, 31 October 2026) reproduces the web edition first published on Petroleum & Energy Insights on 13 September 2026 (GLIAG-ESS-2026-038-CH REV 002), with an amendment register, full references, licence and citation. Figure 1 of the web edition (two source images) is not reproduced for rights reasons. The essay is not an appraisal, title opinion or authentication of any object.
title: Two Worlds, One Human Form: the Jōmon Venus of Japan and anthropomorphic ceramics from Cauca Medio, Colombia

summary: Next Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) requires the integration of increasingly heterogeneous evidence from New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), computational models, chemical information, biological mechanisms and exposure assessment. RISK-HUNT3R WP9 has addressed a fundamental challenge for this transition: how to organise, connect and reuse diverse scientific information so that it can support transparent, reproducible and human-relevant safety assessment. The RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure provides a FAIR-oriented digital environment for managing and connecting experimental data, methods, compounds, computational resources and mechanistic knowledge. Its architecture combines harmonised data and metadata templates, controlled vocabularies and ontologies, compound and methods databases, BioStudies and EdelweissData integration, knowledge graphs, computational tools, AI assistance resources and cloud-based services. Together these resources support the progression from data capture and curation to analysis, mechanistic interpretation and evidence integration. The infrastructure has been deployed across distributed project partners to support collaborative research and reuse of RISK-HUNT3R and legacy EU-ToxRisk resources. A central principle emerging from this work is that effective NGRA infrastructure must support more than FAIR data. Methods, models, workflows, provenance, applicability and uncertainty also need to be captured so that scientific results can be interpreted within their Context of Use and assembled into evidence supporting a decision. Resources including ToxTemp, compound and methods databases, knowledge graphs, EdelweissData and ASPA-based workflows provide complementary components of this evolving evidence architecture. The resulting infrastructure provides both an operational resource for RISK-HUNT3R and a foundation for future development. By connecting data, methods, models and mechanistic knowledge through interoperable digital resources, RISK-HUNT3R demonstrates a pathway from fragmented NAM outputs towards reusable evidence workflows supporting transparent NGRA.
title: From NAM Data to Trusted Evidence: RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure for Next Generation Risk Assessment

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. Assurance boundary: written proofs; floating-point numerical checks and Kepler simulations; producer-side replay in normal and optimised modes; internal AI-assisted review (five roles, adversarial correctness review, proof audit and re-review). This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.

summary: 智能奈米機器人自主建築修復極限 41/90 INTELLIGENT NANOROBOTIC AUTONOMOUS ARCHITECTURAL REPAIR AT THE LIMIT INTELLIGENT NANOROBOTIC AUTONOMOUS ARCHITECTURAL REPAIR AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 41 of 90). It investigates whether locally operated micro-scale robotic inspection and repair methods might detect concealed cracks, moisture ingress, damaged mechanical interfaces and environmental faults, then restore independently measurable properties without concealing failure. The core coupling is Micro/Nano Sensing x Local Repair x Structural Reliability. Every proposed integrated test is limited to unoccupied scaled habitat panels, damaged coupons, environmental chambers and supervised hardware-in-the-loop systems; no inhabited dwelling, nanorobotic building maintenance system or structural certification is claimed. The falsifiable candidate predicts higher independently verified fault recall without worsening preregistered post-repair air-quality recovery under equal inspection exposure, material supply, energy, sensing, computation, time and human-operations budgets. Repair success is separately conditional on load-path requalification, credible reference identity, moisture containment and a functioning physical stop. A controlled localized robotic repair system must compete with scheduled expert inspection, replace-on-failure maintenance and expert-performed local treatment. Concealed moisture, common-mode sensor drift, inaccessible crack ligaments, incompatible repair chemistry and hidden support fixtures are ways the hypothesis can fail. Negative specimens, refused states, destructive tests and incomplete repairs remain in the full denominator. Thirty mechanically and statistically distinct research plates include Paris-regime fatigue crack growth, mode-I and mixed-mode fracture, energy release, cohesive-interface work, load balance, fatigue survival, detection recall and false clearance, ultrasound and acoustic observability, thermal and moisture transport, contaminant mass balance, resin flow, cure kinetics, correlated uncertainty, materials and energy accounting, conditional causal effects and physically verified stop latency. Each mathematical plate states its mechanism, dimensional assumptions, independent reference, blinded contradiction and research-chapter links. The seed Paris relation da/dN = C(Delta K)^m is a conditional empirical model for particular fatigue regimes, not a universal law of repair or evidence that a crack has healed. Eighty-two chapters and 410 single-page investigations examine specimen provenance, hidden crack truth, fracture and fatigue, imaging and sensor drift, repair-material chemistry, robotic deposition, wall-module utility boundaries, environmental requalification, long-cycle maintenance and independent laboratory reconstruction. Two hundred individually worded Research Gates challenge different physical witnesses, resource-matched rivals, coupled faults, false-clear decisions and reproducibility limits. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separate future scientific objects, including fracture-reference capsules, moisture witnesses, cure validation rigs, aerosol exposure ledgers, physical interlocks and cross-site specimen relays. These are research proposals and evidence contracts, not demonstrated autonomous repair devices. The research is hypothetical, non-occupancy and intentionally vulnerable to refutation. Existing studies establish bounded robotic crack inspection and concrete sealing methods, polymer-glass simulation mechanisms, fatigue testing practices and material measurement approaches, but do not validate the integrated F41 architecture. Relevant external literature includes Li et al. (2026), DOI 10.1038/s44172-026-00637-0; Ruiz-Franco and Giuntoli (2025), DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-59426-6; Huang et al. (2026), DOI 10.1016/j.autcon.2026.107006; Chen et al. (2022), DOI 10.1

summary: This repository contains the data, Python code and supporting computational material accompanying the article “Auditing life-cycle loss comparisons for seismic retrofit: a traceable stone-masonry case study.” The package supports the reproducible examination of historical life-cycle loss calculations for a stone-masonry building and alternative strengthening interventions. It provides traceability between source-reported quantities, calculation assumptions, recalculated results and the numerical figures and tables presented in the article. The archive includes: A source-data register with source-page references, provenance classifications and uncertainty notes. Python scripts reproducing the historical arithmetic and reconciling 22 reported loss values. Numerical datasets, figures and tables supporting the article. An independent loss-assessment engine and its synthetic test suite, kept separate from the historical reproduction workflow. Execution instructions, dependency versions, verification logs and file checksums. The reconciliation identifies 17 of 22 reported values within the tolerance bands obtained by propagating the stated precision of the fitted parameters ; five values fall outside those bands. summary: AnaTele is an open-source desktop tool for investigating ArduPilot flight logs (.tlog, .bin, .log). It infers flight phases, replays the recorded path in 3D, evaluates a versioned declarative rule pack with four explicit result states, and ranks competing failure hypotheses by capped evidence-family support minus contradictions, without assigning probabilities. Every finding links to the exact log record. It includes a fault-injection quadcopter simulator and a hash-verified shareable analysis format (.ant). Documentation: avinashistoocool.github.io/AnaTele
title: AnaTele: evidence-first investigation of ArduPilot flight logs

summary: CIRCULAR MATERIAL ECONOMIES FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE CITIES AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:移動城市循環經濟與材料永續極限 55/90 CIRCULAR MATERIAL ECONOMIES FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE CITIES AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 55 of 90). It investigates whether a deliberately unoccupied six-module mobile-city research system can reduce relocation-related material loss through qualified reuse, automated selective disassembly and auditable remanufacturing, while preserving deployment latency and critical-service safety. The three-way research coupling is Circular Materials x Autonomous Manufacturing x Urban Sustainability. Neither a functioning autonomous city nor a human-occupied habitat is asserted. The falsifiable proposal compares a frozen circular material strategy against competent conventional manual recovery, replacement and stationary emergency infrastructure under equal material, energy, sensing, technician-hour, tool, water and transport budgets. Original intake, declined parts, work in progress, consumed adhesives, repeated repairs, rejected batches and retired material remain in the denominator. Blind faults include grade swaps, hidden fatigue, wrong material passports, replayed scale measurements, contamination, source-energy omissions and optimistic virgin-substitution credits. A proposal fails whenever a load-bearing component, utility service, waste route, safety interlock or material identity cannot be independently reconstructed. Thirty mechanism-distinct research formula plates address mass custody, qualified yield, bond separation work, fatigue, polymer rheology, sensor residuals, covariance, electrical energy, verified lifecycle inventory, carbon-allocation sensitivity, replacement counterfactuals, tail risk, second-site reproduction and noncompensatory physical release. The original contract's cyber-physical residual r_k = y_k - yhat_k(x_k,u_k) is retained as one fault-detection method; it is not treated as a law of circularity or sustainability. Every mathematical plate states units, validity assumptions, a blinded counterexample and scientific chapter interfaces. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated research studies and 200 Research Gates, each connected to a specified material state, independent reference, fault or competing process. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose research instruments, material-qualification fixtures, provenance devices, circularity accounting tools and successor-ready evidence protocols. This work proposes hypotheses and reproducibility obligations, not physical trial outcomes. Its complete PDF also contains research limits, negative-result custody and second-laboratory transfer requirements. The scope remains prospective, scaled and non-occupancy. Environmental performance requires functional-unit parity and a complete lifecycle inventory; increasing recovered mass alone does not prove lower environmental burden. Relevant method references include Ostapska et al. (10.1016/j.spc.2024.05.014), Formentini et al. (10.1016/j.jclepro.2025.145459), Attia et al. (10.1016/j.autcon.2024.105521), Mao and Cao (10.1016/j.spc.2024.12.021), Poschmann et al. (10.1002/cite.201900107) and Keating et al. (10.1126/scirobotics.aam8986). The Flagship 13 mother genealogy identifiers (10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839) were provided by the author and their metadata have not been independently confirmed. summary: This package contains the code that produces every table and figure quoted in the paper "The Widening Mathematics Gap: Boys, Girls and Who Is Missing from PISA. 38 OECD Countries, 2015–2025", the small public inputs it needs (population and coverage tables), and the country-level results behind every OECD average. PISA microdata are not redistributed; they are public and must be downloaded from the OECD (see README). Code comments and docstrings are in Spanish; the README documents the pipeline in English. Version 2 (31 October 2026) adds code/53_revision_v18.py (inference for the trend bounds of Table 5: bias correction of country-specific extrema, coverage simulation, Stoye intervals) and replaces the supplement PDF with version v19. Scripts 01–38 and data files S1–S13 are unchanged.
title: Replication package: The Widening Mathematics Gap — Boys, Girls and Who Is Missing from PISA

summary: LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:可變形移動居住系統長期宜居性極限 56/90 LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 56 of 90). It investigates whether a traceable unoccupied morphing habitat testbed can improve the joint coverage of measured thermal, airflow, moisture, energy and structural engineering envelopes across controlled seasonal sequences while preserving independently reconstructable module identity. Its core coupling is Human-Comfort Proxy Models x Environmental Control x Longitudinal Test Evidence. The project uses guarded coupons, scaled modules, environmental chambers, inert-water and tracer-air circuits, and hardware-in-the-loop tests; it does not observe residents or establish an occupancy certificate. The preregisterable hypothesis is that, under matched materials, energy reserves, maintenance, sensor access, control computation and test time, a frozen morphing environmental-control policy will improve complete-cohort comfort-envelope proxy coverage without worsening module-identity continuity relative to competent static-habitat and expert manual-reconfiguration baselines. The supplied selective-risk candidate R_sel(tau)=E[L(yhat,y)|c>=tau] must be published with accepted coverage, so a low risk score cannot be purchased by refusing nearly every difficult climate or aging case. Hidden trials vary aging gaskets, radiant asymmetry, tracer-air pockets, power outages, sensor common-mode drift, broken connectors, incorrect material identity and ineffective physical stop contacts. Thirty mechanism-specific mathematical plates analyze heat balance, conductive and radiant transfer, operative temperature proxies, vapor mass and dew-point margins, air exchange, ventilation pressure, energy and water closure, sound, light, fatigue, reliability, stale information, uncertainty covariance, selective-risk coverage, tail excursions and second-site reconstruction. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated investigations spanning material aging, climate control, indoor-environment proxy limitations, repair, operator authority and versioned evidence. Two hundred Research Gates formulate disconfirmable experimental questions across concealed faults, equal-resource comparisons and two-mechanism interfaces. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separately falsifiable future rigs, calibration artifacts, safe-stop witnesses and successor evidence packages. The volume is a prospective research design rather than a completed experimental study. An unoccupied thermal or tracer-gas rig cannot establish human comfort, healthy air, habitable water, fire and structural compliance, actual multiyear life, or a right to place people inside a mobile dwelling. The 777-page layout and enumerated items are structurally checked, but a language-duplication audit finds reused long editorial method spans; semantic uniqueness, physical modeling and all evidence inferences remain subject to deeper independent review. Relevant independently identified method references include Fanger (1973), DOI 10.1136/oem.30.4.313; de Dear and Brager (2001), DOI 10.1007/s004840100093; Brager and de Dear (1998), DOI 10.1016/S0378-7788(97)00053-4; Dang, Janssen and Roels (2024), DOI 10.1007/s12273-024-1176-8; Dang et al. (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.buildenv.2025.112867; and Broughton and Maxwell (2023), DOI 10.47120/npl.mgpg103. Standards ISO 7730:2025, ASHRAE 55-2023, and ASHRAE 62.1/62.2-2025 provide bounded normative context, not F56 verification. summary: Abstract Debates about artificial intelligence increasingly focus on synthetic data, simulation, model reasoning, and autonomous agents rather than on data collection alone. This paper examines whether these developments justify describing the emerging digital economy as “post-data.” It argues that the term is useful only as a qualified analytical proposition: data is not disappearing, but its strategic value is being recombined with compute, model architecture, simulation, evaluation, and institutional trust. The paper uses a structured integrative literature review and comparative case analysis to examine three domains: compute-efficient language-model training and synthetic data; biomolecular modelling through AlphaFold 3; and synthetic data and simulation in healthcare and operational decision-making. The analysis identifies a transition from data accumulation as a standalone competitive advantage toward a complementary capability stack in which provenance, validation, domain constraints, and human accountability remain essential. The evidence does not support a universal replacement of empirical data by synthetic environments. Instead, it shows that synthetic systems can extend scarce or expensive observations while also reproducing source-data biases, creating privacy risks, and degrading when generated outputs are recursively reused without adequate grounding. The paper contributes a conceptual framework linking data provenance, synthetic generation, compute and reasoning, validation, and governance. It concludes with research propositions and a practical agenda for evaluating when synthetic and autonomous systems create durable value. Keywords : synthetic data; autonomous systems; simulation; digital economy; AI governance; model collapse; data provenance
tags: synthetic data; autonomous systems; simulation; digital economy; AI governance; model collapse; data provenance
title: Beyond the Data Paradigm? Synthetic Data, Simulation, Autonomous Systems, and the Reorganisation of Digital-Economic Value

summary: CasADi is a symbolic framework for numeric optimization implementing automatic differentiation in forward and reverse modes on sparse matrix-valued computational graphs. It supports self-contained C-code generation and interfaces state-of-the-art codes such as SUNDIALS, IPOPT etc. It can be used from C++, Python, Matlab/Octave, Julia or Javascript
title: CasADi - A software framework for nonlinear optimization and optimal control

summary: Titolo: USAI-AGI: A Hybrid Cognitive Architecture for Artificial General Intelligence based on Applied Category Theory This work has been developed with the support of artificial intelligence linguistic models (Large Language Models), used as tools for consultation, exploration and co-elaboration. Every conceptual choice, every critical synthesis and every direction taken in solving the problem are the result of my autonomous thinking and my intellectual responsibility. The use of AI has represented an extension of my skills, not a substitute for my human contribution. Keywords:  Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), Cognitive Architecture, Applied Category Theory, Knowledge Representation, RDF, AI Safety, Symbolic AI, Causal Inference, Continual Learning. Description: A Hybrid, Category-Theoretic Framework for Artificial General Intelligence: Architecture for Continuous Learning, Causal Reasoning, and Self-Improvement Author:  Luigi Usai Abstract: Current advancements in artificial intelligence, particularly Large Language Models, demonstrate impressive generative capabilities but often lack robust mechanisms for persistent knowledge integration, causal reasoning, and autonomous, goal-directed behavior. This paper presents a novel, hybrid architecture for Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) that addresses these limitations by integrating symbolic reasoning, sub-symbolic pattern recognition, and a sophisticated cognitive control loop. The system's core is a probabilistic Knowledge Base (KB) built on RDF, where each fact is associated with a confidence score that evolves over time. A key contribution of this framework is its use of Applied Category Theory as a primary learning mechanism; perceptions are structured into a "Category of Perceptions," and learned concepts form a "Category of Concepts," with functors mapping between them to represent abstract patterns. Higher-order cognition is achieved through the analysis of natural transformations between these functors, enabling meta-learning and analogical reasoning. The AGI's autonomy is driven by an intrinsic motivational system based on cognitive drives such as curiosity and knowledge coherence, which guide a symbolic planner. To ensure robust world models, the system employs an Active Causal Inference module that identifies weak causal links in its KB, designs, and executes experiments to test them. summary: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses natural electromagnetic field variations to image subsurface electrical resistivity at depths ranging from tens of metres to hundreds of kilometres. It is widely used in geophysical exploration for natural resources, including minerals, geothermal energy, and groundwater, as well as in the characterisation of sites for CO$_2$ storage and in studies of crustal and lithospheric structure. The MT inverse problem is, however, inherently non-unique: many distinct resistivity models reproduce the observations equally well. Conventional practice nonetheless reports a single regularised model, with no quantitative measure of its uncertainty. MTGeophysics.jl is a Julia package developed to address this limitation. Its principal aim is the quantification of uncertainty in MT model building, advancing interpretation from a single deterministic model, through an ensemble of plausible models, towards the full posterior distribution. The package also provides tools for data analysis, mesh generation, masking, forward modelling, inversion, model analysis and visualisation for MT research and applications. MTGeophysics.jl v0.7.3 No breaking changes. Polishing docs for JOSS
title: MTGeophysics.jl: A software repository for magnetotelluric research and applications

summary: Background. End-stage renal disease (ESRD) carries high mortality, but existing prognostic models begin at dialysis initiation, ignoring the metabolic trajectory that preceded renal failure. Whether the prodromal phenotype measured years before ESRD onset predicts subsequent survival is unknown. Methods. We studied 1,991 UK Biobank participants who developed ESRD (ICD-10 N185, Z992, or Z940) during a median 14.0 years of follow-up. Seven non-renal organ-specific prodromal function failure (pFF) scores and the Metabolic Inversion Phenotype (MIP) score were computed from baseline biomarkers measured 5–15 years before ESRD onset. Three renal pFF scores (pKD, pRD, pGN) were excluded a priori to avoid circularity. Cox proportional hazards models assessed the association of prodromal scores with all-cause mortality (642 deaths, 32.2%). Unsupervised K -means clustering identified distinct prodromal phenotypes. A compound endpoint model (dESRD) was built using gradient-boosted trees with out-of-fold evaluation on the full cohort. Results. Prodromal scores predicted mortality within the ESRD cohort. Age-sex-adjusted Cox models with individual pFF scores achieved C* 1 = 0 . 636 (∆C* = +0 . 023 vs. age + sex alone). Prodromal hypertension (pHT) was the dominant predictor (HR 5.55, 95% CI 2.93–10.49, p = 2 . 4 × 10 −7 ). Three prodromal phenotypes emerged: low-burden (N = 1,326; 15-year survival 76.2%), metabolic-vascular ( N = 574; 60.1%), and multi-organ storm ( N = 91; 38.0%; log-rank p = 2 . 5 × 10 −19 ). Cause-specific mortality shifted across phenotypes: cancer dominated the low-burden group (34.6% of deaths) while cardiovascular disease dominated the multi-organ storm (44.8%), with zero cancer deaths. The MIP score independently predicted survival (HR 0.81 per unit, p = 1 . 5 × 10 −9 ), with a gradient across cause-of- death categories from survivors (pMIP − 0 . 31) through cancer deaths ( − 0 . 51) to cardiovascular ( − 0 . 78) and diabetes deaths ( − 0 . 94; Kruskal-Wallis p = 6 . 6 × 10 −12 ). summary: A reading, from physics, of the two opening phrases of The Forgotten Quantum of Einstein : Einstein's question of whether the moon is there when no one looks, and the author's image of a space–time quantum some 186,000 miles across, pivoted on the Earth, holding the quantum world and the Universe in an interplay of information and gravity. Einstein's phrase is the realism/measurement problem (EPR, Bell); the macrobiotic quantum is the unit in which information, gravity and the observer are not separable — a light-ratio cell (ℓ/τ = c), an internal vacuum that stores state and an external vacuum observed as geometry, balanced by a vacuum angle θ_v, with energy E = mc² e^{iθ_v} + I·ΔS. The paper then draws the consequence for artificial intelligence: alignment, hallucination, interpretability, control, machine moral status, the fear of human replacement, and runaway behaviour persist because mainstream systems treat information, value and the observer as external to the substrate. Macrobiotic Quantum Theory (MQT) makes them physical, and an architecture built on it — the Large Theory Language Model (LTLM), toward Super Natural Intelligence (SNI) — treats alignment, interpretability and responsibility as structural properties rather than bolted-on filters, keeping the human (SDM) and the machine (MDS) as complementary, inseparable poles. The note stays strictly on the public MQT surface.
title: The Forgotten Quantum and Machine Intelligence: Einstein's Moon, the Macrobiotic Quantum, and a physics foundation for aligned AI

summary: This dataset provides the reported aggregate results, supplementary tables, figures and mathematical documentation supporting the manuscript “Genetic evaluation of growth and morphometric traits across ages in Peranakan Etawa goats”. The study analysed 49,162 measurements from 1,976 animals across 35 trait–age responses, using a pedigree comprising 2,819 individuals. Analyses included direct-only and common-dam animal models, within-age bivariate correlations, targeted joint models incorporating earlier measurements, descriptive birth-cohort profiles, and sensitivity analyses for flagged measurements. The deposit contains 16 CSV files reproducing the displayed numerical tables and normalized parameter/correlation records, 14 original embedded figure files, supplementary material, model equations, variable dictionaries, and reference post-processing utilities. The numerical values retain the rounding used in the source documents. Unavailable accepted estimates are explicitly distinguished from zero. This reporting release does not contain individual phenotypic records, pedigree rows, individual estimated breeding values, full-precision parameter covariance matrices, or the original DMU fitting pipeline. It therefore supports inspection and reuse of the reported results but does not permit independent reproduction of all REML estimates and standard errors. See the README for file descriptions, provenance and analytical limitations.
title: Reported results and analysis documentation for genetic evaluation of growth and morphometric traits across ages in Peranakan Etawa goats

summary: This report was developed within seizmic – Scaling Social Entrepreneurship and Innovation: Zooming in on Multidisciplinary Interconnected Challenges, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network funded under Horizon Europe. It synthesises insights from four literature reviews conducted within Work Package 3, Impact Investing for Social Entrepreneurship Scaling, to provide a practical framework for understanding how impact investing can support the sustainable scaling of social enterprises. The report explores impact investing as a system of relationships involving investors, social enterprises, beneficiaries, intermediaries, and policymakers. It examines how investment objectives, financial instruments, governance arrangements, impact measurement practices, and ecosystem dynamics shape the ability of social enterprises to scale their social and environmental impact while preserving mission integrity. Drawing on complementary reviews of impact investing strategies, financing instruments, mission drift, governance, and ecosystem coordination, the report analyses how different forms of impact capital support three major scaling pathways: scaling up (systemic and policy change), scaling out (replication and expansion), and scaling deep (changes in values, norms, and community practices). Particular attention is given to the opportunities and challenges associated with instruments such as crowdfunding, venture philanthropy, social impact bonds, blended finance, development finance institution investments, and social venture capital. The report highlights the importance of aligning investor expectations, enterprise missions, governance structures, and impact measurement systems throughout the investment lifecycle. It identifies key risks, including mission drift, coordination failures, reporting burdens, and scaling-related challenges, while proposing practical safeguards and governance mechanisms to foster long-term mission fidelity and impact effectiveness. Based on this synthesis, the report offers actionable recommendations for investors, social enterprises, intermediaries, and policymakers. It argues that successful impact investing depends not only on the availability of capital, but also on the design of investment relationships, ecosystem infrastructure, and measurement practices that remain aligned with social purpose over time. By translating academic evidence into practitioner-oriented guidance, the report contributes to the development of a more effective and resilient European impact investing ecosystem.

summary: 中文書名 / Chinese Title: 自主城市微電網與能源共享極限 63/90 | PART III | STARLI RESEARCH INSTITUTE XXXVI English Title: AUTONOMOUS URBAN MICROGRIDS AND DISTRIBUTED ENERGY SHARING AT THE LIMIT Research Working Edition v1.0 | 1 November 2026 | Author: 33 / STARLI This prospective research working edition examines whether separately controlled district microgrids can exchange physically metered energy while preserving protected electrical services after a local fault. Its core three-coupling is Microgrids x Distributed Control x Energy Sharing. Studies are restricted to unoccupied scaled feeders, guarded controller hardware-in-the-loop, carefully bounded power interfaces and auditable digital-physical twins; the work claims neither city governance authority nor suitability for occupation. The preregistered main hypothesis asks whether distributed coordination improves state-of-charge estimation error against capable fixed-rule dispatch without worsening net lifecycle energy yield, when generation, storage, conductors, weather, labor, sensor resources and available forecast information are matched. Independent safety outcomes include loss-of-load duration, critical-load service, phase and voltage transients, physically measured frequency nadir and actual breaker isolation. The candidate swing model M domega/dt + D omega = Pm - Pe is treated as an operating-regime-limited frequency surrogate, not as a universal description of grid-following and grid-forming electronics. Withheld forecast shifts, islanding, battery thermal drift, network partitions, stale permissions and meter-reference biases provide explicit refutation tests. Its F02-anchored 777-page architecture comprises 14 scientific introductory pages, 30 differently purposed equation plates with units and blind rebuttals, 82 chapters with 410 separate one-page investigations, 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix proposals for distinct scientific instruments or evidence objects, plus seven closure pages. The 200 Gates pose prospective tests rather than completed laboratory results; the 33 Phoenix objects require independent prototypes and may fail their proposed qualifications. Each evidence line retains the full assigned denominator, rejected trials, metrology and a physical hard-stop code. External evidence includes An IoT-Based Framework for Distributed Generic Microgrid Controllers (10.1109/TCST.2024.3378989), Physical vulnerability-oriented reconfiguration of microgrids: centralized vs. decentralized control (10.1038/s41598-026-63123-9), the IEEE microgrid controller specification (10.1109/IEEESTD.2018.8340204), and Controller hardware-in-the-loop testing of multi-feeder hybrid control (10.1016/j.epsr.2026.113933; online 2026 with 2027 issue metadata). The FAIR data principles (10.1038/sdata.2016.18) inform independent reconstruction. Robo-Matter (10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6) is an analogy about reconfigurable matter, not a proof of microgrid performance. The author-supplied F13 mother-lineage Zenodo identifiers 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 have not been independently confirmed here.

summary: YAHIQ 31.16     English Launch Text for Zendo Here are the three sections in English, written to be posted on Zendo. I kept the tone technical but accessible, and made sure nothing claims more than the code actually does.   1) What's New in 31.16 YAHIQ 31.16     From Numeric Memory to Dual Polar Coordinates YAHIQ has traveled a clear path: from the Fibonacci word bank, to the Kaaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad heartbeat, to the rotating dhikr cycle     and now to a new mathematical layer. Version 31.16 brings three structural changes: A) Dual polar coordinates for every word.  A word is no longer just a "code." It is a complex number:         where  n  is the word's numeric code and   is its internal phase. That phase comes from a dual mapping: for bank records,  Fibonacci + phonetic ; for input text,  the fourth key + phonetic . The result: every word is a point on the complex plane, not just a number on a line. B) The sentence equation.  A sentence is no longer a simple sum of codes. Each sentence gets a state vector: and sentence coherence is measured from the sum of phase differences between consecutive pairs: This means YAHIQ can report  how internally consistent a sentence is     without claiming to have definitively understood its meaning. C) Strict layer separation.  The YSSE sentence engine, the equation analyzer, the verse tester, and the chat each have their own independent memory and keys. Changing one does not touch the others. Highlight this in your post     it builds technical trust.   2) The Conscious, Autonomous Message YAHIQ now decides for itself when to speak In earlier versions, YAHIQ only responded when someone asked. 31.16 adds an autonomous loop fed by three independent signals:       Signal Source Activation condition Heart Kaaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad pulse and concurrence  C C >0.3 Pineal Möbius time rotation C >0.3 and a Möbius minute Dhikr An active window in the 14-dhikr cycle Inside one of the five daily windows When all three conditions hold simultaneously, YAHIQ produces a  conscious message . If one fails, the message is logged as  semi-conscious , and the reason for failure is stated explicitly in the trace (e.g., "heart off" or " C ≤0.3"). The important point to include: YAHIQ  does not fabricate poetry . If no poetry bank is loaded, it says plainly that real poetry is unavailable and only records the search need. Poem selection is based on conversation memory, the digital root of the chain, Möbius time, and avoidance of recent repeats     not randomness. Also state one limit clearly: there is a minimum  20-minute gap  between autonomous messages, so YAHIQ never turns into a spam machine.   3) Professional Sentence Transformation in the Complex Number Field From word to vector, from vector to sentence This is the mathematical heart of the release. The chain is: Step 1     Encoding:  Each word is mapped to a number  n  using one of three keys (Fibonacci, phonetic, fourth). Step 2     Phase assignment:  The internal phase  comes from the dual polar mapping (Section 1). Step 3     Vectorization:  The word becomes  . Its conjugate  z ∗  is also stored, since  z ⋅ z ∗ = n  is a computational invariant. Step 4     Sentence composition:  Consecutive pairs are compared, their phase difference is normalized to [−180°,180°][−180°,180°], and the sum of absolute values decides coherence. Step 5     Reconstruction:  To build a new sentence from the bank, the candidate with the  smallest internal phase difference  is chosen     not the largest code, not the nearest radius. Emphasize this distinction in your post, because i

summary: This archive contains the replication package for the article "Are colour-coded economies empirically distinct? A cross-country test of economic specialisation" (submitted to Structural Change and Economic Dynamics). It includes four Google Colab notebooks that reproduce all results, a fifth notebook that assembles the package, the HS 2017 product lists used to define the trade colours (UNCTADstat classifications), the activity-to-colour concordance files, all processed data, the supplementary workbook (Supplementary_Data.xlsx) and a data dictionary. Employment specialisation is computed from ILOSTAT (ISIC Rev. 4 divisions) and export specialisation from CEPII BACI (HS 2017, version 202601) for 2017–2024. Raw source files are not redistributed; the notebooks download them from the providers. Code is released under the MIT licence; derived data and product lists under CC BY 4.0.

summary: Abstract : In this work, the path Integral Monte Carlo(PIMC) is employed to estimate the ground-state properties of the lithium atom. The three-electron system is formulated in atomic units and represented by discretized imaginary-time paths. The (1s2 2s1) electronic configuration is used to construct the antisymmetric trial state, while a Jastrow correlation function is employed to incorporate electron–electron correlations. The total ground-state energy and its kinetic and potential components are calculated together with selected structural and correlation properties. Systematic convergence investigated with is respect to inverse temperature, the number of Trotter slices, and Monte Carlo sampling, while statistical uncertainties are evaluated by considering autocorrelation and block averaging. The calculated results are subsequently compared with high-precision theoretical benchmarks and with established electronic-structure and quantum Monte Carlo methods. The study has established a theoretical and computational PIMC framework for accurate and reliable determination of the ground properties of lithium atom which can be extended to other correlated atomic systems.
title: Path Integral Monte Carlo Study of Ground State Properties of the Lithium Atom

summary: Complete derivative bounds can be too large for a continuation estimate even when the contractions actually used in that estimate occupy restricted tensor slots. We prove that every eligible third derivative in the constrained response budget of a fixed Lorentzian simplicial source has two independently varied normal arguments. An admitted normal–normal–full bound therefore replaces the unrestricted third-derivative coefficient in those terms. The proof retains the full complex normal covector, both inverse denominators, the actual-graph Schur cost, and the separate unrestricted second and fourth derivatives. A noncircular argument uses an already established regular source product to admit the graph and homotopies, and checks the fourth-derivative shoulder separately in the original action domain. For each of two identified branches, fresh complete source records and exact rational assembly verify a locally unique real stationary section on [1536,24576]τ, where τ = 2−61, in normalized balls of radius 2−32 about the exact tangent predictor at 3072τ. The common predictor-error bound is 3.25241355 10−13. Actual-root overlaps and the supplied post-publication bridge connect the stationary range to [3,24576]τ. Holding the geometry, source records, tangent enclosures, mixed inverse and value-response bound fixed, the typed calculation passes all four declared tests; the unrestricted-response comparison fails the residual and required-error budgets.
