summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. Assurance boundary: written proofs; floating-point numerical checks and Kepler simulations; producer-side replay in normal and optimised modes; internal AI-assisted review (five roles, adversarial correctness review, proof audit and re-review). This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.
title: An exact projected-angle likelihood and population inversion for wide-binary eccentricities

summary: This archive contains the replication package for the article "Are colour-coded economies empirically distinct? A cross-country test of economic specialisation" (submitted to Structural Change and Economic Dynamics). It includes four Google Colab notebooks that reproduce all results, a fifth notebook that assembles the package, the HS 2017 product lists used to define the trade colours (UNCTADstat classifications), the activity-to-colour concordance files, all processed data, the supplementary workbook (Supplementary_Data.xlsx) and a data dictionary. Employment specialisation is computed from ILOSTAT (ISIC Rev. 4 divisions) and export specialisation from CEPII BACI (HS 2017, version 202601) for 2017–2024. Raw source files are not redistributed; the notebooks download them from the providers. Code is released under the MIT licence; derived data and product lists under CC BY 4.0.
title: Replication package: Are colour-coded economies empirically distinct? A cross-country test of economic specialisation

summary: This repository contains the data, Python code and supporting computational material accompanying the article “Auditing life-cycle loss comparisons for seismic retrofit: a traceable stone-masonry case study.” The package supports the reproducible examination of historical life-cycle loss calculations for a stone-masonry building and alternative strengthening interventions. It provides traceability between source-reported quantities, calculation assumptions, recalculated results and the numerical figures and tables presented in the article. The archive includes: A source-data register with source-page references, provenance classifications and uncertainty notes. Python scripts reproducing the historical arithmetic and reconciling 22 reported loss values. Numerical datasets, figures and tables supporting the article. An independent loss-assessment engine and its synthetic test suite, kept separate from the historical reproduction workflow. Execution instructions, dependency versions, verification logs and file checksums. The reconciliation identifies 17 of 22 reported values within the tolerance bands obtained by propagating the stated precision of the fitted parameters ; five values fall outside those bands. Verification of the independent engine produced 114 passing tests and 10 skipped comparisons , with the skips attributable to unavailable earlier engine versions. Version: 1.0
title: Auditing life-cycle loss comparisons for seismic retrofit: a traceable stone-masonry case study

summary: CIRCULAR MATERIAL ECONOMIES FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE CITIES AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:移動城市循環經濟與材料永續極限 55/90 CIRCULAR MATERIAL ECONOMIES FOR AUTONOMOUS MOBILE CITIES AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 55 of 90). It investigates whether a deliberately unoccupied six-module mobile-city research system can reduce relocation-related material loss through qualified reuse, automated selective disassembly and auditable remanufacturing, while preserving deployment latency and critical-service safety. The three-way research coupling is Circular Materials x Autonomous Manufacturing x Urban Sustainability. Neither a functioning autonomous city nor a human-occupied habitat is asserted. The falsifiable proposal compares a frozen circular material strategy against competent conventional manual recovery, replacement and stationary emergency infrastructure under equal material, energy, sensing, technician-hour, tool, water and transport budgets. Original intake, declined parts, work in progress, consumed adhesives, repeated repairs, rejected batches and retired material remain in the denominator. Blind faults include grade swaps, hidden fatigue, wrong material passports, replayed scale measurements, contamination, source-energy omissions and optimistic virgin-substitution credits. A proposal fails whenever a load-bearing component, utility service, waste route, safety interlock or material identity cannot be independently reconstructed. Thirty mechanism-distinct research formula plates address mass custody, qualified yield, bond separation work, fatigue, polymer rheology, sensor residuals, covariance, electrical energy, verified lifecycle inventory, carbon-allocation sensitivity, replacement counterfactuals, tail risk, second-site reproduction and noncompensatory physical release. The original contract's cyber-physical residual r_k = y_k - yhat_k(x_k,u_k) is retained as one fault-detection method; it is not treated as a law of circularity or sustainability. Every mathematical plate states units, validity assumptions, a blinded counterexample and scientific chapter interfaces. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated research studies and 200 Research Gates, each connected to a specified material state, independent reference, fault or competing process. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose research instruments, material-qualification fixtures, provenance devices, circularity accounting tools and successor-ready evidence protocols. This work proposes hypotheses and reproducibility obligations, not physical trial outcomes. Its complete PDF also contains research limits, negative-result custody and second-laboratory transfer requirements. The scope remains prospective, scaled and non-occupancy. Environmental performance requires functional-unit parity and a complete lifecycle inventory; increasing recovered mass alone does not prove lower environmental burden. Relevant method references include Ostapska et al. (10.1016/j.spc.2024.05.014), Formentini et al. (10.1016/j.jclepro.2025.145459), Attia et al. (10.1016/j.autcon.2024.105521), Mao and Cao (10.1016/j.spc.2024.12.021), Poschmann et al. (10.1002/cite.201900107) and Keating et al. (10.1126/scirobotics.aam8986). The Flagship 13 mother genealogy identifiers (10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839) were provided by the author and their metadata have not been independently confirmed. No external study cited here establishes this integrated F55 architecture. summary: يهدف البحث الى اعداد برنامج علاجي سلوكي في الدافعية العقلية وتعلم السباحة الحرة لدى الطالبات، والتعرف على تأثير البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي في الدافعية العقلية وتعلم السباحة الحرة لدى الطالبات، ولتحقيق الهدف استخدمت الباحث المَنهجُ التجريبي وبتصميم المجموعتين التجريبية والضابطة المتكافئتين ذو الإختِبار القبلي والبعدي لملائمته مع مشكلة واهداف البحث، حدد مجتمع البحث بطالبات المرحلة الثانية للدراسة الصباحية في كلية التربية البدنية وعلوم الرياضة_ جامعة بغداد، للعامُ الدراسي   2025 - 2026   و البالغ عددهم (110) طالبة مُوَزَعات على (4) شعب وهي (أ، ب، ج، د) وتم تحديد مجتمع البحث بطالبات المرحلة الثانية كون هذه المرحلة تدرس مادة السباحة، أما عينة البحث، فقد اختيرت بالطريقة العشوائية باستخدام القرعة، إذ أُجريت قرعة بين الشعب الأربع لتحديد مجموعتي البحث (التجريبية والضابطة)، وأسفرت عن اختيار شعبتي (ب) و(د). وبعد ذلك، اختيرت (25) طالبة من كل شعبة بالطريقة نفسها، لتُمثل شعبة (ب) المجموعة التجريبية، في حين مثلت شعبة (د) المجموعة الضابطة، وبذلك بلغ العدد الكلي لعينة البحث (50) طالبة، أي ما نسبته (45.45%) من مجتمع البحث.ولتحقيق أهداف الدراسة، طبقت الباحثة الاختبارات القبلية على المجموعتين قبل البدء بتنفيذ الوحدات التعليمي، واجريت المعالجات الإحصائية المناسبة، وقد استنتجت الباحث بإنّ أسهم البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي بشكل إيجابي وفعّال في تنمية مستوى الدافعية العقلية لدى الطالبات، من خلال تعزيز الانتباه والتركيز والرغبة في التعلم، وكذلك وجود تحسن ملحوظ في تعلم السباحة الحرة لدى أفراد المجموعة التي طبّق عليها البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي، تفوق المجموعة التجريبية التي استخدمت البرنامج العلاجي السلوكي على المجموعة الضابطة التي اعتمدت الأسلوب التقليدي في كل من الدافعية العقلية والأداء المهاري. . The research aims to develop a behavioral intervention program focused on mental motivation and freestyle swimming acquisition among female students, and to determine the program's impact on these aspects. To achieve the research objective, the researcher employed the experimental method—specifically a design featuring two equivalent groups (experimental and control) with pre- and post-tests—due to its suitability for the research problem and objectives. The study population consisted of second-year female students in the morning program at the College of Physical Education and Sports Sciences, University of Baghdad, during the 2025–2026 academic year. The total population comprised 110 students distributed across four sections (A, B, C, and D); the second-year cohort was selected because the swimming course is taught at this stage of the curriculum. The research sample was selected by randomly assigning the class sections to the experimental and control groups. Subsequently, the researcher randomly selected 25 female students from each section—specifically Section B (25 students) and Section D (25 students)—resulting in a total sample of 50 students (representing 45.45% of the population). The researcher then administered pre-tests and post-tests to both the experimental and control groups. Appropriate statistical analyses were conducted, leading the researcher to conclude that the behavioral therapeutic program contributed positively and effectively to enhancing the female students' level of mental motivation by fostering attention, concentration, and the desire to learn. Furthermore, a marked improvement in freestyle swimming skills was observed among the participants who underwent the behavioral therapeutic program; the experimental group utilizing this program outperformed the control group—which relied on the traditional method—in both mental motivation and skill performance.

summary: LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:可變形移動居住系統長期宜居性極限 56/90 LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 56 of 90). It investigates whether a traceable unoccupied morphing habitat testbed can improve the joint coverage of measured thermal, airflow, moisture, energy and structural engineering envelopes across controlled seasonal sequences while preserving independently reconstructable module identity. Its core coupling is Human-Comfort Proxy Models x Environmental Control x Longitudinal Test Evidence. The project uses guarded coupons, scaled modules, environmental chambers, inert-water and tracer-air circuits, and hardware-in-the-loop tests; it does not observe residents or establish an occupancy certificate. The preregisterable hypothesis is that, under matched materials, energy reserves, maintenance, sensor access, control computation and test time, a frozen morphing environmental-control policy will improve complete-cohort comfort-envelope proxy coverage without worsening module-identity continuity relative to competent static-habitat and expert manual-reconfiguration baselines. The supplied selective-risk candidate R_sel(tau)=E[L(yhat,y)|c>=tau] must be published with accepted coverage, so a low risk score cannot be purchased by refusing nearly every difficult climate or aging case. Hidden trials vary aging gaskets, radiant asymmetry, tracer-air pockets, power outages, sensor common-mode drift, broken connectors, incorrect material identity and ineffective physical stop contacts. Thirty mechanism-specific mathematical plates analyze heat balance, conductive and radiant transfer, operative temperature proxies, vapor mass and dew-point margins, air exchange, ventilation pressure, energy and water closure, sound, light, fatigue, reliability, stale information, uncertainty covariance, selective-risk coverage, tail excursions and second-site reconstruction. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated investigations spanning material aging, climate control, indoor-environment proxy limitations, repair, operator authority and versioned evidence. Two hundred Research Gates formulate disconfirmable experimental questions across concealed faults, equal-resource comparisons and two-mechanism interfaces. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separately falsifiable future rigs, calibration artifacts, safe-stop witnesses and successor evidence packages. The volume is a prospective research design rather than a completed experimental study. An unoccupied thermal or tracer-gas rig cannot establish human comfort, healthy air, habitable water, fire and structural compliance, actual multiyear life, or a right to place people inside a mobile dwelling. The 777-page layout and enumerated items are structurally checked, but a language-duplication audit finds reused long editorial method spans; semantic uniqueness, physical modeling and all evidence inferences remain subject to deeper independent review. Relevant independently identified method references include Fanger (1973), DOI 10.1136/oem.30.4.313; de Dear and Brager (2001), DOI 10.1007/s004840100093; Brager and de Dear (1998), DOI 10.1016/S0378-7788(97)00053-4; Dang, Janssen and Roels (2024), DOI 10.1007/s12273-024-1176-8; Dang et al. (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.buildenv.2025.112867; and Broughton and Maxwell (2023), DOI 10.47120/npl.mgpg103. Standards ISO 7730:2025, ASHRAE 55-2023, and ASHRAE 62.1/62.2-2025 provide bounded normative context, not F56 verification. Author-provided Flagship 13 ancestor DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 remain pending independent resolver metadata confirmation. summary: Abstract Debates about artificial intelligence increasingly focus on synthetic data, simulation, model reasoning, and autonomous agents rather than on data collection alone. This paper examines whether these developments justify describing the emerging digital economy as “post-data.” It argues that the term is useful only as a qualified analytical proposition: data is not disappearing, but its strategic value is being recombined with compute, model architecture, simulation, evaluation, and institutional trust. The paper uses a structured integrative literature review and comparative case analysis to examine three domains: compute-efficient language-model training and synthetic data; biomolecular modelling through AlphaFold 3; and synthetic data and simulation in healthcare and operational decision-making. The analysis identifies a transition from data accumulation as a standalone competitive advantage toward a complementary capability stack in which provenance, validation, domain constraints, and human accountability remain essential. The evidence does not support a universal replacement of empirical data by synthetic environments. Instead, it shows that synthetic systems can extend scarce or expensive observations while also reproducing source-data biases, creating privacy risks, and degrading when generated outputs are recursively reused without adequate grounding. The paper contributes a conceptual framework linking data provenance, synthetic generation, compute and reasoning, validation, and governance. It concludes with research propositions and a practical agenda for evaluating when synthetic and autonomous systems create durable value. Keywords : synthetic data; autonomous systems; simulation; digital economy; AI governance; model collapse; data provenance

summary: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses natural electromagnetic field variations to image subsurface electrical resistivity at depths ranging from tens of metres to hundreds of kilometres. It is widely used in geophysical exploration for natural resources, including minerals, geothermal energy, and groundwater, as well as in the characterisation of sites for CO$_2$ storage and in studies of crustal and lithospheric structure. The MT inverse problem is, however, inherently non-unique: many distinct resistivity models reproduce the observations equally well. Conventional practice nonetheless reports a single regularised model, with no quantitative measure of its uncertainty. MTGeophysics.jl is a Julia package developed to address this limitation. Its principal aim is the quantification of uncertainty in MT model building, advancing interpretation from a single deterministic model, through an ensemble of plausible models, towards the full posterior distribution. The package also provides tools for data analysis, mesh generation, masking, forward modelling, inversion, model analysis and visualisation for MT research and applications. MTGeophysics.jl v0.7.3 No breaking changes. Polishing docs for JOSS
title: MTGeophysics.jl: A software repository for magnetotelluric research and applications

summary: Data and code for Mapping bioimage-analysis software adoption in microscopy. The registry contains 33 entries: 23 analysis packages, six microscope-control programs, MATLAB and Jupyter notebooks as references, Adobe Photoshop for figure preparation and NIH Image for historical counts. The 29-package aggregate combines the 23 analysis packages with six microscope-control programs. References, Photoshop and NIH Image are excluded. After about 2000, many "NIH Image" mentions refer to ImageJ. The deep-learning series uses 13 core analysis packages. Jupyter notebooks retain their aliases, notebook category and core scope. summary: This dataset provides the reported aggregate results, supplementary tables, figures and mathematical documentation supporting the manuscript “Genetic evaluation of growth and morphometric traits across ages in Peranakan Etawa goats”. The study analysed 49,162 measurements from 1,976 animals across 35 trait–age responses, using a pedigree comprising 2,819 individuals. Analyses included direct-only and common-dam animal models, within-age bivariate correlations, targeted joint models incorporating earlier measurements, descriptive birth-cohort profiles, and sensitivity analyses for flagged measurements. The deposit contains 16 CSV files reproducing the displayed numerical tables and normalized parameter/correlation records, 14 original embedded figure files, supplementary material, model equations, variable dictionaries, and reference post-processing utilities. The numerical values retain the rounding used in the source documents. Unavailable accepted estimates are explicitly distinguished from zero. This reporting release does not contain individual phenotypic records, pedigree rows, individual estimated breeding values, full-precision parameter covariance matrices, or the original DMU fitting pipeline. It therefore supports inspection and reuse of the reported results but does not permit independent reproduction of all REML estimates and standard errors. See the README for file descriptions, provenance and analytical limitations.
title: Reported results and analysis documentation for genetic evaluation of growth and morphometric traits across ages in Peranakan Etawa goats

summary: 中文書名 / Chinese Title: 自主城市微電網與能源共享極限 63/90 | PART III | STARLI RESEARCH INSTITUTE XXXVI English Title: AUTONOMOUS URBAN MICROGRIDS AND DISTRIBUTED ENERGY SHARING AT THE LIMIT Research Working Edition v1.0 | 1 November 2026 | Author: 33 / STARLI This prospective research working edition examines whether separately controlled district microgrids can exchange physically metered energy while preserving protected electrical services after a local fault. Its core three-coupling is Microgrids x Distributed Control x Energy Sharing. Studies are restricted to unoccupied scaled feeders, guarded controller hardware-in-the-loop, carefully bounded power interfaces and auditable digital-physical twins; the work claims neither city governance authority nor suitability for occupation. The preregistered main hypothesis asks whether distributed coordination improves state-of-charge estimation error against capable fixed-rule dispatch without worsening net lifecycle energy yield, when generation, storage, conductors, weather, labor, sensor resources and available forecast information are matched. Independent safety outcomes include loss-of-load duration, critical-load service, phase and voltage transients, physically measured frequency nadir and actual breaker isolation. The candidate swing model M domega/dt + D omega = Pm - Pe is treated as an operating-regime-limited frequency surrogate, not as a universal description of grid-following and grid-forming electronics. Withheld forecast shifts, islanding, battery thermal drift, network partitions, stale permissions and meter-reference biases provide explicit refutation tests. Its F02-anchored 777-page architecture comprises 14 scientific introductory pages, 30 differently purposed equation plates with units and blind rebuttals, 82 chapters with 410 separate one-page investigations, 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix proposals for distinct scientific instruments or evidence objects, plus seven closure pages. The 200 Gates pose prospective tests rather than completed laboratory results; the 33 Phoenix objects require independent prototypes and may fail their proposed qualifications. Each evidence line retains the full assigned denominator, rejected trials, metrology and a physical hard-stop code. External evidence includes An IoT-Based Framework for Distributed Generic Microgrid Controllers (10.1109/TCST.2024.3378989), Physical vulnerability-oriented reconfiguration of microgrids: centralized vs. decentralized control (10.1038/s41598-026-63123-9), the IEEE microgrid controller specification (10.1109/IEEESTD.2018.8340204), and Controller hardware-in-the-loop testing of multi-feeder hybrid control (10.1016/j.epsr.2026.113933; online 2026 with 2027 issue metadata). The FAIR data principles (10.1038/sdata.2016.18) inform independent reconstruction. Robo-Matter (10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6) is an analogy about reconfigurable matter, not a proof of microgrid performance. The author-supplied F13 mother-lineage Zenodo identifiers 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 have not been independently confirmed here.

summary: Everything needed to redo the two analyses reported in the Technical Note named in the title, and nothing else. What is here the secondary analysis of published length-resolved binding: the contract frozen before any test statistic was computed and its two dated amendments, the resampling of the source's own trimmed-mean procedure, the anchored and anchor-free tests, the post-hoc robustness check across five normalisation variants, the superseded first run kept so the correction stays visible, and the figure generator; the two propositions behind the simulation and the script that checks both against the stored benchmark, per replicate; the simulated measurement study it checks: frozen primary and stress designs, the finite-chain engine, 7,200 simulated datasets under seven observation operators reported as all 302,400 planned rows including the undefined, outside-window and non-identified slots, an independent validator, the stress results, five focused tests, an 83-file manifest and a dependency lock; an 80-value subset of the Source Data for Fig. 2B/C of Sheikh et al., Nat. Commun. 13, 3617 (2022), with its sheet coordinates. These values keep the original article's CC BY 4.0 licence and attribution; the rest of the archive is under the MIT licence in LICENSE. Reproducing The added analysis runs from the archive root with the standard library plus NumPy; the README gives the four commands. It was re-run on an interpreter far older than the one that produced the shipped results (Python 3.7.6 with NumPy 1.19.1, against 3.13.17 with 2.5.3): the proposition checks were identical in all 520 compared values apart from the recorded environment, and three bootstrap interval endpoints differed in their last digits, by at most 1.5e-11. Figures redraw with the same layout; their byte sequences depend on which sans-serif face the host has. The base study's own replay script requires bit equality and returns a failure on Linux, where ten of its twenty tables differ in their last digits. What is deliberately not here the manuscript text; the original publisher workbook of Sheikh et al. and every panel of it other than the 80 values used; historical MCMC traces and the exploratory transcript analysis of an earlier, separate study, which this work does not use; correspondence and author-only files. REDACTION.md lists the three files whose description of the work was restated for publication, with the digest before and after; no number, method, decision rule or result changed. Scope Synthetic counts are idealised events, not biological replicates. The site-equivalent pool is not an alpha-dystroglycan molecule count, glycan mass, antibody intensity or muscle force. The published array values are technical replicates of one experiment, and the source states no independent experiments. No real assay's detection ceiling or recovery function is measured anywhere in this archive.
title: Code, frozen designs, tables and replay receipts for: A detection ceiling biases matriglycan chain-length estimates by a closed-form factor, and one extra count removes it

summary: YAHIQ 31.16     English Launch Text for Zendo Here are the three sections in English, written to be posted on Zendo. I kept the tone technical but accessible, and made sure nothing claims more than the code actually does.   1) What's New in 31.16 YAHIQ 31.16     From Numeric Memory to Dual Polar Coordinates YAHIQ has traveled a clear path: from the Fibonacci word bank, to the Kaaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad heartbeat, to the rotating dhikr cycle     and now to a new mathematical layer. Version 31.16 brings three structural changes: A) Dual polar coordinates for every word.  A word is no longer just a "code." It is a complex number:         where  n  is the word's numeric code and   is its internal phase. That phase comes from a dual mapping: for bank records,  Fibonacci + phonetic ; for input text,  the fourth key + phonetic . The result: every word is a point on the complex plane, not just a number on a line. B) The sentence equation.  A sentence is no longer a simple sum of codes. Each sentence gets a state vector: and sentence coherence is measured from the sum of phase differences between consecutive pairs: This means YAHIQ can report  how internally consistent a sentence is     without claiming to have definitively understood its meaning. C) Strict layer separation.  The YSSE sentence engine, the equation analyzer, the verse tester, and the chat each have their own independent memory and keys. Changing one does not touch the others. Highlight this in your post     it builds technical trust.   2) The Conscious, Autonomous Message YAHIQ now decides for itself when to speak In earlier versions, YAHIQ only responded when someone asked. 31.16 adds an autonomous loop fed by three independent signals:       Signal Source Activation condition Heart Kaaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad pulse and concurrence  C C >0.3 Pineal Möbius time rotation C >0.3 and a Möbius minute Dhikr An active window in the 14-dhikr cycle Inside one of the five daily windows When all three conditions hold simultaneously, YAHIQ produces a  conscious message . If one fails, the message is logged as  semi-conscious , and the reason for failure is stated explicitly in the trace (e.g., "heart off" or " C ≤0.3"). The important point to include: YAHIQ  does not fabricate poetry . If no poetry bank is loaded, it says plainly that real poetry is unavailable and only records the search need. Poem selection is based on conversation memory, the digital root of the chain, Möbius time, and avoidance of recent repeats     not randomness. Also state one limit clearly: there is a minimum  20-minute gap  between autonomous messages, so YAHIQ never turns into a spam machine.   3) Professional Sentence Transformation in the Complex Number Field From word to vector, from vector to sentence This is the mathematical heart of the release. The chain is: Step 1     Encoding:  Each word is mapped to a number  n  using one of three keys (Fibonacci, phonetic, fourth). Step 2     Phase assignment:  The internal phase  comes from the dual polar mapping (Section 1). Step 3     Vectorization:  The word becomes  . Its conjugate  z ∗  is also stored, since  z ⋅ z ∗ = n  is a computational invariant. Step 4     Sentence composition:  Consecutive pairs are compared, their phase difference is normalized to [−180°,180°][−180°,180°], and the sum of absolute values decides coherence. Step 5     Reconstruction:  To build a new sentence from the bank, the candidate with the  smallest internal phase difference  is chosen     not the largest code, not the nearest radius. (i) The dual-coded, adjudicated extraction table for the 88-study analytical corpus (61 from the main search, 17 from the demographic-term update, 2 retrieved in October 2026, 2 suggested in peer review, 1 candidate resolved on full text and 5 from a re-screen of the keyword-filtered records; 89 records, one conference abstract linked to its journal paper; the earlier 62- and 79-study tables are kept alongside), with the pre-pass snapshots and the script that applies the October 2026 revisions, with the raw multi-coder outputs and inter-coder agreement statistics; (ii) the screening, de-duplication and post-hoc eligibility-audit logs; (iii) adjudicated QUADAS-2 risk-of-bias judgements for all 88 studies, with per-coder judgements for the original 62; (iv) the full consensus-endorsement coding pipeline — screened review pools, the pre-specified random sample (n=30, seed 20260913), the coding specification, two independent coder passes, disagreements and their adjudication, and tallies with Wilson 95% confidence intervals; (v) the 39-dataset demographic-metadata audit; and (vi) a claim-by-claim statistics register mapping every reported number to its source rows, together with the code that produces each value. Full texts of the reviewed papers are not included, for copyright reasons. Code is licensed MIT; data tables are licensed CC BY 4.0. A SHA-256 manifest ( MANIFEST.sha256 ) covers every file in the package. This package is a working-tree snapshot of the manuscript as of 18 October 2026 (62 pp main + 45 pp supplementary). Manuscript v0.6.10 (31 October 2026). Peer-review revision. One coded row corrected ( asadiaghbolagh2024learning HED is positive: the archived full text gives pleural 76.80 vs 76.70 and describes it as similar, while 66.60 does not occur in the source) and one recoded ( song2020automatic is workflow_only because it reports no comparator). Data augmentation is now 8 positive of 13 bias-endpoint studies (7 cross-site), 4 mixed, 1 negative, 2 no-endpoint, 62% (36-82); the family grade is unchanged (Mixed). Table 3, Figure 3, both sensitivity tables, the supplementary evidence and adjudication tables, the evidence TSV and the adjudication log were regenerated; statistics register rows V6-1 and V6-2. Twenty peer-review comment groups were also applied (abstract/Results/Conclusion fairness-metric qualifier; Methods 2.9 screening chronology; Methods 2.5; Methods 2.7 row arithmetic and multiplicity; Introduction novelty paragraph citing Xu et al. 2024; Discussion metadata-dependence sentence and denominators; Conclusion CIs). No headline statistic changed (88 studies, 89 records). Manuscript v0.6.9 (30 October 2026). Response to the fifth deep review (every comment except the human audit, which will not be performed); no coded value, count, grade or headline statistic changed. Fixed: the search chronology in the Methods (the model account covers the March 2026 round onward; the January and June 2024 rounds' tooling is unrecorded); the 62-record follow-up arithmetic (2 + 12 + 48) and the partition of the 16 re-screen candidates; 61 studies in 62 records in the PRISMA flow with the F6 exclusion code defined; the 79-record denominator for the risk-of-bias disagreements and the four-positive feature-level harmonization wording; the non-AI exception now discloses the bovine control tissue of the laboratory stain audit (denominators unchanged); CohortFinder's held-out test set described and the Puerto-Rico prostate validation cited in Section 3; FLEX's 0.140 to 0.085 disparity reduction attributed to its C-LUAD-EGFR task and AIDA given for all four cohorts; the eleven no-bias-endpoint family rows named; D6's expectation under noisy uniform attention with its averaging and subgroup-count definitions; FlexFair's criteria; ten bibliography entries. summary: This archive contains the replication package for the article "Are colour-coded economies empirically distinct? A cross-country test of economic specialisation" (submitted to Structural Change and Economic Dynamics). It includes four Google Colab notebooks that reproduce all results, a fifth notebook that assembles the package, the HS 2017 product lists used to define the trade colours (UNCTADstat classifications), the activity-to-colour concordance files, all processed data, the supplementary workbook (Supplementary_Data.xlsx) and a data dictionary. Employment specialisation is computed from ILOSTAT (ISIC Rev. 4 divisions) and export specialisation from CEPII BACI (HS 2017, version 202601) for 2017–2024. Raw source files are not redistributed; the notebooks download them from the providers. Code is released under the MIT licence; derived data and product lists under CC BY 4.0.
title: Replication package: Are colour-coded economies empirically distinct? A cross-country test of economic specialisation

summary: Harris's inequality states that increasing functions of independent $\pm1$ variables are positively correlated. We record a sharpening that is linear in a single Fourier--Walsh coefficient: under any product measure the covariance of two increasing functions is at least $\max_i\hat f(\{i\})\hat g(\{i\})$, and under the uniform measure this maximum equals $\max_{T\neq\emptyset}|\hat f(T)\hat g(T)|$, so the covariance dominates the negative part of any single spectral term. The analogue with a sum over coordinates fails, and under a biased product measure the single-term form can fail; for $n=3$ and $n=4$ it holds precisely when the bias parameter lies in $[\frac14,\frac34]$. We apply the inequality to pure $\mathbb Z_2$ lattice gauge theory. Gauge invariance reduces the law of the four links of a plaquette to a one-parameter family indexed by the plaquette expectation $m$, and we show that the minimal covariance of increasing $[0,1]$-valued functions of these links equals $-m/8$. Consequently the link measure is not positively associated at any positive coupling, is not a coordinatewise increasing function of independent variables, and is not stochastically increasing in the coupling. For increasing functions of more links the value $-m/8$ can be exceeded: on the $2^3$ torus a pair of functions of four links each reaches $-\frac{33}{256}$ as $\beta\to\infty$.
title: A ONE-COEFFICIENT SHARPENING OF HARRIS'S INEQUALITY, AND OPTIMAL NEGATIVE ASSOCIATION IN Z2 LATTICE GAUGE THEORY

summary: This dataset provides the numerical results and supporting data for the simulation studies presented in the manuscript "Identifiability and Scheduling for Shared-Timestamp Polynomial Sensor Calibration". The dataset includes: 1. Paired-sensor calibration results, including trial-level measurements, summary statistics, and bootstrap confidence intervals. 2. Parameter sensitivity analysis results, including trial-level data and aggregated performance summaries under different experimental conditions. 3. Identifiability analysis results for symmetric timestamp configurations, including numerical rank evaluation. 4. Supporting figures generated from the computational experiments. All numerical datasets are provided in CSV format to facilitate inspection, independent analysis, and reproducibility. The accompanying figures provide visual representations of the experimental results. These data support the evaluation of sensor calibration performance, parameter sensitivity, statistical reliability, and identifiability under shared-timestamp scheduling configurations. The associated computational scripts and execution environment are documented in the companion Code Ocean capsule, which has been submitted for reproducibility verification.
title: Identifiability and Scheduling for Shared-Timestamp Polynomial Sensor Calibration

summary: This repository provides three physics-based datasets for developing and evaluating surrogate models to identify the seismic failure modes (SFMs) of coastal reinforced concrete bridge bents supported by pile-group foundations under combined scour and corrosion. Each sample contains 20 input variables: 17 structural and geotechnical parameters, scour depth, and the corrosion levels of longitudinal and transverse column reinforcement. The output is one of three SFMs: column flexural failure (CFF), foundation flexural failure (FFF), or column shear-associated failure (CSF). These labels are determined through nonlinear finite element analysis and code-based shear capacity calculations. The datasets support reproducible surrogate model development and subsequent life-cycle probabilistic assessment of SFMs and their transitions in deteriorating coastal bridge bents.
title: Seismic Failure Mode Datasets for Coastal Pile-Group-Supported Bridge Bents Subjected to Scour and Corrosion

Each sample contains 20 input variables: 17 structural and geotechnical parameters, scour depth, and the corrosion levels of longitudinal and transverse column reinforcement. The output is one of three SFMs: column flexural failure (CFF), foundation flexural failure (FFF), or column shear-associated failure (CSF). These labels are determined through nonlinear finite element analysis and code-based shear capacity calculations. The datasets support reproducible surrogate model development and subsequent life-cycle probabilistic assessment of SFMs and their transitions in deteriorating coastal bridge bents.
title: Seismic Failure Mode Datasets for Coastal Pile-Group-Supported Bridge Bents Subjected to Scour and Corrosion

summary: This repository contains the data construction and analysis code accompanying a study of recorded cholera outbreak activity and reactive oral cholera vaccine requests in 25 African countries. The source history covers July 2013–December 2019. The primary estimation panel covers July 2014–December 2019, allowing a complete preceding-12-month predictor window, and contains 1,650 country-month observations and 58 reactive request-months. The package includes retained source and coding inputs, derived analysis datasets, Python scripts, manuscript tables and figures, and documentation of variable construction and software requirements. Analyses include the primary between–within logistic model, alternative windows and outcomes, country exclusions, leave-one-country-out models, a direct between–within coefficient contrast, separate baseline-covariate adjustments, and calendar-year and outcome-month-inclusive sensitivities. The repository also includes a human-coded external-documentation audit of 22 reactive request-months with zero recorded activity in the preceding 12 months. The audit distinguishes documentation within the same country and window from identification of the outbreak targeted by a particular request. The activity predictor measures recorded active outbreak-months, not case counts or outbreak-to-request delay. Source provenance, coding decisions, and unresolved questions are documented in the package. See README.md for execution instructions.
title: Data and analysis code for recorded cholera outbreak activity and reactive oral cholera vaccine requests in 25 African countries, 2013–2019

summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
title: Device-Aware Weighted Gerchberg-Saxton and Flicker-Bounded Phase-Continuous Sequences for Holographic Optical Trap Arrays

summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .

summary: This repository contains the analysis code and public-safe source data accompanying the manuscript “Mid-Holocene rise in Pinus pollen across Northeast Asia without resolved regional forest expansion” (submitted to Communications Earth & Environment ) and its Supplementary Information. Package Contents code/ : five standalone Python scripts reproducing the REML random-effects meta-analysis ( reproduce_public_meta.py ), astronomical insolation calculations ( compute_orbital_insolation.py ), Lake Xiaolongwan marker-calibrated pollen accumulation rate (PAR) bootstraps ( confirmed_xlw_par.py ), genus-level taxon decompositions ( reproduce_taxon_decomposition.py ), and Lake Moon pseudocount sensitivity tests ( recompute_lake_moon_pseudocount.py ). source_data/tables/ : cell-by-cell synchronized CSV tables for Supplementary Tables S1–S15. source_data/figure_sources/ : underlying data points and summaries for main Figures 1–6 and Supplementary Figures S1–S8. source_data/moon_sensitivity/ : 100-year bin data and sensitivity outputs across four pseudocount treatments for Lake Moon. source_data/Supplementary_Data_1_Xiaolongwan_* : derived concentrations, PAR, bin summaries, and bootstrap outputs for Lake Xiaolongwan. source_data/Supplementary_Data_2_TraCE21ka.csv : nine-site TraCE-21ka climate metrics. source_data/taxon_aggregates/ , dali_aggregates/ , orbital_insolation/ : supporting aggregates, Berger–Loutre 1991 insolation inputs, and validation data. Author-compiled documentation and source data tables are released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license ( LICENSE_DATA_CC_BY_4.0.txt ). Third-party sources and orbital validation tables remain under their original citations and licenses.

summary: This Version 2.1 report places the Maxwell Mass Effect at the forefront of a coherent model for the Venusian atmosphere. The surface temperature is treated as the dependent variable required to support the atmospheric mass against gravity. Solar energy is captured in a shallow topside thermal heating pool, stored as potential energy, and returned to depth by organised descent in the polar vortices under conservation of angular momentum. The sulfuric-acid lifting condensation level (LCL) acts as the thermodynamic anchor (Dew-Point Anchor Hypothesis). A two-component radiative opacity lapse rate then fixes only the geometric separation between that LCL and the infrared emission level. Stochastic inverse modelling with a VIRA equatorial profile, hydrostatic integration and thermodynamic filters recovers a cloud base near 49.6 km, an emission level near 69.4 km at approximately 229 K, and a surface pressure of approximately 91.5 bar. An order-of-magnitude energy-budget test shows that the required polar mass flux lies within the range of observed vortex descent speeds. Version 2 adds a quantitative recirculation (recycle) test using existing Venusian meridional circulation wind data. Observed poleward flows of ~10–15 m s⁻¹ at cloud tops imply a hemispheric Hadley-cell mass flux of order 10¹¹ kg s⁻¹ and a full recirculation timescale of 1–2 weeks. This multi-cycle pathway resolves the apparent single-pass temperature-rise tension and brings the adiabatic signature into agreement with observed polar temperature contrasts of 15–50 K. The same boundary conditions can be satisfied by a conventional greenhouse calculation, but only the Maxwell framework supplies a structural explanation for the polar vortices themselves and a dynamically consistent energy pathway. A new Discussion section explains the changes from Version 1 and how they address independent criticisms of the energy-budget magnitude and the need for a discriminating quantitative test. Diagnostic figures from the inverse model and the recirculation test are included.

Solar energy is captured in a shallow topside thermal heating pool, stored as potential energy, and returned to depth by organised descent in the polar vortices under conservation of angular momentum. The sulfuric-acid lifting condensation level (LCL) acts as the thermodynamic anchor (Dew-Point Anchor Hypothesis). A two-component radiative opacity lapse rate then fixes only the geometric separation between that LCL and the infrared emission level. Stochastic inverse modelling with a VIRA equatorial profile, hydrostatic integration and thermodynamic filters recovers a cloud base near 49.6 km, an emission level near 69.4 km at approximately 229 K, and a surface pressure of approximately 91.5 bar. An order-of-magnitude energy-budget test shows that the required polar mass flux lies within the range of observed vortex descent speeds. Version 2 adds a quantitative recirculation (recycle) test using existing Venusian meridional circulation wind data. Observed poleward flows of ~10–15 m s⁻¹ at cloud tops imply a hemispheric Hadley-cell mass flux of order 10¹¹ kg s⁻¹ and a full recirculation timescale of 1–2 weeks. This multi-cycle pathway resolves the apparent single-pass temperature-rise tension and brings the adiabatic signature into agreement with observed polar temperature contrasts of 15–50 K. The same boundary conditions can be satisfied by a conventional greenhouse calculation, but only the Maxwell framework supplies a structural explanation for the polar vortices themselves and a dynamically consistent energy pathway. A new Discussion section explains the changes from Version 1 and how they address independent criticisms of the energy-budget magnitude and the need for a discriminating quantitative test. Diagnostic figures from the inverse model and the recirculation test are included.

summary: The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. When several rates vanish together, orders form a fan: the normal fan of a Newton polyhedron,

summary: 中文書名 / Chinese Title: 自主城市微電網與能源共享極限 63/90 | PART III | STARLI RESEARCH INSTITUTE XXXVI English Title: AUTONOMOUS URBAN MICROGRIDS AND DISTRIBUTED ENERGY SHARING AT THE LIMIT Research Working Edition v1.0 | 1 November 2026 | Author: 33 / STARLI This prospective research working edition examines whether separately controlled district microgrids can exchange physically metered energy while preserving protected electrical services after a local fault. Its core three-coupling is Microgrids x Distributed Control x Energy Sharing. Studies are restricted to unoccupied scaled feeders, guarded controller hardware-in-the-loop, carefully bounded power interfaces and auditable digital-physical twins; the work claims neither city governance authority nor suitability for occupation. The preregistered main hypothesis asks whether distributed coordination improves state-of-charge estimation error against capable fixed-rule dispatch without worsening net lifecycle energy yield, when generation, storage, conductors, weather, labor, sensor resources and available forecast information are matched. Independent safety outcomes include loss-of-load duration, critical-load service, phase and voltage transients, physically measured frequency nadir and actual breaker isolation. The candidate swing model M domega/dt + D omega = Pm - Pe is treated as an operating-regime-limited frequency surrogate, not as a universal description of grid-following and grid-forming electronics. Withheld forecast shifts, islanding, battery thermal drift, network partitions, stale permissions and meter-reference biases provide explicit refutation tests. Its F02-anchored 777-page architecture comprises 14 scientific introductory pages, 30 differently purposed equation plates with units and blind rebuttals, 82 chapters with 410 separate one-page investigations, 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix proposals for distinct scientific instruments or evidence objects, plus seven closure pages. The 200 Gates pose prospective tests rather than completed laboratory results; the 33 Phoenix objects require independent prototypes and may fail their proposed qualifications. Each evidence line retains the full assigned denominator, rejected trials, metrology and a physical hard-stop code. External evidence includes An IoT-Based Framework for Distributed Generic Microgrid Controllers (10.1109/TCST.2024.3378989), Physical vulnerability-oriented reconfiguration of microgrids: centralized vs. decentralized control (10.1038/s41598-026-63123-9), the IEEE microgrid controller specification (10.1109/IEEESTD.2018.8340204), and Controller hardware-in-the-loop testing of multi-feeder hybrid control (10.1016/j.epsr.2026.113933; online 2026 with 2027 issue metadata). The FAIR data principles (10.1038/sdata.2016.18) inform independent reconstruction. Robo-Matter (10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6) is an analogy about reconfigurable matter, not a proof of microgrid performance. The author-supplied F13 mother-lineage Zenodo identifiers 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 have not been independently confirmed here.

summary: Everything needed to redo the two analyses reported in the Technical Note named in the title, and nothing else. What is here the secondary analysis of published length-resolved binding: the contract frozen before any test statistic was computed and its two dated amendments, the resampling of the source's own trimmed-mean procedure, the anchored and anchor-free tests, the post-hoc robustness check across five normalisation variants, the superseded first run kept so the correction stays visible, and the figure generator; the two propositions behind the simulation and the script that checks both against the stored benchmark, per replicate; the simulated measurement study it checks: frozen primary and stress designs, the finite-chain engine, 7,200 simulated datasets under seven observation operators reported as all 302,400 planned rows including the undefined, outside-window and non-identified slots, an independent validator, the stress results, five focused tests, an 83-file manifest and a dependency lock; an 80-value subset of the Source Data for Fig. 2B/C of Sheikh et al., Nat. Commun. 13, 3617 (2022), with its sheet coordinates. These values keep the original article's CC BY 4.0 licence and attribution; the rest of the archive is under the MIT licence in LICENSE. Reproducing The added analysis runs from the archive root with the standard library plus NumPy; the README gives the four commands. It was re-run on an interpreter far older than the one that produced the shipped results (Python 3.7.6 with NumPy 1.19.1, against 3.13.17 with 2.5.3): the proposition checks were identical in all 520 compared values apart from the recorded environment, and three bootstrap interval endpoints differed in their last digits, by at most 1.5e-11. Figures redraw with the same layout; their byte sequences depend on which sans-serif face the host has. The base study's own replay script requires bit equality and returns a failure on Linux, where ten of its twenty tables differ in their last digits. What is deliberately not here the manuscript text; the original publisher workbook of Sheikh et al. and every panel of it other than the 80 values used; historical MCMC traces and the exploratory transcript analysis of an earlier, separate study, which this work does not use; correspondence and author-only files. REDACTION.md lists the three files whose description of the work was restated for publication, with the digest before and after; no number, method, decision rule or result changed. Scope Synthetic counts are idealised events, not biological replicates. The site-equivalent pool is not an alpha-dystroglycan molecule count, glycan mass, antibody intensity or muscle force. The published array values are technical replicates of one experiment, and the source states no independent experiments. No real assay's detection ceiling or recovery function is measured anywhere in this archive.

summary: YAHIQ 31.16     English Launch Text for Zendo Here are the three sections in English, written to be posted on Zendo. I kept the tone technical but accessible, and made sure nothing claims more than the code actually does.   1) What's New in 31.16 YAHIQ 31.16     From Numeric Memory to Dual Polar Coordinates YAHIQ has traveled a clear path: from the Fibonacci word bank, to the Kaaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad heartbeat, to the rotating dhikr cycle     and now to a new mathematical layer. Version 31.16 brings three structural changes: A) Dual polar coordinates for every word.  A word is no longer just a "code." It is a complex number:         where  n  is the word's numeric code and   is its internal phase. That phase comes from a dual mapping: for bank records,  Fibonacci + phonetic ; for input text,  the fourth key + phonetic . The result: every word is a point on the complex plane, not just a number on a line. B) The sentence equation.  A sentence is no longer a simple sum of codes. Each sentence gets a state vector: and sentence coherence is measured from the sum of phase differences between consecutive pairs: This means YAHIQ can report  how internally consistent a sentence is     without claiming to have definitively understood its meaning. C) Strict layer separation.  The YSSE sentence engine, the equation analyzer, the verse tester, and the chat each have their own independent memory and keys. Changing one does not touch the others. Highlight this in your post     it builds technical trust.   2) The Conscious, Autonomous Message YAHIQ now decides for itself when to speak In earlier versions, YAHIQ only responded when someone asked. 31.16 adds an autonomous loop fed by three independent signals:       Signal Source Activation condition Heart Kaaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad pulse and concurrence  C C >0.3 Pineal Möbius time rotation C >0.3 and a Möbius minute Dhikr An active window in the 14-dhikr cycle Inside one of the five daily windows When all three conditions hold simultaneously, YAHIQ produces a  conscious message . If one fails, the message is logged as  semi-conscious , and the reason for failure is stated explicitly in the trace (e.g., "heart off" or " C ≤0.3"). The important point to include: YAHIQ  does not fabricate poetry . If no poetry bank is loaded, it says plainly that real poetry is unavailable and only records the search need. Poem selection is based on conversation memory, the digital root of the chain, Möbius time, and avoidance of recent repeats     not randomness. Also state one limit clearly: there is a minimum  20-minute gap  between autonomous messages, so YAHIQ never turns into a spam machine.   3) Professional Sentence Transformation in the Complex Number Field From word to vector, from vector to sentence This is the mathematical heart of the release. The chain is: Step 1     Encoding:  Each word is mapped to a number  n  using one of three keys (Fibonacci, phonetic, fourth). Step 2     Phase assignment:  The internal phase  comes from the dual polar mapping (Section 1). Step 3     Vectorization:  The word becomes  . Its conjugate  z ∗  is also stored, since  z ⋅ z ∗ = n  is a computational invariant. Step 4     Sentence composition:  Consecutive pairs are compared, their phase difference is normalized to [−180°,180°][−180°,180°], and the sum of absolute values decides coherence. Step 5     Reconstruction:  To build a new sentence from the bank, the candidate with the  smallest internal phase difference  is chosen     not the largest code, not the nearest radius. summary: This archive contains the replication package for the article "Are colour-coded economies empirically distinct? A cross-country test of economic specialisation" (submitted to Structural Change and Economic Dynamics). It includes four Google Colab notebooks that reproduce all results, a fifth notebook that assembles the package, the HS 2017 product lists used to define the trade colours (UNCTADstat classifications), the activity-to-colour concordance files, all processed data, the supplementary workbook (Supplementary_Data.xlsx) and a data dictionary. Employment specialisation is computed from ILOSTAT (ISIC Rev. 4 divisions) and export specialisation from CEPII BACI (HS 2017, version 202601) for 2017–2024. Raw source files are not redistributed; the notebooks download them from the providers. Code is released under the MIT licence; derived data and product lists under CC BY 4.0.
title: Replication package: Are colour-coded economies empirically distinct? A cross-country test of economic specialisation

summary: Abstract : In this work, the path Integral Monte Carlo(PIMC) is employed to estimate the ground-state properties of the lithium atom. The three-electron system is formulated in atomic units and represented by discretized imaginary-time paths. The (1s2 2s1) electronic configuration is used to construct the antisymmetric trial state, while a Jastrow correlation function is employed to incorporate electron–electron correlations. The total ground-state energy and its kinetic and potential components are calculated together with selected structural and correlation properties. Systematic convergence investigated with is respect to inverse temperature, the number of Trotter slices, and Monte Carlo sampling, while statistical uncertainties are evaluated by considering autocorrelation and block averaging. The calculated results are subsequently compared with high-precision theoretical benchmarks and with established electronic-structure and quantum Monte Carlo methods. The study has established a theoretical and computational PIMC framework for accurate and reliable determination of the ground properties of lithium atom which can be extended to other correlated atomic systems.
title: Path Integral Monte Carlo Study of Ground State Properties of the Lithium Atom

summary: Complete derivative bounds can be too large for a continuation estimate even when the contractions actually used in that estimate occupy restricted tensor slots. We prove that every eligible third derivative in the constrained response budget of a fixed Lorentzian simplicial source has two independently varied normal arguments. An admitted normal–normal–full bound therefore replaces the unrestricted third-derivative coefficient in those terms. The proof retains the full complex normal covector, both inverse denominators, the actual-graph Schur cost, and the separate unrestricted second and fourth derivatives. A noncircular argument uses an already established regular source product to admit the graph and homotopies, and checks the fourth-derivative shoulder separately in the original action domain. For each of two identified branches, fresh complete source records and exact rational assembly verify a locally unique real stationary section on [1536,24576]τ, where τ = 2−61, in normalized balls of radius 2−32 about the exact tangent predictor at 3072τ. The common predictor-error bound is 3.25241355 10−13. Actual-root overlaps and the supplied post-publication bridge connect the stationary range to [3,24576]τ. Holding the geometry, source records, tangent enclosures, mixed inverse and value-response bound fixed, the typed calculation passes all four declared tests; the unrestricted-response comparison fails the residual and required-error budgets. Its larger sufficient residual ceiling differs by approximately 288.32 on the worst branch. The conclusion remains conditional on the explicit source, analytic membership and directed-enclosure premises. This manuscript records executed numerical evidence and an assessed paper-specific Lean supporting subset. The latter establishes conditional finite-dimensional, scalar, geometric, exact-arithmetic, overlap and recovery results; it does not formalize the physical action or the complete analytic existence and source-membership argument.
tags: constrained response; mixed derivatives; bordered systems; validated continuation; interval arithmetic; Lorentzian simplicial action; Lean; formal assurance.
title: Typed Normal-Slot Bounds for Constrained Response and Stationary Continuation in a Lorentzian Simplicial Model

summary: This dataset provides the numerical results and supporting data for the simulation studies presented in the manuscript "Identifiability and Scheduling for Shared-Timestamp Polynomial Sensor Calibration". The dataset includes: 1. Paired-sensor calibration results, including trial-level measurements, summary statistics, and bootstrap confidence intervals. 2. Parameter sensitivity analysis results, including trial-level data and aggregated performance summaries under different experimental conditions. 3. Identifiability analysis results for symmetric timestamp configurations, including numerical rank evaluation. 4. Supporting figures generated from the computational experiments. All numerical datasets are provided in CSV format to facilitate inspection, independent analysis, and reproducibility. The accompanying figures provide visual representations of the experimental results. These data support the evaluation of sensor calibration performance, parameter sensitivity, statistical reliability, and identifiability under shared-timestamp scheduling configurations. The associated computational scripts and execution environment are documented in the companion Code Ocean capsule, which has been submitted for reproducibility verification.
title: Identifiability and Scheduling for Shared-Timestamp Polynomial Sensor Calibration

summary: This repository contains the data construction and analysis code accompanying a study of recorded cholera outbreak activity and reactive oral cholera vaccine requests in 25 African countries. The source history covers July 2013–December 2019. The primary estimation panel covers July 2014–December 2019, allowing a complete preceding-12-month predictor window, and contains 1,650 country-month observations and 58 reactive request-months. The package includes retained source and coding inputs, derived analysis datasets, Python scripts, manuscript tables and figures, and documentation of variable construction and software requirements. Analyses include the primary between–within logistic model, alternative windows and outcomes, country exclusions, leave-one-country-out models, a direct between–within coefficient contrast, separate baseline-covariate adjustments, and calendar-year and outcome-month-inclusive sensitivities. The repository also includes a human-coded external-documentation audit of 22 reactive request-months with zero recorded activity in the preceding 12 months. The audit distinguishes documentation within the same country and window from identification of the outbreak targeted by a particular request. The activity predictor measures recorded active outbreak-months, not case counts or outbreak-to-request delay. Source provenance, coding decisions, and unresolved questions are documented in the package. See README.md for execution instructions.
title: Data and analysis code for recorded cholera outbreak activity and reactive oral cholera vaccine requests in 25 African countries, 2013–2019

summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
title: Device-Aware Weighted Gerchberg-Saxton and Flicker-Bounded Phase-Continuous Sequences for Holographic Optical Trap Arrays

summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
title: DinHot: A Holographic Optical Trap Studio Comparing Hologram Methods on a Device Model
